Additional analysis shows that the contrastive objective and meta-actions are complementary in achieving the best results, and the resulting agent better aligns its states with corresponding instructions, making it more suitable for real-world embodied agents. The code is available at: https://github.com/joeyy5588/LACMA.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces LACMA, a method that improves embodied instruction following in unseen environments by aligning agent states with language instructions via contrastive learning and introducing meta-actions—higher-level action patterns parsed from action sequences—to bridge the semantic gap between language and low-level actions. The approach achieves a 4.5% absolute gain in success rate on the ALFRED benchmark compared to a strong baseline, demonstrating better generalization and state-instruction alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出LACMA方法，通过对比学习对齐智能体状态与语言指令，并引入元动作（从动作序列中解析出的高层动作模式）来弥合语言与低层动作之间的语义鸿沟，从而提升在未见环境中的具身指令跟随能力。在ALFRED基准上，该方法相比强基线取得了4.5%的绝对成功率提升，展现出更好的泛化能力和状态-指令对齐效果。

papers.title: UReader: Universal OCR-free Visually-situated Language Understanding with Multimodal Large Language Model
papers.short_title: UReader: OCR-free Visual Language Understanding
papers.abstract: Text is ubiquitous in our visual world, conveying crucial information, such as in documents, websites, and everyday photographs. In this work, we propose UReader, a first exploration of universal OCR-free visually-situated language understanding based on the Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM). By leveraging the shallow text recognition ability of the MLLM, we only finetuned 1.2% parameters and the training cost is much lower than previous work following domain-specific pretraining and finetuning paradigms. Concretely, UReader is jointly finetuned on a wide range of Visually-situated Language Understanding tasks via a unified instruction format. To enhance the visual text and semantic understanding, we further apply two auxiliary tasks with the same format, namely text reading and key points generation tasks. We design a shape-adaptive cropping module before the encoder-decoder architecture of MLLM to leverage the frozen low-resolution vision encoder for processing high-resolution images. Without downstream finetuning, our single model achieves state-of-the-art ocr-free performance in 8 out of 10 visually-situated language understanding tasks, across 5 domains: documents, tables, charts, natural images, and webpage screenshots. Codes and instruction-tuning datasets will be released.
papers.summary_en: UReader is a universal OCR-free model for visually-situated language understanding, built on a multimodal large language model. It achieves strong performance by fine-tuning only 1.2% of parameters on diverse tasks using a unified instruction format, with auxiliary tasks for text reading and key point generation. A shape-adaptive cropping module enables processing of high-resolution images with a frozen low-resolution vision encoder. The single model achieves state-of-the-art results on 8 out of 10 tasks across documents, tables, charts, natural images, and webpages.
papers.summary_zh: UReader是一种基于多模态大语言模型的通用无OCR视觉情境语言理解模型。通过仅微调1.2%的参数，并在统一指令格式下联合训练多种任务，辅以文本阅读和关键点生成任务，模型性能显著提升。其形状自适应裁剪模块使得冻结的低分辨率视觉编码器能够处理高分辨率图像。该单一模型在文档、表格、图表、自然图像和网页截图等5个领域的10项任务中，有8项达到了无OCR方法的最优性能。

papers.title: AppBench: Planning of Multiple APIs from Various APPs for Complex User Instruction
papers.short_title: AppBench: Multi-API Planning
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can interact with the real world by connecting with versatile external APIs, resulting in better problem-solving and task automation capabilities. Previous research primarily either focuses on APIs with limited arguments from a single source or overlooks the complex dependency relationship between different APIs. However, it is essential to utilize multiple APIs collaboratively from various sources, especially for complex user instructions. In this paper, we introduce MetaBench, the first benchmark to evaluate LLMs’ ability to plan and execute multiple APIs from various sources in order to complete the user’s task. Specifically, we consider two significant challenges in multiple APIs: 1) graph structures: some APIs can be executed independently while others need to be executed one by one, resulting in graph-like execution order; and 2) permission constraints: which source is authorized to execute the API call. We have experimental results on 9 distinct LLMs; e.g., GPT-4o achieves only a 2.0% success rate at the most complex instruction, revealing that the existing state-of-the-art LLMs still cannot perform well in this situation even with the help of in-context learning and finetuning. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/ruleGreen/AppBench.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces AppBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to plan and execute multiple APIs from various apps to handle complex user instructions. It focuses on two key challenges: graph-structured execution dependencies among APIs and permission constraints across different sources. Experiments on 9 LLMs show that even GPT-4o achieves only a 2% success rate on the most complex tasks, highlighting significant limitations in current models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了AppBench，一个评估大语言模型（LLMs）规划并执行来自多个应用的API以处理复杂用户指令能力的基准。它重点关注两个关键挑战：API之间的图结构执行依赖关系以及不同来源的权限约束。在9个LLM上的实验表明，即使GPT-4o在最复杂任务上的成功率也仅为2%，揭示了当前模型的显著局限性。

papers.title: SUPER: Evaluating Agents on Setting Up and Executing Tasks from Research Repositories
papers.short_title: SUPER: Setup & Execute Research Tasks
papers.abstract: Given that Large Language Models (LLMs) have made significant progress in writing code, can they now be used to autonomously reproduce results from research repositories? Such a capability would be a boon to the research community, helping researchers validate, understand, and extend prior work. To advance towards this goal, we introduce SUPER, the first benchmark designed to evaluate the capability of LLMs in setting up and executing tasks from research repositories. SUPER aims to capture the realistic challenges faced by researchers working with Machine Learning (ML) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) research repositories. Our benchmark comprises three distinct problem sets: 45 end-to-end problems with annotated expert solutions, 152 sub-problems derived from the expert set that focus on specific challenges (e.g., configuring a trainer), and 602 automatically generated problems for larger-scale development. We introduce various evaluation measures to assess both task success and progress, utilizing gold solutions when available or approximations otherwise. We show that state-of-the-art approaches struggle to solve these problems with the best model (GPT-4o) solving only 16.3% of the end-to-end set, and 46.1% of the scenarios. This illustrates the challenge of this task, and suggests that SUPER can serve as a valuable resource for the community to make and measure progress.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces SUPER, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to autonomously set up and execute tasks from ML/NLP research repositories. It includes 45 end-to-end problems, 152 sub-problems, and 602 auto-generated problems, with evaluation measures for task success. State-of-the-art models like GPT-4o solve only 16.3% of end-to-end tasks, highlighting the challenge and the benchmark's value for progress measurement.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文提出了SUPER基准，用于评估大语言模型自主设置并执行机器学习/自然语言处理研究仓库任务的能力。基准包含45个端到端问题、152个子问题和602个自动生成问题，并设计了任务成功与进展的评估指标。当前最优模型GPT-4o仅能解决16.3%的端到端任务，凸显了该任务的挑战性及SUPER作为进展衡量工具的价值。

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation for Situated Action Generation: A Case Study on Minecraft
papers.short_title: RAG Code Gen for Minecraft Actions
papers.abstract: In the Minecraft Collaborative Building Task, two players collaborate: an Architect (A) provides instructions to a Builder (B) to assemble a specified structure using 3D blocks. In this work, we investigate the use of large language models (LLMs) to predict the sequence of actions taken by the Builder. Leveraging LLMs' in-context learning abilities, we use few-shot prompting techniques, that significantly improve performance over baseline methods. Additionally, we present a detailed analysis of the gaps in performance for future work
papers.summary_en: This paper explores using large language models with retrieval-augmented generation to predict builder actions in Minecraft collaborative building tasks. By applying few-shot prompting, the authors significantly improve action prediction accuracy over baseline methods. They also analyze performance gaps to guide future research.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探索使用大型语言模型结合检索增强生成来预测Minecraft协作建筑任务中的建造者动作。通过应用少样本提示，作者显著提高了动作预测的准确性，超越了基线方法。他们还分析了性能差距，为未来研究提供指导。

papers.title: Nebula: A discourse aware Minecraft Builder
papers.short_title: Nebula: A discourse aware Minecraft Builder
papers.abstract: When engaging in collaborative tasks, humans efficiently exploit the semantic structure of a conversation to optimize verbal and nonverbal interactions. But in recent"language to code"or"language to action"models, this information is lacking. We show how incorporating the prior discourse and nonlinguistic context of a conversation situated in a nonlinguistic environment can improve the"language to action"component of such interactions. We finetune an LLM to predict actions based on prior context; our model, Nebula, doubles the net-action F1 score over the baseline on this task of Jayannavar et al.(2020). We also investigate our model's ability to construct shapes and understand location descriptions using a synthetic dataset
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces Nebula, a discourse-aware model that improves language-to-action generation in collaborative tasks by incorporating prior conversation and environmental context. Fine-tuned on an LLM, Nebula doubles the net-action F1 score over the baseline on a Minecraft building task. The model also shows enhanced ability to construct shapes and interpret location descriptions using synthetic data.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了Nebula，一种具有话语感知能力的模型，通过融入先前的对话和环境上下文，改进了协作任务中的语言到动作生成。该模型基于LLM微调，在Minecraft建造任务中，净动作F1分数相比基线提升了一倍。此外，Nebula在使用合成数据构建形状和理解位置描述方面也表现出更强的能力。

papers.title: AUTOGEN STUDIO: A No-Code Developer Tool for Building and Debugging Multi-Agent Systems
papers.short_title: AutoGen Studio: No-Code Multi-Agent Tool
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems, where multiple agents (generative AI models + tools) collaborate, are emerging as an effective pattern for solving long-running, complex tasks in numerous do- mains. However, specifying their parameters (such as models, tools, and orchestration mechanisms etc,.) and debugging them remains challenging for most developers. To address this challenge, we present AUTOGEN STUDIO, a no-code developer tool for rapidly prototyping, debugging, and evaluating multi-agent work- flows built upon the AUTOGEN framework. AUTOGEN STUDIO offers a web interface and a Python API for representing LLM-enabled agents using a declarative (JSON-based) specification. It provides an intuitive drag-and-drop UI for agent workflow specification, interactive evaluation and debugging of workflows, and a gallery of reusable agent components. We highlight four design principles for no-code multi-agent developer tools and contribute an open-source implementation. https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/autogenstudio/samples/apps/autogen-studio
papers.summary_en: AUTOGEN STUDIO is a no-code developer tool that enables rapid prototyping, debugging, and evaluation of multi-agent systems built on the AUTOGEN framework. It provides a drag-and-drop web interface and a JSON-based declarative specification for defining agents, tools, and workflows. The tool includes interactive debugging, evaluation capabilities, and a gallery of reusable components, following four design principles for no-code multi-agent development. The implementation is open-source and available on GitHub.
papers.summary_zh: AUTOGEN STUDIO 是一个无代码开发工具，支持基于 AUTOGEN 框架的多智能体系统的快速原型设计、调试和评估。它提供拖拽式网页界面和基于 JSON 的声明式规范，用于定义智能体、工具和工作流。该工具包含交互式调试、评估功能以及可复用组件库，遵循无代码多智能体开发的四项设计原则。其实现为开源，可在 GitHub 上获取。

papers.title: Read Anywhere Pointed: Layout-aware GUI Screen Reading with Tree-of-Lens Grounding
papers.short_title: Screen Point-and-Read with Tree-of-Lens
papers.abstract: Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) are central to our interaction with digital devices and growing efforts have been made to build models for various GUI understanding tasks. However, these efforts largely overlook an important GUI-referring task: screen reading based on user-indicated points, which we name the Screen Point-and-Read (ScreenPR) task. Currently, this task is predominantly handled by rigid accessible screen reading tools, in great need of new models driven by advancements in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). In this paper, we propose a Tree-of-Lens (ToL) agent, utilizing a novel ToL grounding mechanism, to address the ScreenPR task. Based on the input point coordinate and the corresponding GUI screenshot, our ToL agent constructs a Hierarchical Layout Tree. Based on the tree, our ToL agent not only comprehends the content of the indicated area but also articulates the layout and spatial relationships between elements. Such layout information is crucial for accurately interpreting information on the screen, distinguishing our ToL agent from other screen reading tools. We also thoroughly evaluate the ToL agent against other baselines on a newly proposed ScreenPR benchmark, which includes GUIs from mobile, web, and operating systems. Last but not least, we test the ToL agent on mobile GUI navigation tasks, demonstrating its utility in identifying incorrect actions along the path of agent execution trajectories. Code and data: https://screen-point-and-read.github.io.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces the Screen Point-and-Read (ScreenPR) task, where a model reads GUI content at a user-specified point. The authors propose a Tree-of-Lens (ToL) agent that builds a hierarchical layout tree from the screenshot and point coordinate, enabling it to understand both the content and spatial relationships in the indicated area. The ToL agent outperforms baselines on a new benchmark spanning mobile, web, and OS GUIs, and also helps identify errors in mobile navigation trajectories.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了屏幕点读（ScreenPR）任务，要求模型根据用户指定的点读取GUI内容。作者设计了树透镜（ToL）智能体，通过从截图和点坐标构建层次化布局树，既能理解指示区域的内容，也能描述元素间的空间关系。ToL智能体在涵盖移动端、网页和操作系统的全新基准上优于基线方法，并能用于识别移动导航轨迹中的错误操作。

papers.title: MSI-Agent: Incorporating Multi-Scale Insight into Embodied Agents for Superior Planning and Decision-Making
papers.short_title: MSI-Agent: Multi-Scale Insight Embodied
papers.abstract: Insight gradually becomes a crucial form of long-term memory for an agent. However, the emergence of irrelevant insight and the lack of general insight can greatly undermine the effectiveness of insight. To solve this problem, in this paper, we introduce **M**ulti-**S**cale **I**nsight Agent (MSI-Agent), an embodied agent designed to improve LLMs’ planning and decision-making ability by summarizing and utilizing insight effectively across different scales. MSI achieves this through the experience selector, insight generator, and insight selector. Leveraging a three-part pipeline, MSI can generate task-specific and high-level insight, store it in a database, and then use relevant insight from it to aid in decision-making. Our experiments show that MSI outperforms another insight strategy when planning by GPT3.5. Moreover, We delve into the strategies for selecting seed experience and insight, aiming to provide LLM with more useful and relevant insight for better decision-making. Our observations also indicate that MSI exhibits better robustness when facing domain-shifting scenarios.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces MSI-Agent, an embodied agent that enhances LLM planning and decision-making by generating and utilizing multi-scale insights—both task-specific and high-level—through a three-part pipeline of experience selection, insight generation, and insight selection. It addresses the issues of irrelevant or lacking insight by storing relevant insights in a database for retrieval. Experiments show MSI outperforms other insight strategies with GPT-3.5, and it demonstrates robustness in domain-shifting scenarios.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出MSI-Agent，一种通过多尺度洞察（包括任务特定和高层次洞察）来增强LLM规划与决策能力的具身智能体。它通过经验选择器、洞察生成器和洞察选择器三部分流程，将相关洞察存入数据库以供检索，解决了洞察不相关或缺乏的问题。实验表明，在GPT-3.5上MSI优于其他洞察策略，并在领域迁移场景中展现出更好的鲁棒性。

papers.title: AutoScraper: A Progressive Understanding Web Agent for Web Scraper Generation
papers.short_title: AutoScraper: Web Scraper Generation Agent
papers.abstract: Web scraping is a powerful technique that extracts data from websites, enabling automated data collection, enhancing data analysis capabilities, and minimizing manual data entry efforts. Existing methods, wrappers-based methods suffer from limited adaptability and scalability when faced with a new website, while language agents, empowered by large language models (LLMs), exhibit poor reusability in diverse web environments. In this work, we introduce the paradigm of generating web scrapers with LLMs and propose AutoScraper, a two-stage framework that can handle diverse and changing web environments more efficiently. AutoScraper leverages the hierarchical structure of HTML and similarity across different web pages for generating web scrapers. Besides, we propose a new executability metric for better measuring the performance of web scraper generation tasks. We conduct comprehensive experiments with multiple LLMs and demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework. Our work is now open-source.
papers.summary_en: AutoScraper is a two-stage framework that uses large language models to generate web scrapers by leveraging HTML hierarchy and cross-page similarity, improving adaptability and reusability over traditional wrappers and language agents. It also introduces a new executability metric for better evaluation. Experiments show its effectiveness across multiple LLMs.
papers.summary_zh: AutoScraper是一个两阶段框架，利用大语言模型通过HTML层级结构和跨页面相似性生成网络爬虫，相比传统包装器方法和语言代理，提升了适应性和可复用性。它还提出了一种新的可执行性指标用于更好评估。实验表明其在多种大语言模型上的有效性。

papers.title: Knowledge Navigator: LLM-guided Browsing Framework for Exploratory Search in Scientific Literature
papers.short_title: Knowledge Navigator: LLM Browsing for Sci Literature
papers.abstract: The exponential growth of scientific literature necessitates advanced tools for effective knowledge exploration. We present Knowledge Navigator, a system designed to enhance exploratory search abilities by organizing and structuring the retrieved documents from broad topical queries into a navigable, two-level hierarchy of named and descriptive scientific topics and subtopics. This structured organization provides an overall view of the research themes in a domain, while also enabling iterative search and deeper knowledge discovery within specific subtopics by allowing users to refine their focus and retrieve additional relevant documents. Knowledge Navigator combines LLM capabilities with cluster-based methods to enable an effective browsing method. We demonstrate our approach's effectiveness through automatic and manual evaluations on two novel benchmarks, CLUSTREC-COVID and SCITOC. Our code, prompts, and benchmarks are made publicly available.
papers.summary_en: Knowledge Navigator is a system that helps researchers explore scientific literature by organizing search results into a two-level hierarchy of topics and subtopics, using LLMs and clustering. It provides an overview of research themes and allows users to drill down into specific subtopics for deeper discovery. The system is evaluated on two new benchmarks, showing its effectiveness for exploratory search.
papers.summary_zh: Knowledge Navigator 是一个帮助研究者探索科学文献的系统，它利用大语言模型和聚类方法，将搜索结果组织成两级主题和子主题的层次结构。该系统提供了研究主题的概览，并允许用户深入特定子主题进行更深入的发现。通过在两个新基准上的评估，证明了其在探索性搜索中的有效性。

papers.title: Auto-Intent: Automated Intent Discovery and Self-Exploration for Large Language Model Web Agents
papers.short_title: Auto-Intent: Intent Discovery for LLM Web Agents
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Auto-Intent, a method to adapt a pre-trained large language model (LLM) as an agent for a target domain without direct fine-tuning, where we empirically focus on web navigation tasks. Our approach first discovers the underlying intents from target domain demonstrations unsupervisedly, in a highly compact form (up to three words). With the extracted intents, we train our intent predictor to predict the next intent given the agent's past observations and actions. In particular, we propose a self-exploration approach where top-k probable intent predictions are provided as a hint to the pre-trained LLM agent, which leads to enhanced decision-making capabilities. Auto-Intent substantially improves the performance of GPT-{3.5, 4} and Llama-3.1-{70B, 405B} agents on the large-scale real-website navigation benchmarks from Mind2Web and online navigation tasks from WebArena with its cross-benchmark generalization from Mind2Web.
papers.summary_en: Auto-Intent adapts LLMs for web navigation without fine-tuning by first discovering compact intents (up to three words) from target domain demonstrations, then training an intent predictor to suggest likely next intents as hints to the LLM agent. This self-exploration approach significantly boosts performance of GPT-3.5/4 and Llama-3.1 models on Mind2Web and WebArena benchmarks, including cross-benchmark generalization.
papers.summary_zh: Auto-Intent无需微调即可将大语言模型适配为网络导航代理，首先从目标领域演示中无监督地发现高度紧凑的意图（最多三个词），然后训练意图预测器将最可能的下一步意图作为提示提供给LLM代理。这种自我探索方法显著提升了GPT-3.5/4和Llama-3.1模型在Mind2Web和WebArena基准上的性能，并实现了跨基准泛化。

papers.title: TPTU-v2: Boosting Task Planning and Tool Usage of Large Language Model-based Agents in Real-world Industry Systems
papers.short_title: TPTU-v2: Task Planning & Tool Usage in Industry
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated proficiency in addressing tasks that necessitate a combination of task planning and the usage of external tools, such as weather and calculator APIs. However, real-world industrial systems present prevalent challenges in task planning and tool usage: numerous APIs in the real system make it intricate to invoke the appropriate one, while the inherent limitations of LLMs pose challenges in orchestrating an accurate sub-task sequence and API-calling order. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework aimed at enhancing the Task Planning and Tool Usage (TPTU) abilities of LLM-based agents in industry. Our framework comprises three key components designed to address these challenges: (1) the API Retriever selects the most pertinent APIs among the extensive API set; (2) the Demo Selector retrieves task-level demonstrations, which is further used for in-context learning to aid LLMs in accurately decomposing subtasks and effectively invoking hard-to-distinguish APIs; (3) LLM Finetuner tunes a base LLM to enhance its capability for task planning and API calling. We validate our methods using a real-world industry system and an open-sourced academic dataset, demonstrating the efficacy of each individual component as well as the integrated framework. The code is available at here.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces TPTU-v2, a framework to improve task planning and tool usage in LLM-based agents for real-world industrial systems. It addresses challenges like selecting the correct API from many options and decomposing tasks accurately by combining an API retriever, a demo selector for in-context learning, and LLM fine-tuning. Experiments on a real industrial system and an academic dataset show the effectiveness of each component and the overall framework.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出TPTU-v2框架，旨在提升基于大语言模型的智能体在真实工业系统中的任务规划与工具使用能力。该框架通过API检索器、示例选择器（用于上下文学习）以及大语言模型微调三个组件，解决了从大量API中准确选择、任务分解及API调用顺序编排等挑战。在真实工业系统和开源学术数据集上的实验验证了各组件及整体框架的有效性。

papers.title: An Evaluation Mechanism of LLM-based Agents on Manipulating APIs
papers.short_title: Evaluation: LLM Agents Manipulating APIs
papers.summary_en: This paper proposes an evaluation mechanism for LLM-based agents that manipulate APIs, focusing on measuring their ability to correctly understand API documentation, generate appropriate calls, and handle errors. The mechanism includes a set of metrics and a benchmark dataset covering diverse API tasks. Experiments show that current LLMs still struggle with complex API interactions, highlighting areas for improvement.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种针对基于大语言模型的API操作智能体的评估机制，重点衡量其正确理解API文档、生成合适调用以及处理错误的能力。该机制包含一套指标和一个覆盖多种API任务的基准数据集。实验表明，当前大语言模型在处理复杂API交互时仍存在困难，揭示了需要改进的方向。

papers.title: VGA: Vision GUI Assistant - Minimizing Hallucinations through Image-Centric Fine-Tuning
papers.short_title: VGA: Vision GUI Assistant
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have significantly improve performance in image comprehension tasks, such as formatted charts and rich-content images. Yet, Graphical User Interface (GUI) pose a greater challenge due to their structured format and detailed textual information. Existing LVLMs often overly depend on internal knowledge and neglect image content, resulting in hallucinations and incorrect responses in GUI comprehension. To address these issues, we introduce VGA, a fine-tuned model designed for comprehensive GUI understanding. Our model aims to enhance the interpretation of visual data of GUI and reduce hallucinations. We first construct a Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset of 63.8k high-quality examples with our propose Referent Method, which ensures the model's responses are highly depend on visual content within the image. We then design a two-stage fine-tuning method called Foundation and Advanced Comprehension (FAC) to enhance both the model's ability to extract information from image content and alignment with human intent. Experiments show that our approach enhances the model's ability to extract information from images and achieves state-of-the-art results in GUI understanding tasks. Our dataset and fine-tuning script will be released soon.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces VGA, a fine-tuned Vision-Language Model for GUI understanding that reduces hallucinations by focusing on image content. It constructs a 63.8k VQA dataset using a Referent Method to ensure answers depend on visual data, and proposes a two-stage fine-tuning approach (FAC) to improve information extraction and alignment with human intent. Experiments show state-of-the-art results on GUI tasks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出VGA，一种针对GUI理解微调的视觉语言模型，通过聚焦图像内容减少幻觉。它使用引用方法构建了63.8k的VQA数据集，确保答案依赖视觉数据，并设计了两阶段微调方法（FAC）以提升信息提取能力和与人类意图的对齐。实验表明，该方法在GUI任务上达到了最先进的结果。

papers.title: Free your mouse! Command Large Language Models to Generate Code to Format Word Documents
papers.short_title: LLM Code for Word Formatting
papers.abstract: Recently, LLMs have significantly improved code generation, making it increasingly accessible to users. As a result, LLM-powered code generation applications have sprung up, vastly boosting user productivity. This paper mainly explores how to improve the efficiency and experience of users in formatting the document. Specifically, we propose an automatic document formatting method, Text-to-Format, which is driven by various prompting strategies. Text-to-Format takes the user’s formatting instructions and then generates code that can be run in Microsoft Word to format the content in a document. Further, to evaluate automatic document formatting approaches and advance the document formatting task, we built an evaluation specification including a high-quality dataset DocFormEval data, a code runtime environment, and evaluation metrics. Extensive experimental results on data reveal that the prompting strategy’s effect positively correlates with how much knowledge it introduces related to document formatting task. We believe the constructed DocFormEval data and the exploration about Text-to-Format can help developers build more intelligent tools for automatic document formatting, especially in offline scenarios, where the data privacy is the top priority.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces Text-to-Format, a method that uses LLMs with prompting strategies to generate VBA code for formatting Word documents based on user instructions. To evaluate such approaches, the authors create DocFormEval, a dataset with a runtime environment and metrics. Experiments show that prompting strategies incorporating more domain knowledge yield better results. The work aims to enable efficient, privacy-preserving document formatting in offline settings.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出Text-to-Format方法，利用大语言模型和提示策略生成VBA代码，根据用户指令自动格式化Word文档。为评估此类方法，作者构建了包含数据集、运行环境和评估指标的DocFormEval基准。实验表明，引入更多领域知识的提示策略效果更优。该工作旨在实现离线场景下高效且保护隐私的文档格式化。

papers.title: BASES: Large-scale Web Search User Simulation with Large Language Model based Agents
papers.short_title: BASES: Web Search User Simulation
papers.abstract: Due to the excellent capacities of large language models (LLMs), it becomes feasible to develop LLM-based agents for reliable user simulation. Considering the scarcity and limit (e.g., privacy issues) of real user data, in this paper, we conduct large-scale user simulation for web search, to improve the analysis and modeling of user search behavior. Specially, we propose BASES, a novel user simulation framework with LLM-based agents, designed to facilitate comprehensive simulations of web search user behaviors. Our simulation framework can generate unique user profiles at scale, which subsequently leads to diverse search behaviors. To demonstrate the effectiveness of BASES, we conduct evaluation experiments based on two human benchmarks in both Chinese and English, demonstrating that BASES can effectively simulate large-scale human-like search behaviors. To further accommodate the research on web search, we develop WARRIORS, a new large-scale dataset encompassing web search user behaviors, including both Chinese and English versions, which can greatly bolster research in the field of information retrieval. Our code and data will be publicly released soon.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces BASES, a framework using large language model-based agents to simulate diverse web search user behaviors at scale, addressing the scarcity and privacy issues of real user data. It generates unique user profiles leading to varied search behaviors, validated against human benchmarks in Chinese and English. Additionally, it presents WARRIORS, a large-scale dataset of web search behaviors in both languages to support information retrieval research.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出BASES框架，利用基于大语言模型的智能体大规模模拟网络搜索用户行为，以解决真实用户数据稀缺和隐私问题。该框架可生成多样化的用户画像，进而产生丰富的搜索行为，并在中英文人类基准上得到验证。同时，本文发布了WARRIORS数据集，包含中英文网络搜索行为数据，以支持信息检索领域的研究。

papers.title: Sequential API Function Calling Using GraphQL Schema
papers.short_title: Sequential API Calling via GraphQL
papers.abstract: Function calling using Large Language Models (LLMs) is an active research area that aims to empower LLMs with the ability to execute APIs to perform real-world tasks. However, sequential function calling using LLMs with interdependence between functions is still under-explored. To this end, we introduce GraphQLRestBench, a dataset consisting of natural language utterances paired with function call sequences representing real-world REST API calls with variable mapping between functions. In order to represent the response structure of the functions in the LLM prompt, we use the GraphQL schema of the REST APIs. We also introduce a custom evaluation framework for our dataset consisting of four specially designed metrics. We evaluate various open-source LLMs on our dataset using few-shot Chain-of-Thought and ReAct prompting to establish a reasonable baseline.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the under-explored problem of sequential function calling with LLMs, where API calls depend on each other. The authors introduce GraphQLRestBench, a dataset of natural language queries paired with interdependent REST API call sequences, using GraphQL schemas to represent response structures. They also propose a custom evaluation framework with four metrics and establish baselines by testing open-source LLMs with few-shot Chain-of-Thought and ReAct prompting.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型（LLM）中尚未充分研究的顺序函数调用问题（即API调用之间存在依赖关系）进行了探索。作者提出了GraphQLRestBench数据集，其中包含自然语言查询及其对应的、具有变量映射的REST API调用序列，并利用GraphQL模式来表示函数的响应结构。此外，他们还设计了一个包含四个专门指标的评估框架，并通过少样本思维链和ReAct提示方法测试了多种开源LLM，建立了合理的基线。

papers.title: E²CL: Exploration-based Error Correction Learning for Embodied Agents
papers.short_title: E²CL: Exploration Error Correction
papers.abstract: Language models are exhibiting increasing capability in knowledge utilization and reasoning. However, when applied as agents in embodied environments, they often suffer from misalignment between their intrinsic knowledge and environmental knowledge, leading to infeasible actions. Traditional environment alignment methods, such as supervised learning on expert trajectories and reinforcement learning, encounter limitations in covering environmental knowledge and achieving efficient convergence, respectively. Inspired by human learning, we propose Exploration-based Error Correction Learning (E2CL), a novel framework that leverages exploration-induced errors and environmental feedback to enhance environment alignment for embodied agents. E2CL incorporates teacher-guided and teacher-free explorations to gather environmental feedback and correct erroneous actions. The agent learns to provide feedback and self-correct, thereby enhancing its adaptability to target environments. Extensive experiments in the VirtualHome environment demonstrate that E2CL-trained agents outperform those trained by baseline methods and exhibit superior self-correction capabilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces E2CL, a framework that helps embodied agents align their knowledge with environmental constraints by learning from errors made during exploration. The agent collects feedback from both teacher-guided and teacher-free explorations, then uses this feedback to correct its actions and improve self-correction abilities. Experiments in VirtualHome show that E2CL outperforms supervised learning and reinforcement learning baselines.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出E2CL框架，通过探索中的错误和环境反馈帮助具身智能体对齐其知识与环境约束。智能体在教师引导和自由探索中收集反馈，并利用反馈纠正动作、提升自我修正能力。在VirtualHome环境中的实验表明，E2CL优于监督学习和强化学习基线方法。

papers.title: Navigating the Nuances: A Fine-grained Evaluation of Vision-Language Navigation
papers.short_title: Fine-grained Eval of VLN
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel evaluation framework for the Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) task. It aims to diagnose current models for various instruction categories at a finer-grained level. The framework is structured around the context-free grammar (CFG) of the task. The CFG serves as the basis for the problem decomposition and the core premise of the instruction categories design. We propose a semi-automatic method for CFG construction with the help of Large-Language Models (LLMs). Then, we induct and generate data spanning five principal instruction categories (i.e. direction change, landmark recognition, region recognition, vertical movement, and numerical comprehension). Our analysis of different models reveals notable performance discrepancies and recurrent issues. The stagnation of numerical comprehension, heavy selective biases over directional concepts, and other interesting findings contribute to the development of future language-guided navigation systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a fine-grained evaluation framework for Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) that uses context-free grammar (CFG) to decompose the task into five instruction categories: direction change, landmark recognition, region recognition, vertical movement, and numerical comprehension. The authors propose a semi-automatic method to construct the CFG with large language models and generate targeted test data. Their analysis reveals significant performance gaps across models, including stagnation in numerical comprehension and biases in directional understanding, providing insights for improving future navigation systems.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种细粒度的视觉语言导航（VLN）评估框架，利用上下文无关文法（CFG）将任务分解为五个指令类别：方向变化、地标识别、区域识别、垂直移动和数值理解。作者借助大语言模型提出了一种半自动的CFG构建方法，并生成了针对性的测试数据。分析揭示了不同模型间的显著性能差异，包括数值理解的停滞和方向概念的选择性偏差，为改进未来导航系统提供了见解。

papers.title: MobileVLM: A Vision-Language Model for Better Intra- and Inter-UI Understanding
papers.short_title: MobileVLM: Intra-Inter UI VLM
papers.abstract: Recently, mobile AI agents based on VLMs have been gaining increasing attention. These works typically utilize VLM as a foundation, fine-tuning it with instruction-based mobile datasets. However, these VLMs are typically pre-trained on general-domain data, which often results in a lack of fundamental capabilities specific to the mobile domain. Therefore, they may struggle to recognize specific UI elements and understand intra-UI fine-grained information. In addition, the current fine-tuning task focuses on interacting with the most relevant element for the given instruction. These fine-tuned VLMs may still ignore the relationships between UI pages, neglect the roles of elements in page transitions and lack inter-UI understanding. To address issues, we propose a VLM called MobileVLM, which includes two additional pre-training stages to enhance both intra- and inter-UI understanding. We defined four UI-based pre-training tasks, enabling the model to better perceive fine-grained elements and capture page transition actions. To address the lack of mobile pre-training data, we built a large Chinese mobile dataset Mobile3M from scratch, which contains 3 million UI pages, and real-world transition actions, forming a directed graph structure. Experimental results show MobileVLM excels on both our test set and public mobile benchmarks, outperforming existing VLMs.
papers.summary_en: MobileVLM is a vision-language model designed for mobile UI understanding, addressing limitations in existing VLMs that lack fine-grained intra-UI recognition and inter-UI page transition awareness. It introduces two additional pre-training stages with four UI-specific tasks, and a large-scale Chinese dataset Mobile3M containing 3 million UI pages with real transition actions. The model outperforms prior VLMs on both custom and public benchmarks.
papers.summary_zh: MobileVLM是一种专为移动端UI理解设计的视觉语言模型，解决了现有VLM在细粒度UI元素识别和页面间转换理解上的不足。它通过两个额外的预训练阶段和四个UI特定任务，并构建了包含300万UI页面及真实转换动作的大规模中文数据集Mobile3M，在自定义测试集和公开基准上均优于现有VLM。

papers.title: FlowBench: Revisiting and Benchmarking Workflow-Guided Planning for LLM-based Agents
papers.short_title: FlowBench: Workflow Planning for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents have emerged as promising tools, which are crafted to fulfill complex tasks by iterative planning and action. However, these agents are susceptible to undesired planning hallucinations when lacking specific knowledge for expertise-intensive tasks. To address this, preliminary attempts are made to enhance planning reliability by incorporating external workflow-related knowledge. Despite the promise, such infused knowledge is mostly disorganized and diverse in formats, lacking rigorous formalization and comprehensive comparisons. Motivated by this, we formalize different formats of workflow knowledge and present FlowBench, the first benchmark for workflow-guided planning. FlowBench covers 51 different scenarios from 6 domains, with knowledge presented in diverse formats. To assess different LLMs on FlowBench, we design a multi-tiered evaluation framework. We evaluate the efficacy of workflow knowledge across multiple formats, and the results indicate that current LLM agents need considerable improvements for satisfactory planning. We hope that our challenging benchmark can pave the way for future agent planning research.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces FlowBench, the first benchmark for workflow-guided planning in LLM-based agents, covering 51 scenarios across 6 domains with diverse workflow formats. It formalizes different types of workflow knowledge and proposes a multi-tiered evaluation framework to assess LLMs. Experiments show that current agents still require significant improvements for reliable planning, highlighting the benchmark's value for future research.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了FlowBench，这是首个面向基于LLM的智能体工作流引导规划的基准，涵盖6个领域的51个场景及多种工作流格式。它形式化了不同类型的工作流知识，并设计了多层次评估框架来评测LLM。实验表明，当前智能体在可靠规划方面仍需大幅改进，凸显了该基准对未来研究的价值。

papers.title: Watch Every Step! LLM Agent Learning via Iterative Step-level Process Refinement
papers.short_title: IPR: Iterative Step-level Process Refinement
papers.abstract: Large language model agents have exhibited exceptional performance across a range of complex interactive tasks. Recent approaches have utilized tuning with expert trajectories to enhance agent performance, yet they primarily concentrate on outcome rewards, which may lead to errors or suboptimal actions due to the absence of process supervision signals. In this paper, we introduce the **I**terative step-level **P**rocess **R**efinement **(IPR)** framework, which provides detailed step-by-step guidance to enhance agent training. Specifically, we adopt the Monte Carlo method to estimate step-level rewards. During each iteration, the agent explores along the expert trajectory and generates new actions. These actions are then evaluated against the corresponding step of expert trajectory using step-level rewards. Such comparison helps identify discrepancies, yielding contrastive action pairs that serve as training data for the agent. Our experiments on three complex agent tasks demonstrate that our framework outperforms a variety of strong baselines. Moreover, our analytical finds highlight the effectiveness of IPR in augmenting action efficiency and its applicability to diverse models.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces the Iterative Step-level Process Refinement (IPR) framework for training LLM agents, which uses Monte Carlo methods to estimate step-level rewards and generates contrastive action pairs by comparing agent actions with expert trajectories. Unlike prior work focusing on outcome rewards, IPR provides detailed step-by-step guidance, improving agent performance on complex interactive tasks. Experiments show IPR outperforms strong baselines and enhances action efficiency across diverse models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出迭代步骤级过程优化（IPR）框架，用于训练大语言模型智能体。该框架采用蒙特卡洛方法估计步骤级奖励，通过对比智能体动作与专家轨迹生成对比动作对，提供详细的逐步指导。与仅关注结果奖励的先前工作不同，IPR在复杂交互任务上显著提升智能体性能，实验表明其优于多种强基线方法，并能提高动作效率，适用于不同模型。

papers.title: RESTful-Llama: Connecting User Queries to RESTful APIs
papers.short_title: RESTful-Llama: Queries to REST APIs
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have showcased exceptional performance in zero-shot learning and reasoning tasks. However, integrating these models with external tools - a crucial need for real-world applications - remains a significant challenge. We propose RESTful-Llama, a novel framework designed to enable Llama 3.1 to transform natural language instructions into effective RESTful API calls. To enhance the fine-tuning process, we introduce DOC_Mine, a method to generate fine-tuning datasets from public API documentation. RESTful-Llama distinguishes itself by enabling open-source LLMs to efficiently interact with and adapt to any REST API system. Experiments demonstrate a 31.9% improvement in robustness and a 2.33x increase in efficiency compared to existing methods.
papers.summary_en: RESTful-Llama is a framework that fine-tunes Llama 3.1 to convert natural language into RESTful API calls, using a novel dataset generation method called DOC_Mine from API documentation. It enables open-source LLMs to interact with any REST API, achieving a 31.9% improvement in robustness and 2.33x efficiency gain over existing methods.
papers.summary_zh: RESTful-Llama是一个框架，通过微调Llama 3.1将自然语言转换为RESTful API调用，并利用名为DOC_Mine的新方法从API文档生成微调数据集。它使开源LLM能够与任何REST API交互，相比现有方法，鲁棒性提升31.9%，效率提升2.33倍。

papers.title: AssistantBench: Can Web Agents Solve Realistic and Time-Consuming Tasks?
papers.short_title: AssistantBench: Web Agents Realistic Tasks
papers.abstract: Language agents, built on top of language models (LMs), are systems that can interact with complex environments, such as the open web. In this work, we examine whether such agents can perform realistic and time-consuming tasks on the web, e.g., monitoring real-estate markets or locating relevant nearby businesses. We introduce AssistantBench, a challenging new benchmark consisting of 214 realistic tasks that can be automatically evaluated, covering different scenarios and domains. We find that AssistantBench exposes the limitations of current systems, including language models and retrieval-augmented language models, as no model reaches an accuracy of more than 25 points. While closed-book LMs perform well in terms of accuracy, they exhibit low precision and tend to hallucinate facts. State-of-the-art web agents reach a score of near zero. Additionally, we introduce SeePlanAct (SPA), a new web agent that significantly outperforms previous agents, and an ensemble of SPA and closed-book models reaches the best overall performance. Moreover, we analyze failures of current systems and highlight that open web navigation remains a major challenge.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces AssistantBench, a benchmark of 214 realistic web tasks that are time-consuming and automatically evaluable, revealing that current language agents and models achieve at most 25% accuracy. It also presents SeePlanAct (SPA), a new web agent that outperforms prior agents, and shows that combining SPA with closed-book models yields the best performance, while highlighting open web navigation as a major remaining challenge.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文提出了AssistantBench，一个包含214个耗时且可自动评估的现实网络任务的基准测试，揭示了当前语言智能体和模型最多只能达到25%的准确率。同时，论文介绍了SeePlanAct（SPA），一种优于先前智能体的新型网络智能体，并展示了将SPA与闭卷模型结合可获得最佳性能，同时指出开放网络导航仍是一个主要挑战。

papers.title: R-Judge: Benchmarking Safety Risk Awareness for LLM Agents
papers.short_title: R-Judge: Safety Risk Awareness LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have exhibited great potential in autonomously completing tasks across real-world applications. Despite this, these LLM agents introduce unexpected safety risks when operating in interactive environments. Instead of centering on the harmlessness of LLM-generated content in most prior studies, this work addresses the imperative need for benchmarking the behavioral safety of LLM agents within diverse environments. We introduce R-Judge, a benchmark crafted to evaluate the proficiency of LLMs in judging and identifying safety risks given agent interaction records. R-Judge comprises 569 records of multi-turn agent interaction, encompassing 27 key risk scenarios among 5 application categories and 10 risk types. It is of high-quality curation with annotated safety labels and risk descriptions. Evaluation of 11 LLMs on R-Judge shows considerable room for enhancing the risk awareness of LLMs: The best-performing model, GPT-4o, achieves 74.42% while no other models significantly exceed the random. Moreover, we reveal that risk awareness in open agent scenarios is a multi-dimensional capability involving knowledge and reasoning, thus challenging for LLMs. With further experiments, we find that fine-tuning on safety judgment significantly improve model performance while straightforward prompting mechanisms fail. R-Judge is publicly available at https://github.com/Lordog/R-Judge.
papers.summary_en: R-Judge is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' ability to identify safety risks in interactive environments, featuring 569 multi-turn interaction records across 27 risk scenarios. Tests on 11 LLMs show that even the best model, GPT-4o, achieves only 74.42% accuracy, with most models near random performance, indicating significant room for improvement. The study reveals that risk awareness requires both knowledge and reasoning, and fine-tuning on safety judgment is more effective than prompting.
papers.summary_zh: R-Judge是一个用于评估大语言模型代理在交互环境中识别安全风险能力的基准，包含569条多轮交互记录，覆盖27个风险场景。对11个模型的测试显示，最佳模型GPT-4o仅达到74.42%的准确率，多数模型接近随机水平，表明风险意识仍有很大提升空间。研究揭示风险意识需要知识与推理的结合，且针对安全判断的微调比提示工程更有效。

papers.title: Dynamic Planning for LLM-based Graphical User Interface Automation
papers.short_title: Dynamic Planning LLM GUI Automation
papers.abstract: The advent of large language models (LLMs) has spurred considerable interest in advancing autonomous LLMs-based agents, particularly in intriguing applications within smartphone graphical user interfaces (GUIs). When presented with a task goal, these agents typically emulate human actions within a GUI environment until the task is completed. However, a key challenge lies in devising effective plans to guide action prediction in GUI tasks, though planning have been widely recognized as effective for decomposing complex tasks into a series of steps. Specifically, given the dynamic nature of environmental GUIs following action execution, it is crucial to dynamically adapt plans based on environmental feedback and action history.We show that the widely-used ReAct approach fails due to the excessively long historical dialogues. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach called Dynamic Planning of Thoughts (D-PoT) for LLM-based GUI agents.D-PoT involves the dynamic adjustment of planning based on the environmental feedback and execution history. Experimental results reveal that the proposed D-PoT significantly surpassed the strong GPT-4V baseline by +12.7% (34.66% $\rightarrow$ 47.36%) in accuracy. The analysis highlights the generality of dynamic planning in different backbone LLMs, as well as the benefits in mitigating hallucinations and adapting to unseen tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/sqzhang-lazy/D-PoT.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces Dynamic Planning of Thoughts (D-PoT), a method for LLM-based GUI agents that dynamically adjusts task plans based on environmental feedback and action history, addressing the failure of static planning approaches like ReAct due to long historical dialogues. D-PoT significantly improves accuracy by 12.7% over GPT-4V on GUI tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating hallucinations and adapting to unseen tasks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种名为动态思维规划（D-PoT）的方法，用于基于大语言模型的图形用户界面代理。该方法根据环境反馈和执行历史动态调整任务计划，解决了ReAct等静态规划方法因历史对话过长而失效的问题。在GUI任务上，D-PoT相比GPT-4V基线准确率提升了12.7%，有效缓解了幻觉问题并适应了未见过的任务。

papers.title: PPTC-R benchmark: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models for PowerPoint Task Completion
papers.short_title: PPTC-R: Robustness LLM PowerPoint Tasks
papers.abstract: The growing dependence on Large Language Models (LLMs) for finishing user instructions necessitates a comprehensive understanding of their robustness to complex task completion in real-world situations. To address this critical need, we propose the PowerPoint Task Completion Robustness benchmark (PPTC-R) to measure LLMs' robustness to the user PPT task instruction and software version. Specifically, we construct adversarial user instructions by attacking user instructions at sentence, semantic, and multi-language levels. To assess the robustness of Language Models to software versions, we vary the number of provided APIs to simulate both the newest version and earlier version settings. Subsequently, we test 3 closed-source and 4 open-source LLMs using a benchmark that incorporates these robustness settings, aiming to evaluate how deviations impact LLMs' API calls for task completion. We find that GPT-4 exhibits the highest performance and strong robustness in our benchmark, particularly in the version update and the multilingual settings. However, we find that all LLMs lose their robustness when confronted with multiple challenges (e.g., multi-turn) simultaneously, leading to significant performance drops. We further analyze the robustness behavior and error reasons of LLMs in our benchmark, which provide valuable insights for researchers to understand the LLM's robustness in task completion and develop more robust LLMs and agents. We release the code and data at \url{https://github.com/ZekaiGalaxy/PPTCR}.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces PPTC-R, a benchmark to evaluate the robustness of large language models (LLMs) in completing PowerPoint tasks under adversarial user instructions and varying software versions. It tests seven LLMs by attacking instructions at sentence, semantic, and multilingual levels, and by simulating different API availability. Results show GPT-4 is most robust, but all models struggle with multiple simultaneous challenges like multi-turn interactions. The benchmark provides insights for developing more robust LLMs and agents.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文提出了PPTC-R基准，用于评估大语言模型在完成PowerPoint任务时面对对抗性用户指令和软件版本变化的鲁棒性。它通过攻击句子、语义和多语言层面的指令，并模拟不同API可用性，测试了七个大语言模型。结果显示GPT-4鲁棒性最强，但所有模型在同时面对多轮交互等多重挑战时表现显著下降。该基准为开发更鲁棒的模型和智能体提供了见解。

papers.title: Android in the Zoo: Chain-of-Action-Thought for GUI Agents
papers.short_title: Android Zoo: CoAT for GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) leads to a surge of autonomous GUI agents for smartphone, which completes a task triggered by natural language through predicting a sequence of actions of API. Even though the task highly relies on past actions and visual observations, existing studies typically consider little semantic information carried out by intermediate screenshots and screen operations. To address this, this work presents Chain-of-Action-Thought (dubbed CoAT), which takes the description of the previous actions, the current screen, and more importantly the action thinking of what actions should be performed and the outcomes led by the chosen action. We demonstrate that, in a zero-shot setting upon three off-the-shelf LMMs, CoAT significantly improves the action prediction compared to previous proposed context modeling. To further facilitate the research in this line, we construct a dataset Android-In-The-Zoo (AitZ), which contains 18,643 screen-action pairs together with chain-of-action-thought annotations. Experiments show that fine-tuning a 1B model (i.e. AUTO-UI-base) on our AitZ dataset achieves on-par performance with CogAgent-Chat-18B.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces Chain-of-Action-Thought (CoAT), a method that enhances GUI agents by incorporating descriptions of past actions, current screens, and reasoning about future actions and their outcomes. CoAT significantly improves action prediction in zero-shot settings across three large multimodal models. The authors also present Android-In-The-Zoo (AitZ), a dataset of 18,643 screen-action pairs with CoAT annotations, enabling a 1B model to match the performance of an 18B model after fine-tuning.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出链式动作思维（CoAT），通过整合历史动作描述、当前屏幕信息以及对未来动作及其结果的推理，增强了GUI代理的性能。CoAT在三个现有多模态模型的零样本设置中显著提升了动作预测。作者还构建了Android-In-The-Zoo（AitZ）数据集，包含18,643个屏幕-动作对及CoAT标注，使得1B参数模型微调后性能与18B参数模型相当。

papers.title: WebOlympus: An Open Platform for Web Agents on Live Websites
papers.short_title: WebOlympus: Open Platform for Web Agents
papers.abstract: Web agents are emerging as powerful tools capable of performing complex tasks across diverse web environments. The rapid development of large multimodal models is further enhancing this advancement. However, there is a lack of standardized and user-friendly tools for research and development, as well as experimental platforms on live websites. To address this challenge, we present WebOlympus, an open platform for web agents operating on live websites. WebOlympus offers a Chrome extension-based UI, enabling users without programming experience to easily utilize the platform. It allows users to run web agents with various designs using only a few lines of code or simple clicks on the Chrome extension. To ensure the trustworthiness of web agents, a safety monitor module that prevents harmful actions through human supervision or model-based control is incorporated. WebOlympus supports diverse applications, including annotation interfaces for web agent trajectories and data crawling.
papers.summary_en: WebOlympus is an open platform for web agents operating on live websites, featuring a Chrome extension UI that allows users without programming experience to easily run agents. It supports various agent designs with minimal code or clicks, includes a safety monitor module for preventing harmful actions, and enables applications like trajectory annotation and data crawling.
papers.summary_zh: WebOlympus是一个面向实时网站的网络代理开放平台，通过Chrome扩展界面让无编程经验的用户也能轻松运行代理。它支持用少量代码或点击运行多种代理设计，内置安全监控模块防止有害行为，并支持轨迹标注和数据爬取等应用。

papers.title: MCPEval: Automatic MCP-based Deep Evaluation for AI Agent Models
papers.short_title: MCPEval: MCP-based Eval for AI Agents
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of Large Language Models (LLMs)-based intelligent agents underscores the need for robust, scalable evaluation frameworks. Existing methods rely on static benchmarks and labor-intensive data collection, limiting practical assessment. We introduce MCPEval, an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based framework that automates end-to-end task generation and deep evaluation of LLM agents across diverse domains. MCPEval standardizes metrics, seamlessly integrates with native agent tools, and eliminates manual effort in building evaluation pipelines. Empirical results across five real-world domains show its effectiveness in revealing nuanced, domain-specific performance. We publicly release MCPEval https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/MCPEval to promote reproducible and standardized LLM agent evaluation.
papers.summary_en: MCPEval is an open-source framework that automates the generation and evaluation of tasks for LLM-based agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It eliminates manual effort in building evaluation pipelines, standardizes metrics, and integrates with native agent tools. Experiments across five domains show it effectively reveals nuanced, domain-specific performance, promoting reproducible and standardized evaluation.
papers.summary_zh: MCPEval是一个基于模型上下文协议（MCP）的开源框架，能够自动生成并评估大语言模型（LLM）智能体的任务。它消除了构建评估流程的手工劳动，标准化了评估指标，并与原生智能体工具无缝集成。在五个真实领域上的实验表明，该框架能有效揭示细粒度的领域特定性能，推动了可复现、标准化的LLM智能体评估。

papers.title: AgentCPM-GUI: Building Mobile-Use Agents with Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
papers.short_title: AgentCPM-GUI: Mobile Agents via RL Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: The recent progress of large language model agents has opened new possibilities for automating tasks through graphical user interfaces (GUIs), especially in mobile environments where intelligent interaction can greatly enhance usability. However, practical deployment of such agents remains constrained by several key challenges. Existing training data is often noisy and lack semantic diversity, which hinders the learning of precise grounding and planning. Models trained purely by imitation tend to overfit to seen interface patterns and fail to generalize in unfamiliar scenarios. Moreover, most prior work focuses on English interfaces while overlooks the growing diversity of non-English applications such as those in the Chinese mobile ecosystem. In this work, we present AgentCPM-GUI, an 8B-parameter GUI agent built for robust and efficient on-device GUI interaction. Our training pipeline includes grounding-aware pre-training to enhance perception, supervised fine-tuning on high-quality Chinese and English trajectories to imitate human-like actions, and reinforcement fine-tuning with GRPO to improve reasoning capability. We also introduce a compact action space that reduces output length and supports low-latency execution on mobile devices. AgentCPM-GUI achieves state-of-the-art performance on five public benchmarks and a new Chinese GUI benchmark called CAGUI, reaching $96.9\%$ Type-Match and $91.3\%$ Exact-Match. To facilitate reproducibility and further research, we publicly release all code, model checkpoint, and evaluation data.
papers.summary_en: AgentCPM-GUI is an 8B-parameter mobile GUI agent that achieves state-of-the-art performance through a three-stage training pipeline: grounding-aware pre-training, supervised fine-tuning on high-quality Chinese and English trajectories, and reinforcement fine-tuning with GRPO. It introduces a compact action space for low-latency on-device execution and sets new benchmarks on five public datasets and a new Chinese GUI benchmark CAGUI, with 96.9% Type-Match and 91.3% Exact-Match. The model, code, and data are publicly released.
papers.summary_zh: AgentCPM-GUI是一个80亿参数的移动GUI智能体，通过三阶段训练流程（感知预训练、高质量中英文轨迹监督微调、GRPO强化微调）实现最优性能。它采用紧凑动作空间以支持低延迟设备端执行，在五个公开数据集和新中文GUI基准CAGUI上达到96.9%类型匹配和91.3%精确匹配的新标杆。模型、代码和数据均已开源。

papers.title: FlashAdventure: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Solving Full Story Arcs in Diverse Adventure Games
papers.short_title: FlashAdventure: GUI Agents in Adventure Games
papers.abstract: GUI agents powered by LLMs show promise in interacting with diverse digital environments. Among these, video games offer a valuable testbed due to their varied interfaces, with adventure games posing additional challenges through complex, narrative-driven interactions. Existing game benchmarks, however, lack diversity and rarely evaluate agents on completing entire storylines. To address this, we introduce FlashAdventure, a benchmark of 34 Flash-based adventure games designed to test full story arc completion and tackle the observation-behavior gap: the challenge of remembering and acting on earlier gameplay information. We also propose CUA-as-a-Judge, an automated gameplay evaluator, and COAST, an agentic framework leveraging long-term clue memory to better plan and solve sequential tasks. Experiments show current GUI agents struggle with full story arcs, while COAST improves milestone completion by bridging the observation-behavior gap. Nonetheless, a marked discrepancy between humans and best-performing agents warrants continued research efforts to narrow this divide.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces FlashAdventure, a benchmark of 34 Flash adventure games for evaluating GUI agents on completing entire story arcs, addressing the observation-behavior gap where agents must remember and act on earlier information. The authors propose CUA-as-a-Judge for automated evaluation and COAST, an agentic framework with long-term clue memory to improve sequential task planning. Experiments show current agents struggle with full story arcs, but COAST improves milestone completion, though a significant gap remains compared to human performance.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了FlashAdventure基准，包含34个Flash冒险游戏，用于评估GUI代理完成完整故事弧的能力，并解决观察-行为差距（即代理需记住并利用早期信息）。作者提出了CUA-as-a-Judge自动评估方法和COAST框架，后者通过长期线索记忆改进顺序任务规划。实验表明现有代理难以完成完整故事弧，但COAST提升了里程碑完成率，然而与人类表现仍有显著差距。

papers.title: IPIGuard: A Novel Tool Dependency Graph-Based Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
papers.short_title: IPIGuard: Tool Graph Defense vs Prompt Injection
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are widely deployed in real-world applications, where they leverage tools to retrieve and manipulate external data for complex tasks. However, when interacting with untrusted data sources (e.g., fetching information from public websites), tool responses may contain injected instructions that covertly influence agent behaviors and lead to malicious outcomes, a threat referred to as Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI). Existing defenses typically rely on advanced prompting strategies or auxiliary detection models. While these methods have demonstrated some effectiveness, they fundamentally rely on assumptions about the model's inherent security, which lacks structural constraints on agent behaviors. As a result, agents still retain unrestricted access to tool invocations, leaving them vulnerable to stronger attack vectors that can bypass the security guardrails of the model. To prevent malicious tool invocations at the source, we propose a novel defensive task execution paradigm, called IPIGuard, which models the agents'task execution process as a traversal over a planned Tool Dependency Graph (TDG). By explicitly decoupling action planning from interaction with external data, IPIGuard significantly reduces unintended tool invocations triggered by injected instructions, thereby enhancing robustness against IPI attacks. Experiments on the AgentDojo benchmark show that IPIGuard achieves a superior balance between effectiveness and robustness, paving the way for the development of safer agentic systems in dynamic environments.
papers.summary_en: IPIGuard is a defense against indirect prompt injection attacks on LLM agents that use tools. It models task execution as a traversal over a planned Tool Dependency Graph (TDG), decoupling action planning from external data interaction. This structural constraint prevents malicious tool invocations triggered by injected instructions, achieving a better balance of effectiveness and robustness than existing methods.
papers.summary_zh: IPIGuard是一种针对使用工具的LLM智能体的间接提示注入攻击的防御方法。它将任务执行建模为对预规划的工具依赖图（TDG）的遍历，将动作规划与外部数据交互解耦。这种结构性约束阻止了由注入指令触发的恶意工具调用，在有效性和鲁棒性之间取得了比现有方法更好的平衡。

papers.title: WebMMU: A Benchmark for Multimodal Multilingual Website Understanding and Code Generation
papers.short_title: WebMMU: Multimodal Multilingual Website Benchmark
papers.abstract: We present WebMMU, a multilingual benchmark that evaluates three core web tasks: (1) website visual question answering, (2) code editing involving HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and (3) mockup-to-code generation. Unlike prior benchmarks that treat these tasks separately, WebMMU unifies them using expert-annotated, real-world web data to assess models'abilities in complex multi-step reasoning, precise element grounding, and functional UI comprehension and coding. Our evaluation shows that while multimodal large language models (MLLMs) perform well on basic information extraction, they struggle with reasoning and grounding, editing code to preserve functionality, and generating design-to-code that maintains hierarchy and supports multilingual content. These findings reveal key limitations in current MLLMs and underscore the need for improved multimodal and cross-lingual reasoning to build future web agents capable of automating diverse web development tasks.
papers.summary_en: WebMMU is a new benchmark that unifies three web tasks—visual question answering, code editing, and mockup-to-code generation—using expert-annotated real-world data. It evaluates multimodal LLMs on complex reasoning, element grounding, and functional UI understanding. Results show models struggle with reasoning, preserving code functionality, and generating design-to-code that maintains hierarchy and supports multilingual content, highlighting key limitations for future web agents.
papers.summary_zh: WebMMU是一个新的基准测试，它通过专家标注的真实网页数据，统一了三个网页任务：视觉问答、代码编辑和设计图到代码生成。该基准评估多模态大语言模型在复杂推理、元素定位和功能UI理解方面的能力。结果表明，模型在推理、保持代码功能以及生成维护层次结构并支持多语言内容的设计图到代码方面存在困难，揭示了当前模型的关键局限，为未来网页代理的开发指明了方向。

papers.title: NESTFUL: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Nested Sequences of API Calls
papers.short_title: NESTFUL: Nested API Calls Benchmark
papers.abstract: The resurgence of autonomous agents built using large language models (LLMs) to solve complex real-world tasks has brought increased focus on LLMs' fundamental ability of tool or function calling. At the core of these agents, an LLM must plan, execute, and respond using external tools, APIs, and custom functions. Research on tool calling has gathered momentum, but evaluation benchmarks and datasets representing the complexity of the tasks have lagged behind. In this work, we focus on one such complexity, nested sequencing, with the goal of extending existing benchmarks and evaluation. Specifically, we present NESTFUL, a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on nested sequences of API calls, i.e., sequences where the output of one API call is passed as input to a subsequent call. NESTFUL contains 1800+ nested sequences where all the function calls are executable. Experimental results on a variety of models show that the best-performing model (GPT-4o) achieves a full sequence match accuracy of 28% and a win-rate of 60%, necessitating a large scope for improvement in the nested sequencing aspect of function calling. Our analysis of these results provides possible future research directions for the community, in addition to a benchmark to track progress. We have released the NESTFUL dataset under the Apache 2.0 license at https://github.com/IBM/NESTFUL.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces NESTFUL, a benchmark for evaluating large language models on nested sequences of API calls, where the output of one call becomes input to another. It contains over 1,800 executable sequences, and experiments show that even the best model (GPT-4o) achieves only 28% accuracy and 60% win-rate, highlighting significant room for improvement in nested function calling. The benchmark and analysis aim to guide future research in tool-use capabilities of LLMs.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了NESTFUL基准，用于评估大语言模型在嵌套API调用序列上的表现，其中一次调用的输出作为后续调用的输入。该基准包含1800多个可执行序列，实验表明最佳模型（GPT-4o）仅达到28%的完整序列匹配准确率和60%的胜率，凸显了嵌套函数调用能力的巨大提升空间。该基准和分析旨在为LLM工具使用能力的未来研究提供方向。

papers.title: FlightGPT: Towards Generalizable and Interpretable UAV Vision-and-Language Navigation with Vision-Language Models
papers.short_title: FlightGPT: UAV VLN with VLMs
papers.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) is vital for applications such as disaster response, logistics delivery, and urban inspection. However, existing methods often struggle with insufficient multimodal fusion, weak generalization, and poor interpretability. To address these challenges, we propose FlightGPT, a novel UAV VLN framework built upon Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with powerful multimodal perception capabilities. We design a two-stage training pipeline: first, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) using high-quality demonstrations to improve initialization and structured reasoning; then, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm, guided by a composite reward that considers goal accuracy, reasoning quality, and format compliance, to enhance generalization and adaptability. Furthermore, FlightGPT introduces a Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-based reasoning mechanism to improve decision interpretability. Extensive experiments on the city-scale dataset CityNav demonstrate that FlightGPT achieves state-of-the-art performance across all scenarios, with a 9.22\% higher success rate than the strongest baseline in unseen environments. Our implementation is publicly available.
papers.summary_en: FlightGPT is a new framework for UAV vision-and-language navigation that leverages vision-language models to improve multimodal fusion, generalization, and interpretability. It uses a two-stage training pipeline with supervised fine-tuning and group relative policy optimization, along with a chain-of-thought reasoning mechanism. Experiments on the CityNav dataset show it achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a 9.22% higher success rate in unseen environments.
papers.summary_zh: FlightGPT是一种面向无人机视觉-语言导航的新框架，利用视觉语言模型增强多模态融合、泛化能力和可解释性。它采用两阶段训练流程，包括监督微调和分组相对策略优化，并引入思维链推理机制。在城市级数据集CityNav上的实验表明，该框架在所有场景中均达到最优性能，在未知环境中成功率比最强基线高出9.22%。

papers.title: Hidden Ghost Hand: Unveiling Backdoor Vulnerabilities in MLLM-Powered Mobile GUI Agents
papers.short_title: Hidden Ghost Hand: Backdoor in MLLM GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown greater promise for human-interaction. However, due to the high fine-tuning cost, users often rely on open-source GUI agents or APIs offered by AI providers, which introduces a critical but underexplored supply chain threat: backdoor attacks. In this work, we first unveil that MLLM-powered GUI agents naturally expose multiple interaction-level triggers, such as historical steps, environment states, and task progress. Based on this observation, we introduce AgentGhost, an effective and stealthy framework for red-teaming backdoor attacks. Specifically, we first construct composite triggers by combining goal and interaction levels, allowing GUI agents to unintentionally activate backdoors while ensuring task utility. Then, we formulate backdoor injection as a Min-Max optimization problem that uses supervised contrastive learning to maximize the feature difference across sample classes at the representation space, improving flexibility of the backdoor. Meanwhile, it adopts supervised fine-tuning to minimize the discrepancy between backdoor and clean behavior generation, enhancing effectiveness and utility. Extensive evaluations of various agent models in two established mobile benchmarks show that AgentGhost is effective and generic, with attack accuracy that reaches 99.7\% on three attack objectives, and shows stealthiness with only 1\% utility degradation. Furthermore, we tailor a defense method against AgentGhost that reduces the attack accuracy to 22.1\%. Our code is available at \texttt{anonymous}.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a new backdoor attack vulnerability in MLLM-powered mobile GUI agents, where attackers can inject hidden triggers into the agent's interaction history or task progress. The proposed AgentGhost framework uses composite triggers and a min-max optimization with contrastive learning to achieve high attack success (99.7%) with minimal utility loss (1%). The work also presents a defense method that reduces attack accuracy to 22.1%, highlighting the need for security measures in GUI agent supply chains.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了多模态大模型驱动的移动GUI代理中存在的新型后门攻击漏洞，攻击者可通过交互历史或任务进度等触发器注入隐藏后门。提出的AgentGhost框架利用复合触发器和基于对比学习的极小极大优化，实现了99.7%的攻击成功率且仅造成1%的效用损失。同时，本文还设计了一种防御方法，将攻击成功率降至22.1%，强调了GUI代理供应链中安全防护的必要性。

papers.title: GUI-Bee: Align GUI Action Grounding to Novel Environments via Autonomous Exploration
papers.short_title: GUI-Bee: GUI Grounding via Exploration
papers.abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) action grounding is a critical step in GUI automation that maps language instructions to actionable elements on GUI screens. Most recent works of GUI action grounding leverage large GUI datasets to fine-tune MLLMs. However, the fine-tuning data always covers limited GUI environments, and we find the performance of the resulting model deteriorates in novel environments. We argue that the GUI grounding models should be further aligned to the novel environments to reveal their full potential, when the inference is known to involve novel environments, i.e., environments not used during the previous fine-tuning. To realize this, we first propose GUI-Bee, an MLLM-based autonomous agent, to collect high-quality, environment-specific data through exploration and then continuously fine-tune GUI grounding models with the collected data. Our agent leverages a novel Q-value-Incentive In-Context Reinforcement Learning (Q-ICRL) method to optimize exploration efficiency and data quality. Additionally, we introduce NovelScreenSpot, a benchmark for testing how well the data can help align GUI action grounding models to novel environments and demonstrate the effectiveness of data collected by GUI-Bee in the experiments. Furthermore, we conduct an ablation study to validate the Q-ICRL method in enhancing the efficiency of GUI-Bee. Project page: https://gui-bee.github.io
papers.summary_en: GUI-Bee is an autonomous agent that improves GUI action grounding models for novel environments by collecting high-quality, environment-specific data through exploration and continuous fine-tuning. It uses a Q-value-Incentive In-Context Reinforcement Learning method to optimize exploration efficiency and data quality. The paper also introduces NovelScreenSpot, a benchmark for evaluating alignment to novel environments, and shows that GUI-Bee effectively enhances model performance in such settings.
papers.summary_zh: GUI-Bee是一个自主智能体，通过探索收集高质量、环境特定的数据并持续微调，来改进图形用户界面动作定位模型在新环境中的表现。它采用了一种基于Q值激励的上下文强化学习方法，以优化探索效率和数据质量。论文还引入了NovelScreenSpot基准，用于评估模型对新环境的适应能力，实验表明GUI-Bee能有效提升模型在新环境中的性能。

papers.title: VistaWise: Building Cost-Effective Agent with Cross-Modal Knowledge Graph for Minecraft
papers.short_title: VistaWise: Cross-Modal KG for Minecraft
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown significant promise in embodied decision-making tasks within virtual open-world environments. Nonetheless, their performance is hindered by the absence of domain-specific knowledge. Methods that finetune on large-scale domain-specific data entail prohibitive development costs. This paper introduces VistaWise, a cost-effective agent framework that integrates cross-modal domain knowledge and finetunes a dedicated object detection model for visual analysis. It reduces the requirement for domain-specific training data from millions of samples to a few hundred. VistaWise integrates visual information and textual dependencies into a cross-modal knowledge graph (KG), enabling a comprehensive and accurate understanding of multimodal environments. We also equip the agent with a retrieval-based pooling strategy to extract task-related information from the KG, and a desktop-level skill library to support direct operation of the Minecraft desktop client via mouse and keyboard inputs. Experimental results demonstrate that VistaWise achieves state-of-the-art performance across various open-world tasks, highlighting its effectiveness in reducing development costs while enhancing agent performance.
papers.summary_en: VistaWise is a cost-effective agent framework for Minecraft that integrates a cross-modal knowledge graph and a fine-tuned object detection model, reducing domain-specific training data from millions to hundreds of samples. It combines visual and textual information into a knowledge graph, uses a retrieval-based pooling strategy for task-relevant information extraction, and includes a desktop-level skill library for direct client control. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on open-world tasks while significantly lowering development costs.
papers.summary_zh: VistaWise是一种用于Minecraft的高性价比智能体框架，它集成了跨模态知识图谱和微调的目标检测模型，将领域特定训练数据从数百万样本减少到数百个。该框架将视觉和文本信息整合到知识图谱中，采用基于检索的池化策略提取任务相关信息，并包含桌面级技能库以直接控制客户端。在开放世界任务中，VistaWise实现了最先进的性能，同时显著降低了开发成本。

papers.title: KG-RAG: Enhancing GUI Agent Decision-Making via Knowledge Graph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.short_title: KG-RAG: GUI Agent Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Despite recent progress, Graphic User Interface (GUI) agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle with complex mobile tasks due to limited app-specific knowledge. While UI Transition Graphs (UTGs) offer structured navigation representations, they are underutilized due to poor extraction and inefficient integration. We introduce KG-RAG, a Knowledge Graph-driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework that transforms fragmented UTGs into structured vector databases for efficient real-time retrieval. By leveraging an intent-guided LLM search method, KG-RAG generates actionable navigation paths, enhancing agent decision-making. Experiments across diverse mobile apps show that KG-RAG outperforms existing methods, achieving a 75.8% success rate (8.9% improvement over AutoDroid), 84.6% decision accuracy (8.1% improvement), and reducing average task steps from 4.5 to 4.1. Additionally, we present KG-Android-Bench and KG-Harmony-Bench, two benchmarks tailored to the Chinese mobile ecosystem for future research.
