Finally, KG-RAG transfers to web/desktop (+40% SR on Weibo-web; +20% on QQ Music-desktop), and a UTG cost ablation shows accuracy saturates at ~4h per complex app, enabling practical deployment trade-offs.
papers.summary_en: KG-RAG is a framework that converts fragmented UI Transition Graphs into structured vector databases for real-time retrieval, using intent-guided LLM search to generate navigation paths for GUI agents. It improves decision-making in mobile tasks, achieving 75.8% success rate and 84.6% decision accuracy, outperforming prior methods. The framework also generalizes to web and desktop environments, and introduces two benchmarks for the Chinese mobile ecosystem.
papers.summary_zh: KG-RAG是一个将碎片化的UI转换图转化为结构化向量数据库以支持实时检索的框架，通过意图引导的LLM搜索生成导航路径，增强GUI代理的决策能力。在移动任务中，它实现了75.8%的成功率和84.6%的决策准确率，优于现有方法。该框架还能泛化到网页和桌面环境，并引入了两个面向中国移动生态的基准测试。

papers.title: WebCoT: Enhancing Web Agent Reasoning by Reconstructing Chain-of-Thought in Reflection, Branching, and Rollback
papers.short_title: WebCoT: Reconstructing CoT with Reflection
papers.abstract: Web agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise for next-generation AI, but their limited reasoning in uncertain, dynamic web environments hinders robust deployment. In this paper, we identify key reasoning skills essential for effective web agents, i.e., reflection&lookahead, branching, and rollback, and curate trajectory data that exemplifies these abilities by reconstructing the agent's (inference-time) reasoning algorithms into chain-of-thought rationales. We conduct experiments in the agent self-improving benchmark, OpenWebVoyager, and demonstrate that distilling salient reasoning patterns into the backbone LLM via simple fine-tuning can substantially enhance its performance. Our approach yields significant improvements across multiple benchmarks, including WebVoyager, Mind2web-live, and SimpleQA (web search), highlighting the potential of targeted reasoning skill enhancement for web agents.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies three key reasoning skills—reflection & lookahead, branching, and rollback—that are crucial for web agents to handle uncertain and dynamic environments. The authors reconstruct these reasoning patterns into chain-of-thought rationales from agent trajectories and fine-tune a large language model on this data. Their method significantly improves performance on web agent benchmarks like WebVoyager and Mind2web-live, demonstrating that targeted reasoning skill enhancement can boost agent capabilities.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别出三种关键推理技能——反思与前瞻、分支和回滚——这些技能对于网络代理在不确定和动态环境中运行至关重要。作者通过将代理轨迹中的推理算法重构为思维链理由，并基于此数据微调大型语言模型。该方法在WebVoyager和Mind2web-live等多个网络代理基准测试上显著提升了性能，表明针对性的推理技能增强可以提升代理能力。

papers.title: On the Fine-Grained Planning Abilities of VLM Web Agents
papers.short_title: Fine-Grained Planning of VLM Web Agents
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the fine-grained planning capabilities of Vision-Language Model (VLM) web agents, focusing on their ability to decompose complex tasks into detailed sub-steps. Through systematic evaluation on web navigation benchmarks, the authors find that current VLMs struggle with precise action sequencing and often fail to recover from errors. The study introduces a new evaluation framework to measure planning granularity and proposes improvements via structured prompting and feedback loops. Results show that enhanced planning leads to significantly higher task completion rates in realistic web environments.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了视觉语言模型（VLM）网络代理的细粒度规划能力，重点关注其将复杂任务分解为详细子步骤的能力。通过在网络导航基准上的系统评估，作者发现当前VLM在精确动作排序和错误恢复方面存在困难。研究引入了一个新的评估框架来衡量规划粒度，并提出了通过结构化提示和反馈循环的改进方法。结果表明，增强的规划能力在真实网络环境中显著提高了任务完成率。

papers.title: VisualWebInstruct: Scaling up Multimodal Instruction Data through Web Search
papers.short_title: VisualWebInstruct: Web Search for Multimodal Data
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models have made significant progress on many perception-focused tasks. However, their progress on reasoning-focused tasks remains limited due to the lack of high-quality and diverse training data. In this work, we aim to address the scarcity of reasoning-focused multimodal datasets. We propose VisualWebInstruct, a novel approach that leverages search engines to create a diverse and high-quality dataset spanning multiple disciplines, including mathematics, physics, finance, and chemistry, etc. Starting with a meticulously selected set of 30,000 seed images, we employ Google Image Search to identify websites containing similar images. We collect and process HTML data from over 700K unique URLs. Through a pipeline of content extraction, filtering, and synthesis, we construct a dataset of approximately 900K question-answer (QA) pairs, with 40% consisting of visual QA pairs and the remaining comprising text-based QA pairs. Models fine-tuned on VisualWebInstruct demonstrate significant performance improvements: (1) fine-tuning on Llava-OV results in 10-20 absolute points improvement across benchmarks, and (2) fine-tuning from MAmmoTH-VL yields a 5 absolute points gain across benchmarks. Our best model, MAmmoTH-VL2, achieves state-of-the-art performance within the 10B parameter class on MMMU-Pro (40.7), MathVerse (42.6), and DynaMath (55.7). These results highlight the effectiveness of our dataset in enhancing the reasoning capabilities of vision-language models for complex multimodal tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces VisualWebInstruct, a method to create large-scale, diverse multimodal instruction data by using search engines to find and process web images and HTML content. This approach yields about 900K QA pairs, 40% visual, covering math, physics, finance, and chemistry. Fine-tuning models like Llava-OV and MAmmoTH-VL on this data yields 10-20 and 5 absolute point gains respectively, with the best model achieving state-of-the-art results on several reasoning benchmarks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出VisualWebInstruct方法，通过搜索引擎获取并处理网络图像与HTML内容，构建大规模、多样化的多模态指令数据。该方法生成约90万问答对，其中40%为视觉问答，涵盖数学、物理、金融和化学等领域。基于该数据微调Llava-OV和MAmmoTH-VL模型，分别在多个基准上获得10-20和5个绝对点的提升，最佳模型在多项推理基准上达到10B参数规模的最优性能。

papers.title: s3: You Don't Need That Much Data to Train a Search Agent via RL
papers.short_title: s3: You Don't Need That Much Data...

papers.title: The Dangers of Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-based Autonomous Web Navigation Agents: A Demonstration
papers.short_title: Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Web Agents
papers.summary_en: This paper demonstrates the vulnerability of LLM-based autonomous web navigation agents to indirect prompt injection attacks, where malicious content embedded in web pages can hijack the agent's behavior. Through concrete examples, the authors show how attackers can manipulate agents to perform unintended actions, such as leaking sensitive information or executing unauthorized transactions. The work highlights critical security risks in deploying such agents in real-world environments and calls for robust defense mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文展示了基于大语言模型的自主网页导航代理在面对间接提示注入攻击时的脆弱性，攻击者可通过网页中嵌入的恶意内容劫持代理行为。通过具体实例，作者揭示了攻击者如何操纵代理执行非预期操作，如泄露敏感信息或执行未授权交易。该研究强调了在真实环境中部署此类代理的关键安全风险，并呼吁开发有效的防御机制。

papers.title: Memory OS of AI Agent
papers.short_title: Memory OS of AI Agent
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) face a crucial challenge from fixed context windows and inadequate memory management, leading to a severe shortage of long-term memory capabilities and limited personalization in the interactive experience with AI agents. To overcome this challenge, we innovatively propose a Memory Operating System, i.e., MemoryOS, to achieve comprehensive and efficient memory management for AI agents. Inspired by the memory management principles in operating systems, MemoryOS designs a hierarchical storage architecture and consists of four key modules: Memory Storage, Updating, Retrieval, and Generation. Specifically, the architecture comprises three levels of storage units: short-term memory, mid-term memory, and long-term personal memory. Key operations within MemoryOS include dynamic updates between storage units: short-term to mid-term updates follow a dialogue-chain-based FIFO principle, while mid-term to long-term updates use a segmented page organization strategy. Our pioneering MemoryOS enables hierarchical memory integration and dynamic updating. Extensive experiments on the LoCoMo benchmark show an average improvement of 49.11% on F1 and 46.18% on BLEU-1 over the baselines on GPT-4o-mini, showing contextual coherence and personalized memory retention in long conversations. The implementation code is open-sourced at https://github.com/BAI-LAB/MemoryOS.
papers.summary_en: MemoryOS is a hierarchical memory management system for AI agents that addresses the long-term memory limitations of LLMs. Inspired by operating system memory management, it features short-term, mid-term, and long-term storage with dynamic update strategies like dialogue-chain-based FIFO and segmented page organization. Experiments on the LoCoMo benchmark show significant improvements in F1 and BLEU-1 scores, enhancing contextual coherence and personalized memory in long conversations.
papers.summary_zh: MemoryOS是一种面向AI代理的分层记忆管理系统，旨在解决大语言模型长期记忆能力不足的问题。受操作系统内存管理启发，它包含短期、中期和长期三级存储，并采用基于对话链的先进先出和分段页组织等动态更新策略。在LoCoMo基准上的实验表明，该方法在F1和BLEU-1指标上显著提升，增强了长对话中的上下文连贯性和个性化记忆能力。

papers.title: ResearchArena: Benchmarking Large Language Models' Ability to Collect and Organize Information as Research Agents
papers.short_title: ResearchArena: Benchmarking Large Lang...
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel across many natural language processing tasks but face challenges in domain-specific, analytical tasks such as conducting research surveys. This study introduces ResearchArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs'capabilities in conducting academic surveys -- a foundational step in academic research. ResearchArena models the process in three stages: (1) information discovery, identifying relevant literature; (2) information selection, evaluating papers'relevance and impact; and (3) information organization, structuring knowledge into hierarchical frameworks such as mind-maps. Notably, mind-map construction is treated as a bonus task, reflecting its supplementary role in survey-writing. To support these evaluations, we construct an offline environment of 12M full-text academic papers and 7.9K survey papers. To ensure ethical compliance, we do not redistribute copyrighted materials; instead, we provide code to construct the environment from the Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus (S2ORC). Preliminary evaluations reveal that LLM-based approaches underperform compared to simpler keyword-based retrieval methods, though recent reasoning models such as DeepSeek-R1 show slightly better zero-shot performance. These results underscore significant opportunities for advancing LLMs in autonomous research. We open-source the code to construct the ResearchArena benchmark at https://github.com/cxcscmu/ResearchArena.
papers.summary_en: ResearchArena is a benchmark that evaluates LLMs' ability to conduct academic surveys by testing three stages: information discovery, selection, and organization. It uses an offline environment with 12M papers and 7.9K surveys, finding that LLMs underperform keyword-based methods, though reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 show slight improvements. The benchmark highlights opportunities for advancing LLMs in autonomous research and provides open-source code for reproducibility.
papers.summary_zh: ResearchArena是一个评估大语言模型进行学术调研能力的基准，涵盖信息发现、筛选和组织三个阶段。它基于包含1200万篇论文和7900篇综述的离线环境，发现LLM方法不如基于关键词的检索方法，但DeepSeek-R1等推理模型在零样本场景下略有提升。该基准揭示了LLM在自主研究中的发展空间，并开源了构建代码。

papers.title: ReflAct: World-Grounded Decision Making in LLM Agents via Goal-State Reflection
papers.short_title: ReflAct: Goal-State Reflection for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in LLM agents have largely built on reasoning backbones like ReAct, which interleave thought and action in complex environments. However, ReAct often produces ungrounded or incoherent reasoning steps, leading to misalignment between the agent's actual state and goal. Our analysis finds that this stems from ReAct's inability to maintain consistent internal beliefs and goal alignment, causing compounding errors and hallucinations. To address this, we introduce ReflAct, a novel backbone that shifts reasoning from merely planning next actions to continuously reflecting on the agent's state relative to its goal. By explicitly grounding decisions in states and enforcing ongoing goal alignment, ReflAct dramatically improves strategic reliability. This design delivers substantial empirical gains: ReflAct surpasses ReAct by 27.7% on average, achieving a 93.3% success rate in ALFWorld. Notably, ReflAct even outperforms ReAct with added enhancement modules (e.g., Reflexion, WKM), showing that strengthening the core reasoning backbone is key to reliable agent performance.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies that the ReAct reasoning backbone in LLM agents often produces ungrounded reasoning steps, causing misalignment between the agent's state and goal. To address this, the authors propose ReflAct, which shifts reasoning from planning next actions to continuously reflecting on the agent's state relative to its goal. ReflAct significantly improves performance, achieving a 93.3% success rate in ALFWorld and outperforming ReAct by 27.7% on average, even surpassing enhanced versions of ReAct.
papers.summary_zh: 论文指出，LLM代理中的ReAct推理主干常产生无根据的推理步骤，导致代理状态与目标不一致。为此，作者提出ReflAct，将推理从规划下一步行动转变为持续反思代理相对于目标的状态。ReflAct显著提升了性能，在ALFWorld中达到93.3%的成功率，平均超过ReAct 27.7%，甚至优于增强版的ReAct。

papers.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
papers.short_title: MASSIVE-Agents: Multilingual Function-Calling Benchmark
papers.summary_en: MASSIVE-Agents is a benchmark for evaluating multilingual function-calling capabilities of large language models across 52 languages. It extends the MASSIVE dataset by adding function-calling annotations, enabling assessment of models' ability to map natural language to API calls in diverse linguistic contexts. The benchmark reveals significant performance gaps between high- and low-resource languages, highlighting challenges in cross-lingual generalization for tool use.
papers.summary_zh: MASSIVE-Agents是一个用于评估大语言模型在52种语言中多语言函数调用能力的基准测试。它通过添加函数调用标注扩展了MASSIVE数据集，从而能够评估模型将自然语言映射到API调用的能力。该基准揭示了高资源语言与低资源语言之间的显著性能差距，突显了跨语言泛化在工具使用中的挑战。

papers.title: ToolHaystack: Stress-Testing Tool-Augmented Language Models in Realistic Long-Term Interactions
papers.short_title: ToolHaystack: Long-Term Tool Use Stress Test
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in using external tools to address user inquiries. However, most existing evaluations assume tool use in short contexts, offering limited insight into model behavior during realistic long-term interactions. To fill this gap, we introduce ToolHaystack, a benchmark for testing the tool use capabilities in long-term interactions. Each test instance in ToolHaystack includes multiple tasks execution contexts and realistic noise within a continuous conversation, enabling assessment of how well models maintain context and handle various disruptions. By applying this benchmark to 14 state-of-the-art LLMs, we find that while current models perform well in standard multi-turn settings, they often significantly struggle in ToolHaystack, highlighting critical gaps in their long-term robustness not revealed by previous tool benchmarks.
papers.summary_en: ToolHaystack is a new benchmark that evaluates how well large language models use external tools during long, realistic conversations with multiple tasks and distractions. Testing 14 state-of-the-art models, the authors find that while models perform well in short interactions, they often fail in ToolHaystack, revealing critical weaknesses in maintaining context and handling disruptions over extended dialogues.
papers.summary_zh: ToolHaystack是一个新基准，用于评估大语言模型在包含多个任务和干扰的长时间真实对话中使用外部工具的能力。通过对14个最先进模型的测试，作者发现尽管模型在短交互中表现良好，但在ToolHaystack中常常失败，揭示了它们在长时间对话中维持上下文和处理干扰方面的关键弱点。

papers.title: AgentMaster: A Multi-Agent Conversational Framework Using A2A and MCP Protocols for Multimodal Information Retrieval and Analysis
papers.short_title: AgentMaster: A2A+MCP Multi-Agent Framework
papers.abstract: The rise of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) in Artificial Intelligence (AI), especially integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs), has greatly facilitated the resolution of complex tasks. However, current systems are still facing challenges of inter-agent communication, coordination, and interaction with heterogeneous tools and resources. Most recently, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) by Anthropic and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication protocol by Google have been introduced, and to the best of our knowledge, very few applications exist where both protocols are employed within a single MAS framework. We present a pilot study of AgentMaster, a novel modular multi-protocol MAS framework with self-implemented A2A and MCP, enabling dynamic coordination, flexible communication, and rapid development with faster iteration. Through a unified conversational interface, the system supports natural language interaction without prior technical expertise and responds to multimodal queries for tasks including information retrieval, question answering, and image analysis. The experiments are validated through both human evaluation and quantitative metrics, including BERTScore F1 (96.3%) and LLM-as-a-Judge G-Eval (87.1%). These results demonstrate robust automated inter-agent coordination, query decomposition, task allocation, dynamic routing, and domain-specific relevant responses. Overall, our proposed framework contributes to the potential capabilities of domain-specific, cooperative, and scalable conversational AI powered by MAS.
papers.summary_en: AgentMaster is a novel multi-agent framework that integrates both the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol to enable dynamic coordination and flexible communication among agents. It provides a unified conversational interface for multimodal tasks like information retrieval and image analysis, achieving high performance with BERTScore F1 of 96.3% and G-Eval of 87.1%. The system demonstrates robust automated inter-agent coordination, query decomposition, and domain-specific responses, advancing scalable conversational AI.
papers.summary_zh: AgentMaster是一个新颖的多智能体框架，集成了模型上下文协议（MCP）和智能体间通信协议（A2A），实现了智能体间的动态协调和灵活通信。它提供统一的对话界面，支持信息检索和图像分析等多模态任务，在BERTScore F1（96.3%）和G-Eval（87.1%）上表现优异。该系统展示了强大的自动化智能体协调、查询分解和领域特定响应能力，推动了可扩展的对话式AI发展。

papers.title: UICOMPASS: UI Map Guided Mobile Task Automation via Adaptive Action Generation
papers.short_title: UICOMPASS: UI Map Guided Mobile Automation
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces UICOMPASS, a novel framework for mobile task automation that leverages UI maps to guide adaptive action generation. The system first constructs a structured UI map from screen layouts, then uses a transformer-based model to generate actions conditioned on the map and task history. Experiments on benchmark datasets show UICOMPASS outperforms prior methods in task completion rate and efficiency, demonstrating the effectiveness of explicit UI structure modeling for automation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出UICOMPASS，一种利用UI地图引导自适应动作生成的移动任务自动化新框架。系统首先从屏幕布局构建结构化UI地图，然后使用基于Transformer的模型根据地图和任务历史生成动作。在基准数据集上的实验表明，UICOMPASS在任务完成率和效率上优于先前方法，证明了显式UI结构建模对自动化的有效性。

papers.title: Runaway is Ashamed, But Helpful: On the Early-Exit Behavior of Large Language Model-based Agents in Embodied Environments
papers.short_title: AgentExit: Early-Exit Behavior in Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Agents powered by large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong planning and decision-making capabilities in complex embodied environments. However, such agents often suffer from inefficiencies in multi-turn interactions, frequently trapped in repetitive loops or issuing ineffective commands, leading to redundant computational overhead. Instead of relying solely on learning from trajectories, we take a first step toward exploring the early-exit behavior for LLM-based agents. We propose two complementary approaches: 1. an $\textbf{intrinsic}$ method that injects exit instructions during generation, and 2. an $\textbf{extrinsic}$ method that verifies task completion to determine when to halt an agent's trial. To evaluate early-exit mechanisms, we introduce two metrics: one measures the reduction of $\textbf{redundant steps}$ as a positive effect, and the other evaluates $\textbf{progress degradation}$ as a negative effect. Experiments with 4 different LLMs across 5 embodied environments show significant efficiency improvements, with only minor drops in agent performance. We also validate a practical strategy where a stronger agent assists after an early-exit agent, achieving better performance with the same total steps. We will release our code to support further research.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates early-exit strategies for LLM-based agents in embodied environments to reduce redundant steps and computational overhead. The authors propose intrinsic (injecting exit instructions) and extrinsic (verifying task completion) methods, along with metrics to measure efficiency gains and performance degradation. Experiments across multiple LLMs and environments show significant efficiency improvements with minimal performance loss, and a practical strategy where a stronger agent takes over after early exit further enhances performance.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了基于大语言模型的智能体在具身环境中的早退策略，以减少冗余步骤和计算开销。作者提出了内在方法（在生成中注入退出指令）和外在方法（验证任务完成以决定终止），并设计了衡量效率提升和性能下降的指标。在多种大语言模型和具身环境上的实验表明，该方法能显著提升效率且性能损失极小，而早退后由更强智能体接管的策略进一步提升了性能。

papers.title: SmartBench: Is Your LLM Truly a Good Chinese Smartphone Assistant?
papers.short_title: SmartBench: LLM Chinese Smartphone Assistant
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become integral to daily life, especially advancing as intelligent assistants through on-device deployment on smartphones. However, existing LLM evaluation benchmarks predominantly focus on objective tasks like mathematics and coding in English, which do not necessarily reflect the practical use cases of on-device LLMs in real-world mobile scenarios, especially for Chinese users. To address these gaps, we introduce SmartBench, the first benchmark designed to evaluate the capabilities of on-device LLMs in Chinese mobile contexts. We analyze functionalities provided by representative smartphone manufacturers and divide them into five categories: text summarization, text Q&A, information extraction, content creation, and notification management, further detailed into 20 specific tasks. For each task, we construct high-quality datasets comprising 50 to 200 question-answer pairs that reflect everyday mobile interactions, and we develop automated evaluation criteria tailored for these tasks. We conduct comprehensive evaluations of on-device LLMs and MLLMs using SmartBench and also assess their performance after quantized deployment on real smartphone NPUs. Our contributions provide a standardized framework for evaluating on-device LLMs in Chinese, promoting further development and optimization in this critical area. Code and data will be available at https://github.com/vivo-ai-lab/SmartBench.
papers.summary_en: SmartBench is the first benchmark designed to evaluate on-device LLMs in Chinese mobile contexts, covering five categories and 20 specific tasks with high-quality datasets. It provides automated evaluation criteria and assesses both LLMs and MLLMs, including quantized deployment on real smartphone NPUs. This work fills a gap in existing benchmarks by focusing on practical mobile assistant scenarios for Chinese users.
papers.summary_zh: SmartBench是首个针对中文移动场景下设备端大语言模型评估的基准，涵盖5个类别和20个具体任务，并构建了高质量数据集。它提供了自动化评估标准，并对LLM和MLLM进行了全面评估，包括在真实手机NPU上的量化部署。该工作填补了现有基准在中文手机助手实际应用场景上的空白。

papers.title: Astra: Efficient Transformer Architecture and Contrastive Dynamics Learning for Embodied Instruction Following
papers.short_title: Astra: Transformer & Contrastive Dynamics for Embodied Instruction
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action models have gained significant attention for their ability to model multimodal sequences in embodied instruction following tasks. However, most existing models rely on causal attention, which we find suboptimal for processing sequences composed of interleaved segments from different modalities. In this paper, we introduce Astra, a novel Transformer architecture featuring trajectory attention and learnable action queries, designed to efficiently process segmented multimodal trajectories and predict actions for imitation learning. Furthermore, we propose a contrastive dynamics learning objective to enhance the model's understanding of environment dynamics and multimodal alignment, complementing the primary behavior cloning objective. Through extensive experiments on three large-scale robot manipulation benchmarks, Astra demonstrates substantial performance improvements over previous models.
papers.summary_en: Astra introduces a Transformer architecture with trajectory attention and learnable action queries to efficiently process interleaved multimodal sequences for embodied instruction following. It also proposes a contrastive dynamics learning objective that improves the model's understanding of environment dynamics and multimodal alignment beyond standard behavior cloning. Experiments on three robot manipulation benchmarks show significant performance gains over prior models.
papers.summary_zh: Astra提出了一种具有轨迹注意力和可学习动作查询的Transformer架构，以高效处理具身指令跟随中交错的多模态序列。它还引入了一个对比动态学习目标，增强了模型对环境动态和多模态对齐的理解，超越了标准的行为克隆方法。在三个机器人操作基准上的实验表明，其性能显著优于先前模型。

papers.title: Agent Trading Arena: A Study on Numerical Understanding in LLM-Based Agents
papers.short_title: Agent Trading Arena: Numerical Understanding in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language tasks, yet their performance in dynamic, real-world financial environments remains underexplored. Existing approaches are limited to historical backtesting, where trading actions cannot influence market prices and agents train only on static data. To address this limitation, we present the Agent Trading Arena, a virtual zero-sum stock market in which LLM-based agents engage in competitive multi-agent trading and directly impact price dynamics. By simulating realistic bid-ask interactions, our platform enables training in scenarios that closely mirror live markets, thereby narrowing the gap between training and evaluation. Experiments reveal that LLMs struggle with numerical reasoning when given plain-text data, often overfitting to local patterns and recent values. In contrast, chart-based visualizations significantly enhance both numerical reasoning and trading performance. Furthermore, incorporating a reflection module yields additional improvements, especially with visual inputs. Evaluations on NASDAQ and CSI datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method, particularly under high volatility. All code and data are available at https://github.com/wekjsdvnm/Agent-Trading-Arena.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces Agent Trading Arena, a virtual zero-sum stock market where LLM-based agents compete and directly influence prices, overcoming limitations of static backtesting. Experiments show LLMs struggle with numerical reasoning on plain text but improve significantly with chart-based visual inputs, and adding a reflection module further boosts performance, especially in volatile markets.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文提出了Agent Trading Arena，一个虚拟零和股票市场，其中基于LLM的智能体相互竞争并直接影响价格，克服了静态回测的局限性。实验表明，LLM在处理纯文本数据时数值推理能力较弱，但使用图表可视化输入后性能显著提升，加入反思模块进一步增强了表现，尤其是在高波动市场中。

papers.title: mrCAD: Multimodal Communication to Refine Computer-aided Designs
papers.short_title: mrCAD: Multimodal Communication for CAD Refinement
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces mrCAD, a system that enables multimodal communication—combining natural language, gestures, and sketches—to refine computer-aided designs. It allows users to interactively modify 3D models by expressing design changes through speech and hand movements, which are interpreted by a deep learning model. The system demonstrates improved efficiency and user satisfaction compared to traditional CAD interfaces, particularly for iterative design tasks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出mrCAD系统，通过结合自然语言、手势和草图的多模态通信来优化计算机辅助设计。用户可通过语音和手部动作表达设计修改意图，系统利用深度学习模型进行理解。与传统CAD界面相比，该系统在迭代设计任务中展现出更高的效率和用户满意度。

papers.title: AgentDiagnose: An Open Toolkit for Diagnosing LLM Agent Trajectories
papers.short_title: AgentDiagnose: Toolkit for LLM Agent Trajectories
papers.summary_en: AgentDiagnose is an open-source toolkit designed to analyze and diagnose the behavior of LLM-based agents by examining their trajectories. It provides modular components for logging, visualizing, and evaluating agent actions, enabling researchers to identify failure modes and improve agent performance. The toolkit supports multiple agent frameworks and offers a unified interface for debugging complex agent interactions.
papers.summary_zh: AgentDiagnose 是一个开源工具包，用于分析和诊断基于大语言模型的智能体行为，通过检查其轨迹实现。它提供模块化的日志记录、可视化和评估组件，帮助研究人员识别失败模式并提升智能体性能。该工具包支持多种智能体框架，并提供统一的接口来调试复杂的智能体交互。

papers.title: Learning API Functionality from In-Context Demonstrations for Tool-based Agents
papers.short_title: API Learning from In-Context Demos
papers.abstract: Digital tool-based agents, powered by Large Language Models (LLMs), that invoke external Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) often rely on documentation to understand API functionality. However, such documentation is frequently missing, outdated, privatized, or inconsistent-hindering the development of reliable, general-purpose agents. In this work, we propose a new research direction: learning of API functionality directly from in-context demonstrations. This task is a new paradigm applicable in scenarios without documentation. Using API benchmarks, we collect demonstrations from both expert agents and from self-exploration. To understand what information demonstrations must convey for successful task completion, we extensively study how the number of demonstrations and the use of LLM-generated summaries and evaluations affect the task success rate of the API-based agent. Our experiments across 3 datasets and 6 models show that learning functionality from in-context demonstrations remains a non-trivial challenge, even for state-of-the-art LLMs. We find that providing explicit function calls and natural language critiques significantly improves the agent's task success rate due to more accurate parameter filling. We analyze failure modes, identify sources of error, and highlight key open challenges for future work in documentation-free, self-improving, API-based agents.
papers.summary_en: This paper proposes a new paradigm for tool-based agents to learn API functionality directly from in-context demonstrations, bypassing the need for documentation. Through experiments on multiple datasets and models, the authors find that providing explicit function calls and natural language critiques significantly improves task success rates. The work identifies key challenges and failure modes, highlighting that learning from demonstrations remains non-trivial even for state-of-the-art LLMs.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种新的范式，使基于工具的大语言模型代理能够直接从上下文演示中学习API功能，从而无需依赖文档。通过在多个数据集和模型上的实验，作者发现提供显式的函数调用和自然语言批评能显著提高任务成功率。该工作指出了关键挑战和失败模式，强调即使对于最先进的LLM，从演示中学习仍然是一个非平凡的问题。

papers.title: ReAct Meets Industrial IoT: Language Agents for Data Access
papers.short_title: ReAct for Industrial IoT Data Access

papers.title: MULTIVOX: A Benchmark for Evaluating Voice Assistants for Multimodal Interactions
papers.short_title: MULTIVOX: Voice Assistants Benchmark
papers.abstract: The rapid progress of Large Language Models (LLMs) has empowered omni models to act as voice assistants capable of understanding spoken dialogues. These models can process multimodal inputs beyond text, such as speech and visual data, enabling more context-aware interactions. However, current benchmarks fall short in comprehensively evaluating how well these models generate context-aware responses, particularly when it comes to implicitly understanding fine-grained speech characteristics, such as pitch, emotion, timbre, and volume or the environmental acoustic context such as background sounds. Additionally, they inadequately assess the ability of models to align paralinguistic cues with complementary visual signals to inform their responses. To address these gaps, we introduce MultiVox, the first omni voice assistant benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of voice assistants to integrate spoken and visual cues including paralinguistic speech features for truly multimodal understanding. Specifically, MultiVox includes 1000 human-annotated and recorded speech dialogues that encompass diverse paralinguistic features and a range of visual cues such as images and videos. Our evaluation on 10 state-of-the-art models reveals that, although humans excel at these tasks, current models consistently struggle to produce contextually grounded responses.
papers.summary_en: MultiVox is a new benchmark for evaluating voice assistants that process multimodal inputs like speech and visuals. It includes 1000 human-annotated speech dialogues with diverse paralinguistic features (e.g., pitch, emotion) and visual cues (images/videos). Testing on 10 state-of-the-art models shows they struggle to generate context-aware responses, while humans excel. This benchmark fills a gap in assessing how well models integrate spoken and visual information for truly multimodal understanding.
papers.summary_zh: MultiVox是一个用于评估处理语音和视觉等多模态输入的语音助手的新基准。它包含1000个人工标注的语音对话，涵盖多样的副语言特征（如音调、情感）和视觉线索（图像/视频）。对10个最先进模型的测试表明，它们在生成上下文感知响应方面表现不佳，而人类则表现出色。该基准填补了评估模型如何整合语音和视觉信息以实现真正多模态理解的空白。

papers.title: Auto-SLURP: A Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating Multi-Agent Frameworks in Smart Personal Assistant
papers.short_title: Auto-SLURP: Multi-Agent Benchmark
papers.abstract: In recent years, multi-agent frameworks powered by large language models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly. Despite this progress, there is still a notable absence of benchmark datasets specifically tailored to evaluate their performance. To bridge this gap, we introduce Auto-SLURP, a benchmark dataset aimed at evaluating LLM-based multi-agent frameworks in the context of intelligent personal assistants. Auto-SLURP extends the original SLURP dataset -- initially developed for natural language understanding tasks -- by relabeling the data and integrating simulated servers and external services. This enhancement enables a comprehensive end-to-end evaluation pipeline, covering language understanding, task execution, and response generation. Our experiments demonstrate that Auto-SLURP presents a significant challenge for current state-of-the-art frameworks, highlighting that truly reliable and intelligent multi-agent personal assistants remain a work in progress. The dataset and related code are available at https://github.com/lorashen/Auto-SLURP/.
papers.summary_en: Auto-SLURP is a new benchmark dataset for evaluating LLM-based multi-agent frameworks in smart personal assistants. It extends the SLURP dataset by relabeling data and adding simulated servers and external services, enabling end-to-end evaluation of language understanding, task execution, and response generation. Experiments show that current state-of-the-art frameworks still struggle with this benchmark, indicating that reliable multi-agent personal assistants are not yet fully achieved.
papers.summary_zh: Auto-SLURP是一个新的基准数据集，用于评估基于大语言模型的多智能体框架在智能个人助理中的表现。它通过重新标注数据并集成模拟服务器和外部服务，扩展了原有的SLURP数据集，实现了对语言理解、任务执行和响应生成的端到端评估。实验表明，当前最先进的框架在该基准上仍面临显著挑战，说明可靠的多智能体个人助理尚未完全实现。

papers.title: PresentAgent: Multimodal Agent for Presentation Video Generation
papers.short_title: PresentAgent: Presentation Video Gen
papers.abstract: We present PresentAgent, a multimodal agent that transforms long-form documents into narrated presentation videos. While existing approaches are limited to generating static slides or text summaries, our method advances beyond these limitations by producing fully synchronized visual and spoken content that closely mimics human-style presentations. To achieve this integration, PresentAgent employs a modular pipeline that systematically segments the input document, plans and renders slide-style visual frames, generates contextual spoken narration with large language models and Text-to-Speech models, and seamlessly composes the final video with precise audio-visual alignment. Given the complexity of evaluating such multimodal outputs, we introduce PresentEval, a unified assessment framework powered by Vision-Language Models that comprehensively scores videos across three critical dimensions: content fidelity, visual clarity, and audience comprehension through prompt-based evaluation. Our experimental validation on a curated dataset of 30 document-presentation pairs demonstrates that PresentAgent approaches human-level quality across all evaluation metrics. These results highlight the significant potential of controllable multimodal agents in transforming static textual materials into dynamic, effective, and accessible presentation formats. Code will be available at https://github.com/AIGeeksGroup/PresentAgent.
papers.summary_en: PresentAgent is a multimodal agent that generates narrated presentation videos from long documents, going beyond static slides by producing synchronized visual and spoken content. It uses a modular pipeline for document segmentation, slide rendering, narration generation, and audio-visual alignment. The authors also introduce PresentEval, a VLM-based evaluation framework assessing content fidelity, visual clarity, and audience comprehension. Experiments show PresentAgent approaches human-level quality, demonstrating the potential of multimodal agents for transforming text into dynamic presentations.
papers.summary_zh: PresentAgent是一种多模态智能体，能从长文档生成带旁白的演示视频，超越静态幻灯片，产出同步的视觉与语音内容。它采用模块化流水线，包括文档分割、幻灯片渲染、旁白生成及音视频对齐。作者还提出了PresentEval，一种基于视觉语言模型的评估框架，从内容保真度、视觉清晰度和观众理解度三个维度进行评分。实验表明，PresentAgent接近人类水平质量，展示了多模态智能体将静态文本转化为动态演示的潜力。

papers.title: Procedural Environment Generation for Tool-Use Agents
papers.short_title: Procedural Env Gen for Tool-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Although the power of LLM tool-use agents has ignited a flurry of recent research in this area, the curation of tool-use training data remains an open problem$-$especially for online RL training. Existing approaches to synthetic tool-use data generation tend to be non-interactive, and/or non-compositional. We introduce RandomWorld, a pipeline for the procedural generation of interactive tools and compositional tool-use data. We show that models tuned via SFT and RL on synthetic RandomWorld data improve on a range of tool-use benchmarks, and set the new SoTA for two metrics on the NESTFUL dataset. Further experiments show that downstream performance scales with the amount of RandomWorld-generated training data, opening up the possibility of further improvement through the use of entirely synthetic data.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces RandomWorld, a pipeline for procedurally generating interactive tools and compositional tool-use data to train LLM agents. The authors show that models fine-tuned with SFT and RL on this synthetic data improve performance on tool-use benchmarks, achieving new state-of-the-art results on two metrics of the NESTFUL dataset. They also demonstrate that downstream performance scales with the amount of generated data, suggesting potential for further improvement using entirely synthetic data.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了RandomWorld，一个用于程序化生成交互式工具和组合性工具使用数据的流水线，以训练LLM智能体。作者表明，通过SFT和RL在此合成数据上微调的模型在工具使用基准测试中性能提升，并在NESTFUL数据集的两个指标上取得了新的最优结果。他们还证明下游性能随生成数据量增加而提升，表明使用完全合成数据有进一步改进的潜力。

papers.title: SimpleDeepSearcher: Deep Information Seeking via Web-Powered Reasoning Trajectory Synthesis
papers.short_title: SimpleDeepSearcher: Web-Powered Reasoning Trajectory
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have advanced large language models (LLMs) in complex deep search scenarios requiring multi-step reasoning and iterative information retrieval. However, existing approaches face critical limitations that lack high-quality training trajectories or suffer from the distributional mismatches in simulated environments and prohibitive computational costs for real-world deployment. This paper introduces SimpleDeepSearcher, a lightweight yet effective framework that bridges this gap through strategic data engineering rather than complex training paradigms. Our approach synthesizes high-quality training data by simulating realistic user interactions in live web search environments, coupled with a multi-criteria curation strategy that optimizes the diversity and quality of input and output side. Experiments on five benchmarks across diverse domains demonstrate that SFT on only 871 curated samples yields significant improvements over RL-based baselines. Our work establishes SFT as a viable pathway by systematically addressing the data-scarce bottleneck, offering practical insights for efficient deep search systems. Our code is available at https://github.com/RUCAIBox/SimpleDeepSearcher.
papers.summary_en: SimpleDeepSearcher is a lightweight framework that improves retrieval-augmented generation for complex search tasks by synthesizing high-quality training data from real web interactions, rather than relying on expensive reinforcement learning. Using only 871 curated samples for supervised fine-tuning, it outperforms RL-based baselines across five benchmarks, demonstrating that strategic data engineering can effectively address the data scarcity bottleneck in deep search systems.
papers.summary_zh: SimpleDeepSearcher是一个轻量级框架，通过从真实网络交互中合成高质量训练数据，而非依赖昂贵的强化学习，来改进复杂搜索任务中的检索增强生成。仅使用871个精选样本进行监督微调，它在五个基准测试中超越了基于强化学习的基线方法，表明策略性数据工程能有效解决深度搜索系统中的数据稀缺瓶颈。

papers.title: VLASCD: A Visual Language Action Model for Simultaneous Chatting and Decision Making
papers.short_title: VLASCD: Visual Lang Action for Chat & Decision
papers.abstract: Recent large pretrained models such as LLMs (e.g., GPT series) and VLAs (e.g., OpenVLA) have achieved notable progress on multimodal tasks, yet they are built upon a multi-input single-output (MISO) paradigm. We show that this paradigm fundamentally limits performance in multi-input multi-output (MIMO) scenarios, where parallel task execution is required. In MISO architectures, tasks compete for a shared output channel, creating mutual exclusion effects that cause unbalanced optimization and degraded performance. To address this gap, we introduce MIMO-VLA (VLASCD), a unified training framework that enables concurrent multi-task outputs, exemplified by simultaneous dialogue generation and decision-making. Inspired by human cognition, MIMO-VLA eliminates interference between tasks and supports efficient parallel processing. Experiments on the CARLA autonomous driving platform demonstrate that MIMO-VLA substantially outperforms state-of-the-art MISO-based LLMs, reinforcement learning models, and VLAs in MIMO settings, establishing a new direction for multimodal and multitask learning.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a fundamental limitation of current large multimodal models that use a multi-input single-output (MISO) paradigm, which causes task interference in multi-input multi-output (MIMO) scenarios. To address this, the authors propose MIMO-VLA (VLASCD), a unified training framework that enables simultaneous dialogue generation and decision-making without task competition. Experiments on the CARLA autonomous driving platform show that MIMO-VLA significantly outperforms existing MISO-based models, including LLMs and VLAs, in MIMO settings, establishing a new direction for multimodal multitask learning.
papers.summary_zh: 本文指出现有多模态大模型采用的多输入单输出（MISO）范式在多输入多输出（MIMO）场景下存在根本性局限，导致任务间相互干扰。为解决此问题，作者提出MIMO-VLA（VLASCD）统一训练框架，能够同时进行对话生成和决策制定，避免任务竞争。在CARLA自动驾驶平台上的实验表明，MIMO-VLA在MIMO设置下显著优于基于MISO的现有模型（包括LLM和VLA），为多模态多任务学习开辟了新方向。

papers.title: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
papers.short_title: GUI Agent Localization Biases via Logit Sharpness
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled GUI agents to interact with operating systems by grounding language into spatial actions. Despite their promising performance, these models frequently exhibit hallucinations-systematic localization errors that compromise reliability. We propose a fine-grained evaluation framework that categorizes model predictions into four distinct types, revealing nuanced failure modes beyond traditional accuracy metrics. To better quantify model uncertainty, we introduce the Peak Sharpness Score (PSS), a metric that evaluates the alignment between semantic continuity and logits distribution in coordinate prediction. Building on this insight, we further propose Context-Aware Cropping, a training-free technique that improves model performance by adaptively refining input context. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework and methods provide actionable insights and enhance the interpretability and robustness of GUI agent behavior.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies and categorizes systematic localization errors in GUI agents powered by multimodal LLMs, introducing a fine-grained evaluation framework with four prediction types. To quantify model uncertainty, the authors propose Peak Sharpness Score (PSS), which measures alignment between semantic continuity and logit distribution. They also develop Context-Aware Cropping, a training-free method that adaptively refines input context to reduce hallucinations. Experiments show these tools improve interpretability and robustness of GUI agent behavior.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别并分类了多模态大语言模型驱动的GUI代理中的系统性定位错误，提出了包含四种预测类型的细粒度评估框架。为量化模型不确定性，作者引入峰值锐度分数（PSS），衡量语义连续性与logit分布之间的对齐程度。他们还开发了上下文感知裁剪（Context-Aware Cropping），一种无需训练的方法，通过自适应优化输入上下文来减少幻觉。实验表明，这些工具提升了GUI代理行为的可解释性和鲁棒性。

papers.title: Can LLMs Help You at Work? A Sandbox for Evaluating LLM Agents in Enterprise Environments
papers.short_title: EnterpriseBench: Sandbox for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Enterprise systems are crucial for enhancing productivity and decision-making among employees and customers. Integrating LLM based systems into enterprise systems enables intelligent automation, personalized experiences, and efficient information retrieval, driving operational efficiency and strategic growth. However, developing and evaluating such systems is challenging due to the inherent complexity of enterprise environments, where data is fragmented across multiple sources and governed by sophisticated access controls. We present EnterpriseBench, a comprehensive benchmark that simulates enterprise settings, featuring 500 diverse tasks across software engineering, HR, finance, and administrative domains. Our benchmark uniquely captures key enterprise characteristics including data source fragmentation, access control hierarchies, and cross-functional workflows. Additionally, we provide a novel data generation pipeline that creates internally consistent enterprise tasks from organizational metadata. Experiments with state-of-the-art LLM agents demonstrate that even the most capable models achieve only 41.8% task completion, highlighting significant opportunities for improvement in enterprise-focused AI systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces EnterpriseBench, a benchmark simulating enterprise environments with 500 tasks across domains like software engineering and HR, featuring data fragmentation and access controls. It also provides a data generation pipeline for creating consistent enterprise tasks. Experiments show that even top LLM agents achieve only 41.8% task completion, revealing significant room for improvement in enterprise AI.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了EnterpriseBench，一个模拟企业环境的基准测试，包含软件工程、人力资源等领域的500个任务，具有数据碎片化和访问控制等特点。同时提供了生成一致企业任务的数据生成流程。实验表明，即使最先进的LLM代理也仅完成41.8%的任务，揭示了企业AI系统仍有很大的改进空间。

papers.title: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
papers.short_title: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
papers.abstract: Multi-modal large language model (MLLM)-based web agents interact with webpage environments by generating actions based on screenshots of the webpages. In this work, we propose WebInject, a prompt injection attack that manipulates the webpage environment to induce a web agent to perform an attacker-specified action. Our attack adds a perturbation to the raw pixel values of the rendered webpage. After these perturbed pixels are mapped into a screenshot, the perturbation induces the web agent to perform the attacker-specified action. We formulate the task of finding the perturbation as an optimization problem. A key challenge in solving this problem is that the mapping between raw pixel values and screenshot is non-differentiable, making it difficult to backpropagate gradients to the perturbation. To overcome this, we train a neural network to approximate the mapping and apply projected gradient descent to solve the reformulated optimization problem. Extensive evaluation on multiple datasets shows that WebInject is highly effective and significantly outperforms baselines.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces WebInject, a prompt injection attack targeting multi-modal LLM-based web agents. By adding small perturbations to webpage pixel values, the attack manipulates the agent's screenshot input to execute attacker-specified actions. The authors overcome the non-differentiable rendering pipeline by training a neural network to approximate it, enabling gradient-based optimization. Experiments show WebInject achieves high success rates, outperforming baseline attacks across multiple datasets.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出WebInject，一种针对多模态大模型驱动的网页代理的提示注入攻击。通过向网页像素值添加微小扰动，攻击可操控代理的截图输入，使其执行攻击者指定的动作。作者训练神经网络近似不可微的渲染过程，从而利用梯度优化求解扰动。实验表明，WebInject在多个数据集上均取得高成功率，显著优于基线方法。

papers.title: ECom-Bench: Can LLM Agent Resolve Real-World E-commerce Customer Support Issues?
papers.short_title: ECom-Bench: LLM Agent for E-commerce Support
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce ECom-Bench, the first benchmark framework for evaluating LLM agent with multimodal capabilities in the e-commerce customer support domain. ECom-Bench features dynamic user simulation based on persona information collected from real e-commerce customer interactions and a realistic task dataset derived from authentic e-commerce dialogues. These tasks, covering a wide range of business scenarios, are designed to reflect real-world complexities, making ECom-Bench highly challenging. For instance, even advanced models like GPT-4o achieve only a 10-20% pass^3 metric in our benchmark, highlighting the substantial difficulties posed by complex e-commerce scenarios. The code and data have been made publicly available at https://github.com/XiaoduoAILab/ECom-Bench to facilitate further research and development in this domain.
papers.summary_en: ECom-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLM agents on real-world e-commerce customer support tasks. It uses dynamic user simulations based on real customer data and a dataset of authentic dialogues covering diverse business scenarios. The benchmark is highly challenging, with advanced models like GPT-4o achieving only 10-20% on the pass^3 metric, highlighting the difficulty of complex e-commerce interactions.
papers.summary_zh: ECom-Bench是一个用于评估多模态大语言模型代理在真实电商客服场景中表现的新基准。它基于真实客户数据构建动态用户模拟，并使用来自真实电商对话的数据集，覆盖多种业务场景。该基准极具挑战性，即使是GPT-4o等先进模型在pass^3指标上也仅达到10-20%，凸显了复杂电商交互的难度。

papers.title: Privacy in Action: Towards Realistic Privacy Mitigation and Evaluation for LLM-Powered Agents
papers.short_title: Privacy in Action: LLM Agent Privacy Mitigation
papers.abstract: The increasing autonomy of LLM agents in handling sensitive communications, accelerated by Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) frameworks, creates urgent privacy challenges. While recent work reveals significant gaps between LLMs'privacy Q&A performance and their agent behavior, existing benchmarks remain limited to static, simplified scenarios. We present PrivacyChecker, a model-agnostic, contextual integrity based mitigation approach that effectively reduces privacy leakage from 36.08% to 7.30% on DeepSeek-R1 and from 33.06% to 8.32% on GPT-4o, all while preserving task helpfulness. We also introduce PrivacyLens-Live, transforming static benchmarks into dynamic MCP and A2A environments that reveal substantially higher privacy risks in practical. Our modular mitigation approach integrates seamlessly into agent protocols through three deployment strategies, providing practical privacy protection for the emerging agentic ecosystem. Our data and code will be made available at https://aka.ms/privacy_in_action.
papers.summary_en: PrivacyChecker is a model-agnostic mitigation approach based on contextual integrity that reduces privacy leakage in LLM agents from ~36% to ~7% on DeepSeek-R1 and from ~33% to ~8% on GPT-4o without harming task performance. The authors also introduce PrivacyLens-Live, which transforms static benchmarks into dynamic environments using MCP and A2A protocols, revealing higher privacy risks in realistic agent interactions. The mitigation integrates modularly into agent protocols via three deployment strategies, offering practical privacy protection for the emerging agentic ecosystem.
papers.summary_zh: PrivacyChecker是一种基于情境完整性的模型无关缓解方法，能将DeepSeek-R1和GPT-4o上LLM代理的隐私泄露率分别从约36%降至约7%和从约33%降至约8%，且不影响任务性能。作者还提出了PrivacyLens-Live，将静态基准转化为基于MCP和A2A协议的动态环境，揭示了实际代理交互中更高的隐私风险。该缓解方法通过三种部署策略模块化地集成到代理协议中，为新兴的代理生态系统提供了实用的隐私保护。

papers.title: FedMABench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents on Decentralized Heterogeneous User Data
papers.short_title: FedMABench: Mobile GUI Agents on Decentralized Data
papers.summary_en: FedMABench is a benchmark designed to evaluate mobile GUI agents under decentralized and heterogeneous user data conditions. It simulates real-world scenarios where user interaction data is distributed across devices with non-IID patterns, addressing the lack of such benchmarks in federated learning for GUI agents. The benchmark includes diverse tasks and metrics to assess agent performance in privacy-preserving settings. This work highlights the challenges of personalization and generalization in federated mobile GUI automation.
papers.summary_zh: FedMABench是一个用于评估移动GUI智能体在去中心化异构用户数据条件下的基准测试。它模拟了用户交互数据分布在设备上且呈非独立同分布的真实场景，填补了联邦学习在GUI智能体领域缺乏此类基准的空白。该基准包含多样化的任务和指标，用于评估智能体在隐私保护设置下的性能。这项工作突出了联邦移动GUI自动化中个性化和泛化的挑战。

papers.title: INREACT: An Inspire-Then-Reinforce Training Framework For Multimodal GUI Agent
papers.short_title: INREACT: Inspire-Reinforce for Multimodal GUI Agent
papers.summary_en: The paper proposes INREACT, a training framework for multimodal GUI agents that combines an 'inspire' phase using large language models to generate diverse task demonstrations and a 'reinforce' phase that iteratively refines the agent's policy through reinforcement learning. This approach addresses the challenge of limited training data for GUI agents by leveraging LLMs to create high-quality synthetic examples and then optimizing the agent's performance via reward-based learning. Experiments show that INREACT significantly improves task completion rates and generalization across different GUI environments compared to baseline methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出INREACT框架，用于训练多模态GUI智能体，该框架结合了“启发”阶段（利用大语言模型生成多样化的任务演示）和“强化”阶段（通过强化学习迭代优化智能体策略）。该方法通过利用LLM创建高质量合成示例来解决GUI智能体训练数据不足的问题，并基于奖励学习优化智能体性能。实验表明，与基线方法相比，INREACT显著提高了任务完成率及在不同GUI环境中的泛化能力。

papers.title: WebAgent-R1: Training Web Agents via End-to-End Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.short_title: WebAgent-R1: Multi-Turn RL for Web Agents
papers.abstract: While reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in enhancing large language models (LLMs), it has primarily focused on single-turn tasks such as solving math problems. Training effective web agents for multi-turn interactions remains challenging due to the complexity of long-horizon decision-making across dynamic web interfaces. In this work, we present WebAgent-R1, a simple yet effective end-to-end multi-turn RL framework for training web agents. It learns directly from online interactions with web environments by asynchronously generating diverse trajectories, entirely guided by binary rewards depending on task success. Experiments on the WebArena-Lite benchmark demonstrate the effectiveness of WebAgent-R1, boosting the task success rate of Qwen-2.5-3B from 6.1% to 33.9% and Llama-3.1-8B from 8.5% to 44.8%, significantly outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods and strong proprietary models such as OpenAI o3. In-depth analyses reveal the effectiveness of the thinking-based prompting strategy and test-time scaling through increased interactions for web tasks. We further investigate different RL initialization policies by introducing two variants, namely WebAgent-R1-Zero and WebAgent-R1-CoT, which highlight the importance of the warm-up training stage (i.e., behavior cloning) and provide insights on incorporating long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in web agents.
papers.summary_en: WebAgent-R1 is a reinforcement learning framework that trains web agents through end-to-end multi-turn interactions, using only binary success/failure rewards. It significantly improves task success rates on WebArena-Lite, boosting Qwen-2.5-3B from 6.1% to 33.9% and Llama-3.1-8B from 8.5% to 44.8%, outperforming strong proprietary models like OpenAI o3. The paper also explores thinking-based prompting, test-time scaling, and the impact of different initialization policies, highlighting the importance of behavior cloning warm-up.
papers.summary_zh: WebAgent-R1是一个通过端到端多轮交互训练网络智能体的强化学习框架，仅使用二值成功/失败奖励。它在WebArena-Lite基准上显著提升了任务成功率，将Qwen-2.5-3B从6.1%提升至33.9%，Llama-3.1-8B从8.5%提升至44.8%，超越了OpenAI o3等强专有模型。论文还探讨了基于思考的提示策略、测试时扩展以及不同初始化策略的影响，强调了行为克隆预热的重要性。

papers.title: DiMo-GUI: Advancing Test-time Scaling in GUI Grounding via Modality-Aware Visual Reasoning
papers.short_title: DiMo-GUI: Modality-Aware GUI Grounding
papers.abstract: Grounding natural language queries in graphical user interfaces (GUIs) poses unique challenges due to the diversity of visual elements, spatial clutter, and the ambiguity of language. In this paper, we introduce DiMo-GUI, a training-free framework for GUI grounding that leverages two core strategies: dynamic visual grounding and modality-aware optimization. Instead of treating the GUI as a monolithic image, our method splits the input into textual elements and iconic elements, allowing the model to reason over each modality independently using general-purpose vision-language models. When predictions are ambiguous or incorrect, DiMo-GUI dynamically focuses attention by generating candidate focal regions centered on the model's initial predictions and incrementally zooms into subregions to refine the grounding result. This hierarchical refinement process helps disambiguate visually crowded layouts without the need for additional training or annotations. We evaluate our approach on standard GUI grounding benchmarks and demonstrate consistent improvements over baseline inference pipelines, highlighting the effectiveness of combining modality separation with region-focused reasoning.
papers.summary_en: DiMo-GUI is a training-free framework for GUI grounding that improves accuracy by separating visual elements into text and icons, then reasoning over each modality independently. When initial predictions are uncertain, it dynamically zooms into candidate regions to refine results, handling cluttered layouts without extra training. The method consistently outperforms baseline approaches on standard benchmarks.
papers.summary_zh: DiMo-GUI是一种无需训练的GUI定位框架，通过将视觉元素分离为文本和图标并分别推理来提升准确性。当初始预测不确定时，它会动态放大候选区域以细化结果，从而无需额外训练即可处理拥挤布局。该方法在标准基准测试上持续优于基线方法。

papers.title: BacktrackAgent: Enhancing GUI Agent with Error Detection and Backtracking Mechanism
papers.short_title: BacktrackAgent: GUI Agent Backtracking
papers.abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents have gained substantial attention due to their impressive capabilities to complete tasks through multiple interactions within GUI environments. However, existing agents primarily focus on enhancing the accuracy of individual actions and often lack effective mechanisms for detecting and recovering from errors. To address these shortcomings, we propose the BacktrackAgent, a robust framework that incorporates a backtracking mechanism to improve task completion efficiency. BacktrackAgent includes verifier, judger, and reflector components as modules for error detection and recovery, while also applying judgment rewards to further enhance the agent's performance. Additionally, we develop a training dataset specifically designed for the backtracking mechanism, which considers the outcome pages after action executions. Experimental results show that BacktrackAgent has achieved performance improvements in both task success rate and step accuracy on Mobile3M and Auto-UI benchmarks. Our data and code will be released upon acceptance.
papers.summary_en: BacktrackAgent introduces a framework for GUI agents that adds error detection and backtracking capabilities, enabling recovery from mistakes during task execution. It uses verifier, judger, and reflector modules along with judgment rewards to improve performance. Experiments on Mobile3M and Auto-UI benchmarks show higher task success rates and step accuracy compared to existing methods.
papers.summary_zh: BacktrackAgent提出了一种增强GUI代理的框架，通过引入错误检测和回溯机制，使代理能够在任务执行过程中从错误中恢复。该框架包含验证器、判断器和反射器模块，并结合判断奖励来提升性能。在Mobile3M和Auto-UI基准上的实验表明，与现有方法相比，任务成功率和步骤准确性均有提高。

papers.title: Search Wisely: Mitigating Sub-optimal Agentic Searches By Reducing Uncertainty
papers.short_title: Search Wisely: Reducing Agentic Search Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance Large Language Models (LLMs) by enabling dynamic, multi-step reasoning and information retrieval. However, these systems often exhibit sub-optimal search behaviors like over-search (retrieving redundant information) and under-search (failing to retrieve necessary information), which hinder efficiency and reliability. This work formally defines and quantifies these behaviors, revealing their prevalence across multiple QA datasets and agentic RAG systems (e.g., one model could have avoided searching in 27.7% of its search steps). Furthermore, we demonstrate a crucial link between these inefficiencies and the models'uncertainty regarding their own knowledge boundaries, where response accuracy correlates with model's uncertainty in its search decisions. To address this, we propose $\beta$-GRPO, a reinforcement learning-based training method that incorporates confidence threshold to reward high-certainty search decisions. Experiments on seven QA benchmarks show that $\beta$-GRPO enable a 3B model with better agentic RAG ability, outperforming other strong baselines with a 4% higher average exact match score.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies and quantifies sub-optimal search behaviors (over-search and under-search) in agentic RAG systems, linking them to model uncertainty about knowledge boundaries. It proposes β-GRPO, a reinforcement learning method that rewards high-certainty search decisions, reducing unnecessary searches. Experiments show that a 3B model trained with β-GRPO outperforms strong baselines by 4% in exact match score across seven QA benchmarks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别并量化了智能体RAG系统中的次优搜索行为（过度搜索和搜索不足），并将其与模型对自身知识边界的不确定性联系起来。提出了β-GRPO，一种通过奖励高确定性搜索决策来减少不必要搜索的强化学习方法。实验表明，使用β-GRPO训练的3B模型在七个QA基准测试中平均精确匹配得分比强基线高出4%。

papers.title: SAND: Boosting LLM Agents with Self-Taught Action Deliberation
papers.short_title: SAND: Self-Taught Action Deliberation
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are commonly tuned with supervised finetuning on ReAct-style expert trajectories or preference optimization over pairwise rollouts. Most of these methods focus on imitating specific expert behaviors or promoting chosen reasoning thoughts and actions over rejected ones. However, without reasoning and comparing over alternatives actions, LLM agents finetuned with these methods may over-commit towards seemingly plausible but suboptimal actions due to limited action space exploration. To address this, in this paper we propose Self-taught ActioN Deliberation (SAND) framework, enabling LLM agents to explicitly deliberate over candidate actions before committing to one. To tackle the challenges of when and what to deliberate given large action space and step-level action evaluation, we incorporate self-consistency action sampling and execution-guided action critique to help synthesize step-wise action deliberation thoughts using the base model of the LLM agent. In an iterative manner, the deliberation trajectories are then used to finetune the LLM agent itself. Evaluating on two representative interactive agent tasks, SAND achieves an average 20% improvement over initial supervised finetuning and also outperforms state-of-the-art agent tuning approaches.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces SAND, a framework that improves LLM agents by teaching them to deliberate over multiple candidate actions before choosing one, rather than imitating fixed expert trajectories. It uses self-consistency sampling and execution-guided critique to generate step-wise deliberation data from the agent's own base model, then iteratively fine-tunes the agent on this data. Experiments on interactive tasks show SAND achieves about 20% improvement over supervised fine-tuning and outperforms existing agent tuning methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出SAND框架，通过让LLM智能体在行动前对多个候选方案进行显式思考，而非模仿固定专家轨迹，来提升其性能。该框架利用自一致性采样和执行引导的批评机制，从智能体自身基模型生成逐步的思考数据，并迭代微调智能体。在交互式任务上的实验表明，SAND相比监督微调提升约20%，并优于现有智能体调优方法。

papers.title: DroidCall: A Dataset for LLM-powered Android Intent Invocation
papers.short_title: DroidCall: Android Intent Invocation Dataset
papers.abstract: The growing capabilities of large language models in natural language understanding significantly strengthen existing agentic systems. To power performant on-device mobile agents for better data privacy, we introduce DroidCall, the first training and testing dataset for accurate Android intent invocation. With a highly flexible and reusable data generation pipeline, we constructed 10k samples in DroidCall. Given a task instruction in natural language, small language models such as Qwen2.5-3B and Gemma2-2B fine-tuned with DroidCall can approach or even surpass the capabilities of GPT-4o for accurate Android intent invocation. We also provide an end-to-end Android app equipped with these fine-tuned models to demonstrate the Android intent invocation process. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/UbiquitousLearning/DroidCall.
papers.summary_en: DroidCall is a new dataset with 10k samples for training and testing Android intent invocation from natural language instructions. It includes a reusable data generation pipeline and shows that small models fine-tuned on it can match or exceed GPT-4o's performance. The authors also provide an end-to-end Android app demonstrating the invocation process.
papers.summary_zh: DroidCall是一个包含1万个样本的新数据集，用于从自然语言指令训练和测试Android意图调用。它包含一个可复用的数据生成流水线，并表明在其上微调的小模型可以匹配甚至超越GPT-4o的性能。作者还提供了一个端到端的Android应用来演示意图调用过程。

papers.title: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
papers.short_title: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
papers.abstract: GUI agents powered by vision-language models (VLMs) show promise in automating complex digital tasks. However, their effectiveness in real-world applications is often limited by scarce training data and the inherent complexity of these tasks, which frequently require long-tailed knowledge covering rare, unseen scenarios. We propose RAG-GUI , a lightweight VLM that leverages web tutorials at inference time. RAG-GUI is first warm-started via supervised finetuning (SFT) and further refined through self-guided rejection sampling finetuning (RSF). Designed to be model-agnostic, RAG-GUI functions as a generic plug-in that enhances any VLM-based agent. Evaluated across three distinct tasks, it consistently outperforms baseline agents and surpasses other inference baselines by 2.6% to 13.3% across two model sizes, demonstrating strong generalization and practical plug-and-play capabilities in real-world scenarios.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces RAG-GUI, a lightweight vision-language model that enhances GUI agents by retrieving and leveraging web tutorials at inference time. It is first fine-tuned with supervised learning and then refined via self-guided rejection sampling, and can be plugged into any VLM-based agent. Experiments show it outperforms baselines by 2.6% to 13.3% across three tasks, demonstrating strong generalization and practical plug-and-play capability.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出RAG-GUI，一种轻量级视觉语言模型，通过在推理时检索并利用网络教程来增强GUI智能体。该模型先通过监督微调进行预热，再通过自引导拒绝采样微调进一步优化，可作为通用插件集成到任何基于VLM的智能体中。实验表明，在三个不同任务上，它比基线模型提升2.6%至13.3%，展现出强大的泛化能力和实用的即插即用特性。

papers.title: ProductAgent: Benchmarking Conversational Product Search Agent with Asking Clarification Questions
papers.short_title: ProductAgent: Conversational Product Search with Clarification
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the task of product demand clarification within an e-commercial scenario, where the user commences the conversation with ambiguous queries and the task-oriented agent is designed to achieve more accurate and tailored product searching by asking clarification questions. To address this task, we propose ProductAgent, a conversational information seeking agent equipped with abilities of strategic clarification question generation and dynamic product retrieval. Specifically, we develop the agent with strategies for product feature summarization, query generation, and product retrieval. Furthermore, we propose the benchmark called PROCLARE to evaluate the agent's performance both automatically and qualitatively with the aid of a LLM-driven user simulator. Experiments show that ProductAgent interacts positively with the user and enhances retrieval performance with increasing dialogue turns, where user demands become gradually more explicit and detailed. All the source codes will be released after the review anonymity period.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces ProductAgent, a conversational product search agent that asks clarification questions to resolve ambiguous user queries in e-commerce. It proposes a benchmark, PROCLARE, with an LLM-driven user simulator for evaluation. Experiments show that ProductAgent improves retrieval performance as dialogue progresses by making user demands more explicit.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了ProductAgent，一种通过提问澄清问题来解决电商场景中模糊用户查询的对话式产品搜索代理。它构建了名为PROCLARE的基准测试，并借助大语言模型驱动的用户模拟器进行评估。实验表明，ProductAgent能随着对话轮次增加提升检索性能，使用户需求逐渐明确化。

papers.title: Unlocking Smarter Device Control: Foresighted Planning with a World Model-Driven Code Execution Approach
papers.short_title: World Model-Driven Code Execution for Device Control
papers.abstract: The automatic control of mobile devices is essential for efficiently performing complex tasks that involve multiple sequential steps. However, these tasks pose significant challenges due to the limited environmental information available at each step, primarily through visual observations. As a result, current approaches, which typically rely on reactive policies, focus solely on immediate observations and often lead to suboptimal decision-making. To address this problem, we propose \textbf{Foresighted Planning with World Model-Driven Code Execution (FPWC)},a framework that prioritizes natural language understanding and structured reasoning to enhance the agent's global understanding of the environment by developing a task-oriented, refinable \emph{world model} at the outset of the task. Foresighted actions are subsequently generated through iterative planning within this world model, executed in the form of executable code. Extensive experiments conducted in simulated environments and on real mobile devices demonstrate that our method outperforms previous approaches, particularly achieving a 44.4\% relative improvement in task success rate compared to the state-of-the-art in the simulated environment. Code and demo are provided in the supplementary material.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces FPWC, a framework for mobile device control that builds a task-oriented world model from initial observations and uses it for foresighted planning via code execution. Unlike reactive methods, FPWC enables global understanding and iterative planning, achieving a 44.4% relative improvement in task success rate over state-of-the-art in simulated environments.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出FPWC框架，通过从初始观察构建任务导向的世界模型，并基于该模型进行前瞻性代码执行规划。与仅依赖即时观察的反应式方法不同，FPWC实现了全局理解和迭代规划，在模拟环境中任务成功率相对提升44.4%。

papers.title: UIOrchestra: Generating High-Fidelity Code from UI Designs with a Multi-agent System
papers.short_title: UIOrchestra: Multi-agent Code from UI Designs
papers.summary_en: UIOrchestra introduces a multi-agent system that converts UI designs into high-fidelity code by decomposing the task into specialized roles: a planner, a designer, and a coder. The planner analyzes the design and creates a structured plan, the designer generates visual assets, and the coder implements the code, with agents collaborating iteratively to refine output. This approach significantly improves code quality and fidelity compared to single-model baselines, achieving state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets.
papers.summary_zh: UIOrchestra提出了一种多智能体系统，通过将任务分解为规划者、设计者和编码者等专门角色，将UI设计转换为高保真代码。规划者分析设计并制定结构化方案，设计者生成视觉资源，编码者实现代码，智能体通过迭代协作优化输出。该方法相比单模型基线显著提升了代码质量和保真度，在基准数据集上取得了最先进的结果。

papers.title: Proactive Assistant Dialogue Generation from Streaming Egocentric Videos
papers.short_title: Proactive Dialogue from Egocentric Videos
papers.abstract: Recent advances in conversational AI have been substantial, but developing real-time systems for perceptual task guidance remains challenging. These systems must provide interactive, proactive assistance based on streaming visual inputs, yet their development is constrained by the costly and labor-intensive process of data collection and system evaluation. To address these limitations, we present a comprehensive framework with three key contributions. First, we introduce a novel data curation pipeline that synthesizes dialogues from annotated egocentric videos, resulting in \dataset, a large-scale synthetic dialogue dataset spanning multiple domains. Second, we develop a suite of automatic evaluation metrics, validated through extensive human studies. Third, we propose an end-to-end model that processes streaming video inputs to generate contextually appropriate responses, incorporating novel techniques for handling data imbalance and long-duration videos. This work lays the foundation for developing real-time, proactive AI assistants capable of guiding users through diverse tasks. Project page: https://pro-assist.github.io/
papers.summary_en: This paper presents a framework for building proactive AI assistants that generate real-time dialogue from streaming egocentric video. It introduces a data curation pipeline to synthesize large-scale dialogue datasets, a suite of automatic evaluation metrics validated by human studies, and an end-to-end model that handles data imbalance and long videos. The work addresses the high cost of data collection and evaluation, enabling the development of interactive assistants for perceptual task guidance.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一个框架，用于从流式第一人称视频中生成实时对话，构建主动式AI助手。它引入了一个数据合成流水线来生成大规模对话数据集，一套经人工验证的自动评估指标，以及一个能处理数据不平衡和长视频的端到端模型。该工作解决了数据收集和评估成本高的问题，为开发交互式感知任务指导助手奠定了基础。

papers.title: ActionStudio: A Lightweight Framework for Data and Training of Large Action Models
papers.short_title: ActionStudio: Framework for Large Action Models
papers.abstract: Large Action models are essential for enabling autonomous agents to perform complex tasks. However, training such models remains challenging due to the diversity of agent environments and the complexity of noisy agentic data. Existing infrastructure offers limited support for scalable, agent-specific fine-tuning and standardized agent data processing. We introduce ActionStudio, a lightweight and extensible data and training framework designed for large action models. ActionStudio unifies diverse agent trajectories using our proposed Unified Format 2.0, supports a range of training workflows with optimized multi-node distributed setup, and integrates robust preprocessing and real-time verification tools. ActionStudio demonstrates up to 9x higher throughput compared to existing agentic training frameworks, and our trained models yield top performances across public and realistic agent benchmarks. To support the broader research community, we open-source the ActionStudio framework and release actionstudio-98k, a curated dataset of 98k high-quality trajectories. Code: https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/xLAM.
papers.summary_en: ActionStudio is a lightweight framework for training large action models, unifying diverse agent trajectories via Unified Format 2.0 and supporting scalable multi-node fine-tuning. It achieves up to 9x higher throughput than existing frameworks and yields top performance on agent benchmarks. The framework is open-sourced along with a curated dataset of 98k high-quality trajectories.
papers.summary_zh: ActionStudio是一个轻量级框架，用于训练大型动作模型，通过统一格式2.0整合多样化的智能体轨迹，并支持可扩展的多节点微调。相比现有框架，其吞吐量提升高达9倍，在智能体基准测试中取得顶尖性能。该框架与包含9.8万条高质量轨迹的精选数据集一同开源。

papers.title: Vision-and-Language Navigation with Analogical Textual Descriptions in LLMs
papers.short_title: VLN with Analogical Textual Descriptions in LLMs
papers.abstract: Integrating large language models (LLMs) into embodied AI models is becoming increasingly prevalent. However, existing zero-shot LLM-based Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) agents either encode images as textual scene descriptions, potentially oversimplifying visual details, or process raw image inputs, which can fail to capture abstract semantics required for high-level reasoning. In this paper, we improve the navigation agent's contextual understanding by incorporating textual descriptions from multiple perspectives that facilitate analogical reasoning across images. By leveraging text-based analogical reasoning, the agent enhances its global scene understanding and spatial reasoning, leading to more accurate action decisions. We evaluate our approach on the R2R dataset, where our experiments demonstrate significant improvements in navigation performance.
papers.summary_en: This paper improves Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) by using large language models (LLMs) to generate analogical textual descriptions of images from multiple perspectives. These descriptions help the agent perform analogical reasoning across scenes, enhancing global understanding and spatial reasoning for better action decisions. Experiments on the R2R dataset show significant navigation performance gains over existing zero-shot LLM-based methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过利用大语言模型（LLMs）从多个视角生成图像的类比文本描述，改进了视觉-语言导航（VLN）。这些描述帮助智能体在场景间进行类比推理，增强了全局理解和空间推理能力，从而做出更准确的动作决策。在R2R数据集上的实验表明，与现有的零样本LLM方法相比，导航性能有显著提升。

papers.title: Knowing More, Acting Better: Hierarchical Representation for Embodied Decision-Making
papers.short_title: Hierarchical Representation for Embodied Decision-Making
