papers.summary_en: This paper proposes a hierarchical representation framework for embodied decision-making that integrates high-level semantic knowledge with low-level sensorimotor data. The approach enables agents to reason about abstract goals while grounding actions in physical reality, improving both planning efficiency and execution robustness. Experiments in simulated environments show significant performance gains over flat representations, particularly in long-horizon tasks requiring compositional reasoning.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种用于具身决策的分层表示框架，将高层语义知识与低层感知运动数据相结合。该方法使智能体能够推理抽象目标，同时将动作锚定在物理现实中，从而提升规划效率和执行鲁棒性。在模拟环境中的实验表明，该方法在需要组合推理的长时域任务中，性能显著优于扁平表示方法。

papers.title: UI-Hawk: Unleashing the Screen Stream Understanding for Mobile GUI Agents
papers.short_title: UI-Hawk: Screen Stream Understanding for Mobile GUI Agents
papers.summary_en: UI-Hawk is a vision-language model designed to enhance mobile GUI agents' understanding of screen streams. It introduces a novel approach to process continuous screen frames, enabling agents to better comprehend dynamic UI changes and user interactions. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on several GUI understanding benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world mobile tasks.
papers.summary_zh: UI-Hawk是一种专为增强移动GUI代理对屏幕流理解而设计的视觉语言模型。它引入了一种处理连续屏幕帧的新方法，使代理能够更好地理解动态UI变化和用户交互。该模型在多个GUI理解基准测试中取得了最先进的性能，展示了其在真实移动任务中的有效性。

papers.title: COLA: Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework with Dynamic Task Scheduling for GUI Automation
papers.short_title: COLA: Multi-Agent Framework for GUI Automation
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces COLA, a collaborative multi-agent framework for GUI automation that dynamically schedules tasks among specialized agents. It addresses the limitations of static task allocation by using a coordinator agent to decompose complex tasks and assign them to appropriate agents based on real-time context. Experimental results demonstrate that COLA improves task completion efficiency and accuracy compared to existing single-agent and fixed-pipeline approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出COLA，一种用于GUI自动化的协作式多智能体框架，通过动态任务调度实现智能体间的协同。该框架利用协调智能体将复杂任务分解，并根据实时上下文分配给合适的专业智能体，从而克服了静态任务分配的局限性。实验结果表明，与现有单智能体和固定流水线方法相比，COLA在任务完成效率和准确性上均有显著提升。

papers.title: CityEQA: A Hierarchical LLM Agent on Embodied Question Answering Benchmark in City Space
papers.short_title: CityEQA: Hierarchical LLM Agent for City EQA
papers.abstract: Embodied Question Answering (EQA) has primarily focused on indoor environments, leaving the complexities of urban settings-spanning environment, action, and perception-largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce CityEQA, a new task where an embodied agent answers open-vocabulary questions through active exploration in dynamic city spaces. To support this task, we present CityEQA-EC, the first benchmark dataset featuring 1,412 human-annotated tasks across six categories, grounded in a realistic 3D urban simulator. Moreover, we propose Planner-Manager-Actor (PMA), a novel agent tailored for CityEQA. PMA enables long-horizon planning and hierarchical task execution: the Planner breaks down the question answering into sub-tasks, the Manager maintains an object-centric cognitive map for spatial reasoning during the process control, and the specialized Actors handle navigation, exploration, and collection sub-tasks. Experiments demonstrate that PMA achieves 60.7% of human-level answering accuracy, significantly outperforming competitive baselines. While promising, the performance gap compared to humans highlights the need for enhanced visual reasoning in CityEQA. This work paves the way for future advancements in urban spatial intelligence. Dataset and code are available at https://github.com/BiluYong/CityEQA.git.
papers.summary_en: CityEQA introduces a new embodied question answering task in dynamic urban environments, along with a benchmark dataset of 1,412 human-annotated tasks. The proposed Planner-Manager-Actor (PMA) agent achieves 60.7% of human-level accuracy through hierarchical planning and spatial reasoning, significantly outperforming baselines. This work extends EQA from indoor to city spaces, highlighting the need for improved visual reasoning in complex urban settings.
papers.summary_zh: CityEQA提出了一个在动态城市环境中的具身问答新任务，并提供了包含1412个人工标注任务的基准数据集。所提出的规划者-管理者-执行者（PMA）智能体通过分层规划和空间推理达到了人类水平60.7%的准确率，显著优于基线方法。该工作将EQA从室内扩展到城市空间，揭示了在复杂城市环境中提升视觉推理能力的必要性。

papers.title: ChatVLA: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Robot Control with Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.short_title: ChatVLA: Unified Multimodal Understanding & Robot Control
papers.abstract: Humans possess a unified cognitive ability to perceive, comprehend, and interact with the physical world. Why can't large language models replicate this holistic understanding? Through a systematic analysis of existing training paradigms in vision-language-action models (VLA), we identify two key challenges: spurious forgetting, where robot training overwrites crucial visual-text alignments, and task interference, where competing control and understanding tasks degrade performance when trained jointly. To overcome these limitations, we propose ChatVLA, a novel framework featuring Phased Alignment Training, which incrementally integrates multimodal data after initial control mastery, and a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to minimize task interference. ChatVLA demonstrates competitive performance on visual question-answering datasets and significantly surpasses state-of-the-art vision-language-action (VLA) methods on multimodal understanding benchmarks. Notably, it achieves a six times higher performance on MMMU and scores 47.2% on MMStar with a more parameter-efficient design than ECoT. Furthermore, ChatVLA demonstrates superior performance on 25 real-world robot manipulation tasks compared to existing VLA methods like OpenVLA. Our findings highlight the potential of our unified framework for achieving both robust multimodal understanding and effective robot control.
papers.summary_en: ChatVLA introduces a unified vision-language-action model that addresses spurious forgetting and task interference in robot learning through Phased Alignment Training and a Mixture-of-Experts architecture, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both multimodal understanding benchmarks and real-world robot manipulation tasks.
papers.summary_zh: ChatVLA提出了一种统一的视觉-语言-动作模型，通过分阶段对齐训练和混合专家架构解决了机器人学习中的虚假遗忘和任务干扰问题，在多模态理解基准和真实机器人操作任务上均达到了最先进性能。

papers.title: Enabling Conversational Interaction with Mobile UI using Large Language Models
papers.short_title: Conversational Mobile UI with LLMs
papers.abstract: Conversational agents show the promise to allow users to interact with mobile devices using language. However, to perform diverse UI tasks with natural language, developers typically need to create separate datasets and models for each specific task, which is expensive and effort-consuming. Recently, pre-trained large language models (LLMs) have been shown capable of generalizing to various downstream tasks when prompted with a handful of examples from the target task. This paper investigates the feasibility of enabling versatile conversational interactions with mobile UIs using a single LLM. We designed prompting techniques to adapt an LLM to mobile UIs. We experimented with four important modeling tasks that address various scenarios in conversational interaction. Our method achieved competitive performance on these challenging tasks without requiring dedicated datasets and training, offering a lightweight and generalizable approach to enable language-based mobile interaction.
papers.summary_en: This paper explores using a single large language model (LLM) to enable conversational interaction with mobile UIs, avoiding the need for task-specific datasets and training. By designing prompting techniques, the authors adapt an LLM to perform four key UI tasks, achieving competitive performance. The work demonstrates a lightweight, generalizable approach for language-based mobile interaction.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探索使用单一大型语言模型（LLM）实现与移动界面的对话交互，避免了为每个任务单独构建数据集和训练模型的需求。通过设计提示技术，作者将LLM适配到四个关键的UI任务上，并取得了有竞争力的性能。该工作展示了一种轻量级、可泛化的方法，用于实现基于语言的移动交互。

papers.title: WebUI: A Dataset for Enhancing Visual UI Understanding with Web Semantics
papers.short_title: WebUI: Visual UI Understanding with Web Semantics
papers.abstract: Modeling user interfaces (UIs) from visual information allows systems to make inferences about the functionality and semantics needed to support use cases in accessibility, app automation, and testing. Current datasets for training machine learning models are limited in size due to the costly and time-consuming process of manually collecting and annotating UIs. We crawled the web to construct WebUI, a large dataset of 400,000 rendered web pages associated with automatically extracted metadata. We analyze the composition of WebUI and show that while automatically extracted data is noisy, most examples meet basic criteria for visual UI modeling. We applied several strategies for incorporating semantics found in web pages to increase the performance of visual UI understanding models in the mobile domain, where less labeled data is available: (i) element detection, (ii) screen classification and (iii) screen similarity.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces WebUI, a large dataset of 400,000 rendered web pages with automatically extracted metadata, designed to train visual UI understanding models. It addresses the scarcity of labeled UI data by leveraging web semantics, showing that noisy web data can still be useful. The authors demonstrate that incorporating web semantics improves performance on mobile UI tasks like element detection, screen classification, and screen similarity.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文提出了WebUI，一个包含40万个渲染网页及其自动提取元数据的大型数据集，旨在训练视觉UI理解模型。它通过利用网页语义解决了标注UI数据稀缺的问题，并表明即使存在噪声，网页数据仍然有效。作者证明，融入网页语义能提升移动端UI任务（如元素检测、屏幕分类和屏幕相似性）的性能。

papers.title: MUD: Towards a Large-Scale and Noise-Filtered UI Dataset for Modern Style UI Modeling
papers.short_title: MUD: Large-Scale Noise-Filtered UI Dataset
papers.abstract: The importance of computational modeling of mobile user interfaces (UIs) is undeniable. However, these require a high-quality UI dataset. Existing datasets are often outdated, collected years ago, and are frequently noisy with mismatches in their visual representation. This presents challenges in modeling UI understanding in the wild. This paper introduces a novel approach to automatically mine UI data from Android apps, leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to mimic human-like exploration. To ensure dataset quality, we employ the best practices in UI noise filtering and incorporate human annotation as a final validation step. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of LLMs-enhanced app exploration in mining more meaningful UIs, resulting in a large dataset MUD of 18k human-annotated UIs from 3.3k apps. We highlight the usefulness of MUD in two common UI modeling tasks: element detection and UI retrieval, showcasing its potential to establish a foundation for future research into high-quality, modern UIs.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces MUD, a large-scale, noise-filtered UI dataset of 18k human-annotated screens from 3.3k Android apps, created using LLMs to simulate human-like app exploration and rigorous noise filtering. The dataset addresses the limitations of existing outdated and noisy UI datasets, enabling better modeling of modern mobile UIs. Experiments show MUD's effectiveness in improving UI element detection and retrieval tasks, providing a foundation for future UI modeling research.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了MUD，一个大规模、经过噪声过滤的UI数据集，包含来自3300个安卓应用的1.8万个人工标注界面，通过利用大语言模型模拟人类探索应用并严格过滤噪声构建而成。该数据集解决了现有UI数据集过时且噪声多的问题，有助于更好地建模现代移动界面。实验表明，MUD能有效提升UI元素检测和检索任务的效果，为未来UI建模研究奠定了基础。

papers.title: Automatic Macro Mining from Interaction Traces at Scale
papers.short_title: Macro Mining from Interaction Traces
papers.abstract: Macros are building block tasks of our everyday smartphone activity (e.g., "login", or "booking a flight"). Effectively extracting macros is important for understanding mobile interaction and enabling task automation. These macros are however difficult to extract at scale as they can be comprised of multiple steps yet hidden within programmatic components of mobile apps. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach based on Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically extract semantically meaningful macros from both random and user-curated mobile interaction traces. The macros produced by our approach are automatically tagged with natural language descriptions and are fully executable. We conduct multiple studies to validate the quality of extracted macros, including user evaluation, comparative analysis against human-curated tasks, and automatic execution of these macros. These experiments and analyses demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and the usefulness of extracted macros in various downstream applications.
papers.summary_en: This paper presents a novel method using Large Language Models to automatically extract semantically meaningful macros from mobile interaction traces. The macros are tagged with natural language descriptions and are fully executable. Experiments show the approach produces high-quality macros useful for task automation and understanding mobile interactions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种基于大语言模型的新方法，能够从移动交互轨迹中自动提取具有语义意义的宏。这些宏带有自然语言描述且可完全执行。实验表明，该方法能生成高质量的宏，有助于任务自动化及理解移动交互。

papers.title: Demonstrating PANDALens: Enhancing Daily Activity Documentation with AI-assisted In-Context Writing on OHMD
papers.short_title: PANDALens: AI-assisted Writing on OHMD
papers.abstract: We introduce PANDALens, a Proactive AI Narrative Documentation Assistant built on an Optical See-Through Head-Mounted Display that transforms the in-context writing tool into an intelligent companion during daily activities. PANDALens observes multimodal contextual information from user behaviors and the environment to detect interesting moments and elicit contemplation. It also employs Large Language Models to transform such multimodal information into coherent narratives with significantly reduced user effort. PANDALens was iteratively designed through a formative study identifying the user requirements. We verify its utility in a real-world travel scenario in improving writing quality and travel enjoyment while minimizing user effort.
papers.summary_en: PANDALens is an AI-powered assistant for Optical See-Through Head-Mounted Displays that helps users document daily activities by automatically detecting interesting moments and generating coherent narratives from multimodal context, reducing user effort while improving writing quality and enjoyment.
papers.summary_zh: PANDALens是一款基于光学透视头戴显示器的AI辅助工具，通过自动检测有趣时刻并从多模态上下文生成连贯叙述，帮助用户记录日常活动，在减少用户努力的同时提升写作质量和体验。

papers.title: Computational Representations for Graphical User Interfaces
papers.short_title: Computational Representations for GUIs
papers.abstract: Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) have been widely used in daily life. To enhance GUI design and interaction experience on GUIs, it is important to understand GUIs and understand how individuals interact with them. Consequently, my thesis focuses on applying computational approaches to improve our understanding of GUIs and user interactions. First, I introduce novel GUI representations to capture the visual, spatial, and semantic factors of GUIs and improve the performance of downstream GUI tasks. Second, I simulate how users visually engage with GUIs to understand user interactions to help inform the design of GUI representations. Third, based on the understanding of GUIs and interactions on GUIs, I develop language language representations aimed at assisting users in understanding and more effectively interacting with GUIs.
papers.summary_en: This thesis introduces novel computational representations for graphical user interfaces (GUIs) that capture visual, spatial, and semantic features to improve downstream tasks. It also simulates user visual engagement with GUIs to better understand interaction patterns and inform representation design. Finally, it develops language representations to help users understand and interact with GUIs more effectively.
papers.summary_zh: 本论文提出了新颖的图形用户界面（GUI）计算表示方法，捕捉视觉、空间和语义特征以提升下游任务性能。同时，通过模拟用户对GUI的视觉参与来理解交互模式，从而指导表示设计。最后，开发了语言表示以帮助用户更有效地理解和操作GUI。

papers.title: Graph4GUI: Graph Neural Networks for Representing Graphical User Interfaces
papers.short_title: Graph4GUI: GNN for GUI Representation
papers.abstract: Present-day graphical user interfaces (GUIs) exhibit diverse arrangements of text, graphics, and interactive elements such as buttons and menus, but representations of GUIs have not kept up. They do not encapsulate both semantic and visuo-spatial relationships among elements. To seize machine learning’s potential for GUIs more efficiently, Graph4GUI exploits graph neural networks to capture individual elements’ properties and their semantic—visuo-spatial constraints in a layout. The learned representation demonstrated its effectiveness in multiple tasks, especially generating designs in a challenging GUI autocompletion task, which involved predicting the positions of remaining unplaced elements in a partially completed GUI. The new model’s suggestions showed alignment and visual appeal superior to the baseline method and received higher subjective ratings for preference. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical benefits and efficiency advantages designers perceive when utilizing our model as an autocompletion plug-in.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces Graph4GUI, a graph neural network approach to represent graphical user interfaces by capturing both semantic and visuo-spatial relationships among UI elements. The learned representation is applied to a GUI autocompletion task, where it predicts positions for unplaced elements in a partially completed layout, outperforming baselines in alignment and visual appeal. User studies also show that designers perceive practical benefits and efficiency gains when using the model as a plug-in tool.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出Graph4GUI，一种利用图神经网络表示图形用户界面的方法，能够同时捕捉UI元素间的语义和视觉空间关系。该表示被应用于GUI自动补全任务，即预测部分完成布局中未放置元素的位置，在对齐度和视觉吸引力上优于基线方法。用户研究还表明，设计师在使用该模型作为插件工具时感知到实际效益和效率提升。

papers.title: OmniActions: Predicting Digital Actions in Response to Real-World Multimodal Sensory Inputs with LLMs
papers.short_title: OmniActions: Digital Actions from Multimodal Inputs
papers.abstract: The progression to “Pervasive Augmented Reality” envisions easy access to multimodal information continuously. However, in many everyday scenarios, users are occupied physically, cognitively or socially. This may increase the friction to act upon the multimodal information that users encounter in the world. To reduce such friction, future interactive interfaces should intelligently provide quick access to digital actions based on users’ context. To explore the range of possible digital actions, we conducted a diary study that required participants to capture and share the media that they intended to perform actions on (e.g., images or audio), along with their desired actions and other contextual information. Using this data, we generated a holistic design space of digital follow-up actions that could be performed in response to different types of multimodal sensory inputs. We then designed OmniActions, a pipeline powered by large language models (LLMs) that processes multimodal sensory inputs and predicts follow-up actions on the target information grounded in the derived design space. Using the empirical data collected in the diary study, we performed quantitative evaluations on three variations of LLM techniques (intent classification, in-context learning and finetuning) and identified the most effective technique for our task. Additionally, as an instantiation of the pipeline, we developed an interactive prototype and reported preliminary user feedback about how people perceive and react to the action predictions and its errors.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces OmniActions, a system that uses large language models to predict digital actions users might want to take in response to real-world multimodal sensory inputs like images or audio. The authors first conducted a diary study to collect examples of such actions and created a design space of possible follow-up actions. They then built a pipeline that processes multimodal inputs and predicts actions, evaluating different LLM techniques and finding finetuning most effective. A prototype was developed and tested, showing promise for reducing user friction in pervasive augmented reality scenarios.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了OmniActions系统，利用大语言模型预测用户对现实世界多模态感官输入（如图像或音频）可能想要执行的数字动作。作者首先通过日记研究收集了此类动作的示例，并构建了可能的后续动作设计空间。随后，他们构建了一个处理多模态输入并预测动作的流水线，评估了不同的大语言模型技术，发现微调最为有效。最后开发了原型并进行了测试，表明其在减少普适增强现实场景中用户摩擦方面具有潜力。

papers.title: Reducing the Search Space on demand helps Older Adults find Mobile UI Features quickly, on par with Younger Adults
papers.short_title: Search Space Reduction: Older Adults UI
papers.abstract: As mobile user interfaces (UI) become feature-rich, navigation gets more complex. Finding features quickly starts demanding information-intensive strategies for decision-making—which can be challenging for older adults. Older adults examine fewer details, requiring fewer cognitive resources, when searching for information with a large number of alternatives. In this paper, we first systematically examine various ways to convey a reduced feature space. Visually emphasizing three relevant options helped older adults find a specific feature more quickly—on par with younger adults. Older users were more efficient when options were highlighted along with their context or with a weighted zoom than when just highlighted, and they also preferred these two the most. We then present Nav Nudge, an interaction technique that uses voice input and large language models to visually reduce the feature search space on demand—and discuss how older adults use it within a mobile map application.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how reducing the search space in mobile UIs can help older adults find features as quickly as younger adults. Through systematic experiments, they found that visually emphasizing three relevant options, especially with context or weighted zoom, significantly improved older adults' efficiency. They then developed Nav Nudge, a voice- and LLM-based technique that reduces the feature search space on demand, and demonstrated its effectiveness in a mobile map application.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了在移动界面中减少搜索空间如何帮助老年人像年轻人一样快速找到功能。通过系统实验，他们发现视觉上突出三个相关选项，尤其是结合上下文或加权缩放，能显著提高老年人的效率。随后，他们开发了Nav Nudge，一种基于语音和大语言模型的按需减少特征搜索空间的技术，并在移动地图应用中展示了其有效性。

papers.title: Over the Mouse: Navigating across the GUI with Finger-Lifting Operation Mouse
papers.short_title: Finger-Lifting Mouse GUI Navigation
papers.abstract: Modern GUIs often have a hierarchical structure, i.e., the z-axis of the GUI interaction space. However, conventional mice do not support effective navigation along the z-axis, leading to increased physical movements and cognitive load. To address this inefficiency, we present the OtMouse, a novel mouse that supports finger-lifting operations by detecting finger height through proximity sensors embedded beneath the mouse buttons, and ‘Over the Mouse’ (OtM) interface, a set of interaction techniques along the z-axis of the GUI interaction space with the OtMouse. Initially, We evaluated the performance of finger-lifting operations (n = 8) with the OtMouse for two- and three-level lifting discrimination tasks. Subsequently, we conducted a user study (n = 16) to compare the usability of the OtM interface and traditional mouse interface for three representative tasks: ‘Context Switch,’ ‘Video Preview,’ and ‘Map Zooming.’ The results showed that OtM interface was both qualitatively and quantitatively superior to using traditional mouse in the Context Switch and Video Preview tasks. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to enhance mouse-based GUI navigation experiences.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces OtMouse, a novel mouse with proximity sensors under its buttons that detect finger-lifting height, enabling z-axis navigation in hierarchical GUIs. The accompanying 'Over the Mouse' interface supports tasks like context switching, video preview, and map zooming. User studies show that OtMouse significantly outperforms traditional mice in efficiency and user preference for context switch and video preview tasks, reducing physical movement and cognitive load.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种新型鼠标OtMouse，通过在按键下方嵌入接近传感器检测手指抬起高度，支持在层级化图形用户界面中进行Z轴导航。配套的“Over the Mouse”界面实现了上下文切换、视频预览和地图缩放等任务。用户研究表明，在上下文切换和视频预览任务中，OtMouse在效率和用户偏好上显著优于传统鼠标，减少了物理移动和认知负荷。

papers.title: UXAgent: An LLM Agent-Based Usability Testing Framework for Web Design
papers.short_title: UXAgent: LLM Usability Testing
papers.abstract: Usability testing is a fundamental yet challenging research method for user experience (UX) researchers to evaluate a web design. Recent advances in Large Language Model-simulated Agent (LLM Agent) research inspired us to design UXAgent to support UX researchers in evaluating and reiterating their usability testing study design before they conduct the real human-subject study. Our system features an LLM Agent module and a universal browser connector module so that UX researchers can automatically generate thousands of simulated users to test the target website. The system can generate UX study results in qualitative (e.g., interviewing how an agent thinks), quantitative (e.g., # of actions), and video recording formats for UX researchers to analyze. Through a heuristic user evaluation with five UX researchers, participants praised the innovation of our system but also expressed concerns about the future of UX study with LLM Agents1.
papers.summary_en: UXAgent is a framework that uses LLM-based agents to simulate thousands of users for automated usability testing of web designs, generating qualitative, quantitative, and video results. It aims to help UX researchers evaluate and refine their study designs before human testing. A heuristic evaluation with five researchers praised its innovation but raised concerns about the role of LLM agents in future UX studies.
papers.summary_zh: UXAgent是一个利用大语言模型智能体模拟数千用户进行网页设计自动化可用性测试的框架，可生成定性、定量及视频结果。其目标是帮助用户体验研究者在进行真人测试前评估和优化研究设计。五位研究者的启发式评估称赞了该系统的创新性，但也对LLM智能体在未来用户体验研究中的角色表达了担忧。

papers.title: Plan-Then-Execute: An Empirical Study of User Trust and Team Performance When Using LLM Agents As A Daily Assistant
papers.short_title: Plan-Then-Execute: LLM Agent Trust
papers.abstract: Since the explosion in popularity of ChatGPT, large language models (LLMs) have continued to impact our everyday lives. Equipped with external tools that are designed for a specific purpose (e.g., for flight booking or an alarm clock), LLM agents exercise an increasing capability to assist humans in their daily work. Although LLM agents have shown a promising blueprint as daily assistants, there is a limited understanding of how they can provide daily assistance based on planning and sequential decision making capabilities. We draw inspiration from recent work that has highlighted the value of ‘LLM-modulo’ setups in conjunction with humans-in-the-loop for planning tasks. We conducted an empirical study (N = 248) of LLM agents as daily assistants in six commonly occurring tasks with different levels of risk typically associated with them (e.g., flight ticket booking and credit card payments). To ensure user agency and control over the LLM agent, we adopted LLM agents in a plan-then-execute manner, wherein the agents conducted step-wise planning and step-by-step execution in a simulation environment. We analyzed how user involvement at each stage affects their trust and collaborative team performance. Our findings demonstrate that LLM agents can be a double-edged sword — (1) they can work well when a high-quality plan and necessary user involvement in execution are available, and (2) users can easily mistrust the LLM agents with plans that seem plausible. We synthesized key insights for using LLM agents as daily assistants to calibrate user trust and achieve better overall task outcomes. Our work has important implications for the future design of daily assistants and human-AI collaboration with LLM agents.
papers.summary_en: This paper presents an empirical study (N=248) of LLM agents used as daily assistants in six common tasks with varying risk levels. The agents operate in a 'plan-then-execute' manner with human oversight, and the study examines how user involvement affects trust and team performance. Results show LLM agents are a double-edged sword: they perform well with high-quality plans and user involvement, but users can easily mistrust plausible-looking plans. The work provides insights for calibrating trust and improving human-AI collaboration in daily assistance scenarios.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过一项包含248名参与者的实证研究，探讨了LLM代理作为日常助手在六种不同风险水平的常见任务中的应用。代理采用“先规划后执行”的方式，并在人类监督下运行，研究分析了用户参与如何影响信任和团队协作表现。结果表明，LLM代理是一把双刃剑：在高质量规划和必要用户参与下表现良好，但用户容易对看似合理的计划产生不信任。该研究为校准信任和改善日常助手场景中的人机协作提供了关键见解。

papers.title: GenerativeGUI: Dynamic GUI Generation Leveraging LLMs for Enhanced User Interaction on Chat Interfaces
papers.short_title: GenerativeGUI: LLM GUI Generation
papers.abstract: Conversational AI (CAI) systems using large language models (LLMs) are becoming increasingly adept at performing a wide range of tasks with text-based interfaces. However, tasks that require detailed input can reduce usability and efficiency, as they often involve lengthy text exchanges. This paper introduces GenerativeGUI, a novel approach where LLMs dynamically generate graphical user interfaces (GUIs) tailored to the ongoing conversation. By generating HTML, which is rendered into an interactive GUI, GenerativeGUI presents intuitive widgets, enhancing user interaction and reducing cognitive load. A user study comparing GenerativeGUI with conventional text-based CAI systems demonstrated that the new system significantly improves usability, particularly in scenarios requiring multiple clarifying questions. Specifically, GenerativeGUI reduces mental demand, effort and task completion time, and enhances user satisfaction. This research highlights the potential of dynamic GUI generation to streamline complex CAI interactions, providing an effective solution to improve user experience in multi-turn conversations.
papers.summary_en: GenerativeGUI is a system that uses large language models to dynamically generate graphical user interfaces (GUIs) during conversations, replacing lengthy text exchanges with interactive widgets. This approach reduces cognitive load and task completion time, especially for tasks requiring multiple clarifying questions. A user study showed significant improvements in usability, mental demand, and user satisfaction compared to traditional text-based conversational AI.
papers.summary_zh: GenerativeGUI 是一种利用大语言模型在对话过程中动态生成图形用户界面（GUI）的系统，用交互式小部件替代冗长的文本交流。该方法能降低认知负荷和任务完成时间，尤其适用于需要多次澄清问题的场景。用户研究表明，与传统基于文本的对话式 AI 相比，该系统在可用性、心理需求和用户满意度方面均有显著提升。

papers.title: Observe, Ask, Intervene: Designing AI Agents for More Inclusive Meetings
papers.short_title: OAI: AI Agents for Inclusive Meetings
papers.abstract: Video conferencing meetings are more effective when they are inclusive, but inclusion often hinges on meeting leaders’ and/or co-facilitators’ practices. AI systems can be designed to improve meeting inclusion at scale by moderating negative meeting behaviors and supporting meeting leaders. We explored this design space by conducting 9 user-centered ideation sessions, instantiating design insights in a prototype “virtual co-host” system, and testing the system in a formative exploratory lab study (n = 68 across 12 groups, 18 interviews). We found that ideation session participants wanted AI agents to ask questions before intervening, which we formalized as the “Observe, Ask, Intervene” (OAI) framework. Participants who used our prototype preferred OAI over fully autonomous intervention, but rationalized away the virtual co-host’s critical feedback. From these findings, we derive guidelines for designing AI agents to influence behavior and mediate group work. We also contribute methodological and design guidelines specific to mitigating inequitable meeting participation.
papers.summary_en: This paper explores how AI agents can improve inclusivity in video meetings by introducing the 'Observe, Ask, Intervene' (OAI) framework, where the agent first observes, then asks participants before intervening. Through user studies and a prototype virtual co-host, the authors found that participants preferred OAI over fully autonomous intervention, though they often dismissed the agent's critical feedback. The work provides design guidelines for AI agents that influence group behavior and mitigate inequitable participation in meetings.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了AI代理如何通过提出“观察、询问、干预”（OAI）框架来提升视频会议的包容性，即代理先观察，再询问参与者，然后才进行干预。通过用户研究和原型虚拟联合主持人，作者发现参与者更偏好OAI而非完全自主的干预，尽管他们常常忽视代理的批评性反馈。该研究为设计影响群体行为并缓解会议中不平等参与的AI代理提供了指导原则。

papers.title: Leveraging Multimodal LLM for Inspirational User Interface Search
papers.short_title: Multimodal LLM for Inspirational UI Search
papers.abstract: Inspirational search, the process of exploring designs to inform and inspire new creative work, is pivotal in mobile user interface (UI) design. However, exploring the vast space of UI references remains a challenge. Existing AI-based UI search methods often miss crucial semantics like target users or the mood of apps. Additionally, these models typically require metadata like view hierarchies, limiting their practical use. We used a multimodal large language model (MLLM) to extract and interpret semantics from mobile UI images. We identified key UI semantics through a formative study and developed a semantic-based UI search system. Through computational and human evaluations, we demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing UI retrieval methods, offering UI designers a more enriched and contextually relevant search experience. We enhance the understanding of mobile UI design semantics and highlight MLLMs’ potential in inspirational search, providing a rich dataset of UI semantics for future studies.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a novel approach to inspirational UI search using multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to extract and interpret design semantics from mobile UI images, overcoming limitations of existing methods that rely on metadata or miss key semantics like target users and mood. Through a formative study, the authors identify critical UI semantics and build a semantic-based search system that outperforms current retrieval methods in both computational and human evaluations. The work provides a rich dataset of UI semantics and demonstrates the potential of MLLMs for enhancing inspirational design search.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种利用多模态大语言模型（MLLM）从移动界面图像中提取和解释设计语义的新方法，用于灵感式界面搜索，克服了现有方法依赖元数据或忽略目标用户、情绪等关键语义的局限。通过形成性研究，作者识别了关键的界面语义，并构建了基于语义的搜索系统，在计算评估和人工评估中均优于现有检索方法。该工作提供了丰富的界面语义数据集，展示了MLLM在增强灵感式设计搜索方面的潜力。

papers.title: Aptly: Making Mobile Apps from Natural Language
papers.short_title: Aptly: Making Mobile Apps from Natural Language
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Aptly, a platform designed to democratize mobile app development, particularly for young learners. Aptly integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) with App Inventor, enabling users to create apps using their natural language. User’s description is translated into a programming language that corresponds with App Inventor’s visual blocks. A preliminary study with high school students demonstrated the usability and potential of the platform. Prior programming experience influenced how users interact with Aptly. Participants identified areas for improvement and expressed a shift in perspective regarding programming accessibility and AI’s role in creative endeavors.
papers.summary_en: Aptly is a platform that combines a large language model with App Inventor to let users create mobile apps from natural language descriptions. It translates user input into a programming language for visual blocks, making app development accessible to beginners. A study with high school students showed its usability, with prior programming experience affecting interaction and participants gaining a new perspective on AI in creative tasks.
papers.summary_zh: Aptly是一个将大语言模型与App Inventor结合的平台，允许用户通过自然语言描述创建移动应用。它将用户输入转化为可视化块的编程语言，使应用开发对初学者更加友好。一项针对高中生的初步研究展示了其可用性，编程经验影响用户交互方式，参与者对AI在创意任务中的作用有了新认识。

papers.title: Talk to the Hand: an LLM-powered Chatbot with Visual Pointer as Proactive Companion for On-Screen Tasks
papers.short_title: Talk to the Hand: LLM Chatbot with Visual Pointer
papers.abstract: This paper presents Pointer Assistant, a novel human-AI interaction technique for on-screen tasks. The design features a chatbot displayed as an extra mouse pointer, alongside the user’s, which proactively gives feedback on user actions while directing them to relevant areas on the screen and responding to the user’s direct chat messages. The effectiveness of the design’s key characteristics, pointer form and proactivity, was investigated in a study involving 220 participants in a financial budget planning task. Results demonstrated that the pointer design and interaction reduced task load while improving satisfaction with the experience, and increased the number of budget categories ideated during the task compared to the traditional passive chat log design. Participants viewed Pointer Assistant as a fun, innovative, and helpful visual guide while noting that its assertiveness can be improved. Future developments could offer even further enhancements to the user experience of human-AI collaboration and task outcomes.
papers.summary_en: Pointer Assistant is a novel chatbot that appears as an extra mouse pointer on the screen, proactively guiding users through on-screen tasks by providing feedback and directing attention. A study with 220 participants showed that this pointer-based proactive design reduced task load, improved satisfaction, and increased idea generation compared to a traditional passive chat log. The system was perceived as fun and helpful, though its assertiveness could be improved, suggesting potential for enhancing human-AI collaboration in task-oriented interfaces.
papers.summary_zh: Pointer Assistant 是一种新型人机交互技术，以额外鼠标指针的形式呈现，主动为用户提供屏幕任务反馈并引导注意力。针对220名参与者的财务预算规划任务研究表明，与传统被动聊天记录相比，这种指针式主动设计降低了任务负荷、提升了满意度，并增加了预算类别的构思数量。用户认为该系统有趣、创新且实用，但指出其主动性有待加强，表明该技术有望提升面向任务的人机协作体验。

papers.title: IntentPrism: Human-AI Intent Manifestation for Web Information Foraging
papers.short_title: IntentPrism: Human-AI Intent for Web Foraging
papers.abstract: Intent-based User Interface (IBI) is an emerging topic in HCI about supporting user interaction with intelligent systems. We introduce IntentPrism, an approach to explicitly visualizing LLM-recognized user intents in a web information foraging task, in order to facilitate human-AI collaboration. Implemented as a web browser plug-in, IntentPrism provides real-time intent analysis from bookmarked web content, intent tree visualization and relevant content highlighting on webpages. It aims to support users in refining vague intentions, improving focus, and uncovering relevant content. The preliminary user study (n = 5) showed the promising potential of this approach in refining coarse-grained intents and improving efficiency especially when conducting in-depth exploration tasks. Additionally, user feedback highlights the demands for a multi-layered intent structure and a feedback mechanism for inaccurate highlights. Overall, IntentPrism represents a novel exploration of designing advanced intent-based user interfaces.
papers.summary_en: IntentPrism is a browser plug-in that visualizes user intents recognized by LLMs during web information foraging, helping users refine vague goals and improve focus. It provides real-time intent analysis, tree visualization, and content highlighting. A preliminary study with 5 users showed it enhances efficiency in deep exploration tasks, with feedback suggesting improvements like multi-layered intent structures and feedback mechanisms for inaccurate highlights. This work explores a novel approach to intent-based user interfaces for human-AI collaboration.
papers.summary_zh: IntentPrism是一个浏览器插件，通过可视化大语言模型识别的用户意图，帮助用户在网页信息搜寻中细化模糊目标并提升专注力。它提供实时意图分析、意图树可视化和相关内容高亮。初步用户研究（n=5）表明，该方法能提高深度探索任务的效率，用户反馈建议增加多层意图结构和错误高亮的反馈机制。该工作探索了面向人机协作的意图型用户界面新方法。

papers.title: GenieWizard: Multimodal App Feature Discovery with Large Language Models
papers.short_title: GenieWizard: Multimodal App Feature Discovery
papers.abstract: Multimodal interactions are more flexible, efficient, and adaptable than graphical interactions, allowing users to execute commands beyond simply tapping GUI buttons. However, the flexibility of multimodal commands makes it hard for designers to prototype and provide design specifications for developers. It is also hard for developers to anticipate what actions users may want. We present GenieWizard, a tool to aid developers in discovering potential features to implement in multimodal interfaces. GenieWizard supports user-desired command discovery early in the implementation process, streamlining the development process. GenieWizard uses an LLM to generate potential user interactions and parse these interactions into a form that can be used to discover the missing features for developers. Our evaluations showed that GenieWizard can reliably simulate user interactions and identify missing features. Also, in a study (N = 12), we demonstrated that developers using GenieWizard can identify and implement 42% of the missing features of multimodal apps compared to only 10% without GenieWizard.
papers.summary_en: GenieWizard is a tool that uses large language models to help developers discover and implement missing features in multimodal interfaces by simulating user interactions. It generates potential multimodal commands and identifies gaps in current app functionality, streamlining the development process. In evaluations, it reliably identified missing features, and a user study showed developers using GenieWizard implemented 42% of missing features versus 10% without it.
papers.summary_zh: GenieWizard 是一款利用大语言模型帮助开发者发现并实现多模态界面中缺失功能的工具，通过模拟用户交互来生成潜在的多模态指令并识别当前应用的功能缺口，从而简化开发流程。评估表明它能可靠地识别缺失功能，用户研究显示使用 GenieWizard 的开发者实现了 42% 的缺失功能，而未使用的开发者仅实现 10%。

papers.title: From Operation to Cognition: Automatic Modeling Cognitive Dependencies from User Demonstrations for GUI Task Automation
papers.short_title: CogDep: GUI Task Automation from Demos
papers.abstract: Traditional Programming by Demonstration (PBD) systems primarily automate tasks by recording and replaying operations on Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs), without fully considering the cognitive processes behind operations. This limits their ability to generalize tasks with interdependent operations to new contexts (e.g. collecting and summarizing introductions depending on different search keywords from varied websites). We propose TaskMind, a system that automatically identifies the semantics of operations, and the cognitive dependencies between operations from demonstrations, building a user-interpretable task graph. Users modify this graph to define new task goals, and TaskMind executes the graph to dynamically generalize new parameters for operations, with the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs). We compared TaskMind with a baseline end-to-end LLM which automates tasks from demonstrations and natural language commands, without task graph. In studies with 20 participants on both predefined and customized tasks, TaskMind significantly outperforms the baseline in both success rate and controllability.
papers.summary_en: TaskMind is a system that enhances Programming by Demonstration by automatically inferring cognitive dependencies between GUI operations from user demonstrations, building an interpretable task graph. It allows users to modify this graph to define new goals and uses Large Language Models to dynamically generalize parameters for operations. In user studies, TaskMind significantly outperformed an end-to-end LLM baseline in both success rate and controllability for GUI task automation.
papers.summary_zh: TaskMind是一个系统，通过从用户演示中自动推断GUI操作之间的认知依赖关系，构建可解释的任务图，从而增强编程演示。它允许用户修改该图以定义新目标，并利用大语言模型动态泛化操作参数。在用户研究中，TaskMind在GUI任务自动化的成功率和可控性上均显著优于端到端LLM基线。

papers.title: AppAgent: Multimodal Agents as Smartphone Users
papers.short_title: AppAgent: Multimodal Agents as Smartphone Users
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have led to the creation of intelligent agents capable of performing complex tasks. This paper introduces a novel LLM-based multimodal agent framework designed to operate smartphone applications. Our framework allows the agent to mimic human-like interactions such as tapping and swiping through a simplified action space, eliminating the need for system back-end access and enhancing its versatility across various apps. Central to the agent’s functionality is an innovative in-context learning method, where it either autonomously explores or learns from human demonstrations, creating a knowledge base used to execute complex tasks across diverse applications. We conducted extensive testing with our agent on over 50 tasks spanning 10 applications, ranging from social media to sophisticated image editing tools. Additionally, a user study confirmed the agent’s superior performance and practicality in handling a diverse array of high-level tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world settings. Our project page is available at https://appagent-official.github.io/.
papers.summary_en: This paper presents AppAgent, an LLM-based multimodal agent that can operate smartphone apps by mimicking human touch gestures like tapping and swiping, without needing system back-end access. The agent uses in-context learning to autonomously explore apps or learn from human demonstrations, building a knowledge base for executing complex tasks. Tested on over 50 tasks across 10 apps, including social media and image editing, it showed superior performance in a user study, demonstrating practical effectiveness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出AppAgent，一种基于大语言模型的多模态智能体，能够通过模拟点击、滑动等人类触控操作来使用智能手机应用，无需系统后端访问。该智能体采用上下文学习方法，自主探索应用或从人类演示中学习，构建知识库以执行复杂任务。在涵盖社交媒体和图像编辑等10个应用的50多项任务测试中，用户研究证实其性能优越且实用有效。

papers.title: Tap&Say: Touch Location-Informed Large Language Model for Multimodal Text Correction on Smartphones
papers.short_title: Tap&Say: Touch Location-Informed L...
papers.abstract: While voice input offers a convenient alternative to traditional text editing on mobile devices, practical implementations face two key challenges: 1) reliably distinguishing between editing commands and content dictation, and 2) effortlessly pinpointing the intended edit location. We propose Tap&Say, a novel multimodal system that combines touch interactions with Large Language Models (LLMs) for accurate text correction. By tapping near an error, users signal their edit intent and location, addressing both challenges. Then, the user speaks the correction text. Tap&Say utilizes the touch location, voice input, and existing text to generate contextually relevant correction suggestions. We propose a novel touch location-informed attention layer that integrates the tap location into the LLM’s attention mechanism, enabling it to utilize the tap location for text correction. We fine-tuned the touch location-informed LLM on synthetic touch locations and correction commands, achieving significantly higher correction accuracy than the state-of-the-art method VT [45]. A 16-person user study demonstrated that Tap&Say outperforms VT [45] with \(16.4\%\) shorter task completion time and \(47.5\%\) fewer keyboard clicks and is preferred by users.
papers.summary_en: Tap&Say is a multimodal system that combines touch input with large language models to improve voice-based text correction on smartphones. By tapping near an error, users indicate both the edit location and intent, then speak the correction. The system integrates tap location into the LLM's attention mechanism, achieving higher accuracy than prior methods and reducing task completion time by 16.4% and keyboard clicks by 47.5% in a user study.
papers.summary_zh: Tap&Say是一种结合触摸输入与大语言模型的多模态系统，用于改进智能手机上的语音文本纠错。用户通过点击错误附近来指示编辑位置和意图，然后说出修正内容。该系统将点击位置集成到大语言模型的注意力机制中，在用户研究中相比先前方法实现了更高的纠错准确率，并将任务完成时间缩短16.4%，键盘点击减少47.5%。

papers.title: Exploring Mobile Touch Interaction with Large Language Models
papers.short_title: Mobile Touch Interaction with LLMs
papers.abstract: Interacting with Large Language Models (LLMs) for text editing on mobile devices currently requires users to break out of their writing environment and switch to a conversational AI interface. In this paper, we propose to control the LLM via touch gestures performed directly on the text. We first chart a design space that covers fundamental touch input and text transformations. In this space, we then concretely explore two control mappings: spread-to-generate and pinch-to-shorten, with visual feedback loops. We evaluate this concept in a user study (N=14) that compares three feedback designs: no visualisation, text length indicator, and length + word indicator. The results demonstrate that touch-based control of LLMs is both feasible and user-friendly, with the length + word indicator proving most effective for managing text generation. This work lays the foundation for further research into gesture-based interaction with LLMs on touch devices.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a novel approach to interact with Large Language Models (LLMs) on mobile devices by using touch gestures directly on text, such as spread-to-generate and pinch-to-shorten. The authors design a design space for touch input and text transformations, and evaluate three visual feedback designs in a user study. Results show that touch-based LLM control is feasible and user-friendly, with the length+word indicator being most effective. This work lays the foundation for gesture-based LLM interaction on touch devices.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种在移动设备上通过触摸手势直接与大型语言模型（LLM）交互的新方法，例如展开生成和捏合缩短。作者设计了触摸输入和文本转换的设计空间，并通过用户研究评估了三种视觉反馈设计。结果表明，基于触摸的LLM控制是可行且用户友好的，其中长度+单词指示器最为有效。这项工作为触摸设备上基于手势的LLM交互奠定了基础。

papers.title: "Having Lunch Now": Understanding How Users Engage with a Proactive Agent for Daily Planning and Self-Reflection
papers.short_title: "Having Lunch Now": Understa...
papers.abstract: Conversational agents have been studied as tools to scaffold planning and self-reflection for productivity and well-being. While prior work has demonstrated positive outcomes, we still lack a clear understanding of what drives these results and how users behave and communicate with agents that act as coaches rather than assistants. Such understanding is critical for designing interactions in which agents foster meaningful behavioral change. We conducted a 14-day longitudinal study with 12 participants using a proactive agent that initiated regular check-ins to support daily planning and reflection. Our findings reveal diverse interaction patterns: participants accepted or negotiated suggestions, developed shared mental models, reported progress, and at times resisted or disengaged. We also identified problematic aspects of the agent’s behavior, including rigidity, premature turn-taking, and overpromising. Our work contributes to understanding how people interact with a proactive, coach-like agent and offers design considerations for facilitating effective behavioral change.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how users interact with a proactive conversational agent designed as a coach for daily planning and self-reflection. Through a 14-day study with 12 participants, the authors identify diverse interaction patterns such as acceptance, negotiation, resistance, and disengagement, as well as problematic agent behaviors like rigidity and premature turn-taking. The findings provide insights into user behavior with coach-like agents and offer design considerations for fostering effective behavioral change.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了用户如何与一个旨在作为日常规划和自我反思教练的主动式对话代理进行互动。通过一项为期14天、涉及12名参与者的纵向研究，作者识别出多样化的互动模式，如接受、协商、抵抗和脱离，以及代理行为中的问题，如僵化和过早轮换。研究结果揭示了用户与教练式代理的互动行为，并为促进有效行为改变提供了设计考量。

papers.title: DroidRetriever: A Transparent and Steerable Automation System for Collaborative Mobile Information Seeking
papers.short_title: DroidRetriever: Collaborative Mobile Info Seeking
papers.abstract: Information seeking on mobile devices is often fragmented, trapping users in repetitive cycles of context switching and data re-entry, which increases cognitive load and disrupts workflow. Existing mobile agents provide limited cross-source integration and are largely opaque, presenting progress as a linear feed with few opportunities to intervene, steer, or take control. We present DroidRetriever, a transparent, steerable system for cross-source mobile information seeking. It accepts voice or typed input and the multi-LLM system decomposes the task, navigates to target pages, takes screenshots, and synthesizes a concise report with citation-linked screenshots. We make the process transparent through a progress dashboard combining sub-task progress and real-time exploration maps for seamless takeover. DroidRetriever also pauses on detected privacy or high-risk screens and prompts intervention. Across 35 tasks over 24 apps, experiments and user studies demonstrate improvements in coverage, transparency, and reduced workload. We release our code at https://github.com/AkimotoAyako/DroidRetriever.
papers.summary_en: DroidRetriever is a transparent and steerable mobile automation system that uses multiple LLMs to decompose complex information-seeking tasks, navigate across apps, and generate citation-linked reports. It features a progress dashboard with real-time exploration maps for user oversight and intervention, and pauses on privacy-sensitive screens. Experiments across 35 tasks show improved coverage, transparency, and reduced cognitive load compared to existing opaque agents.
papers.summary_zh: DroidRetriever是一个透明且可操控的移动自动化系统，利用多个大语言模型分解复杂的信息检索任务，跨应用导航并生成带引用的报告。它通过进度仪表盘和实时探索地图提供用户监督与干预能力，并在检测到隐私敏感界面时暂停。在35个任务上的实验表明，与现有不透明代理相比，该系统在覆盖率、透明度和降低认知负荷方面均有提升。

papers.title: Measuring the Semantic Accessibility Gap in LLM-Generated Web UIs
papers.short_title: Semantic Accessibility Gap in LLM Web UIs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models are increasingly used to generate web interfaces from natural language specifications. Automated accessibility tools evaluate these interfaces by detecting syntactic violations such as missing attributes, but cannot assess whether accessibility content is actually meaningful—an image with alt=“image” passes every check yet conveys nothing to screen reader users. We investigate the prevalence of such semantic accessibility violations in LLM-generated interfaces. Analyzing 300 UIs produced by three commercial models, we identify 541 semantic violations across six fault types. We validate an LLM-as-judge approach through controlled fault injection, achieving recall rates of 80–92%, and triangulate with a preliminary human annotation study. Our findings suggest that LLM judges can extend accessibility evaluation into the semantic dimension that automated tools miss, opening opportunities for their integration as reward signals in accessibility-aware development workflows.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a 'semantic accessibility gap' in LLM-generated web UIs, where automated tools miss meaningless alt text like 'image'. Analyzing 300 UIs from three models, the authors find 541 semantic violations across six types. They validate an LLM-as-judge approach with 80–92% recall, showing it can detect these issues and serve as a reward signal for accessibility-aware development.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了LLM生成的网页界面中存在‘语义可访问性鸿沟’，即自动工具无法检测到如‘image’这类无意义的替代文本。通过分析三个模型的300个界面，作者发现了541个语义违规，涵盖六种类型。他们验证了LLM作为评判者的方法，召回率达80–92%，表明该方法能检测这些问题，并可作为可访问性感知开发中的奖励信号。

papers.title: WebUI-95: A Large-Scale Dataset of Normalized Web Interfaces via UI-to-Code Generation
papers.short_title: WebUI-95: Normalized Web Interfaces Dataset
papers.abstract: Large-scale web UI datasets are essential resources for training and evaluating machine learning models in user interface research, yet real-world web scraping produces data consisting of framework boilerplate, build artifacts, and deeply nested elements, resulting from software engineering practices. These complexities conflict with learning design patterns and complicate code understanding and manipulation. Recent advances in vision-language modelling and verifiable reward have enabled a new generation of UI-to-code systems that produce high-fidelity reproductions of web interfaces from screenshots. In this work, we apply a state-of-the-art UI-to-code model to the WebUI dataset. Our analysis shows that this transformation achieves 94% visual fidelity (mean UIClip cosine similarity of 0.938) while reducing code size by approximately 95% and improving predicted visual quality. We release the dataset and generation pipeline to support research in layout modeling, code generation, and design research.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces WebUI-95, a large-scale dataset of normalized web interfaces created by applying a state-of-the-art UI-to-code model to the existing WebUI dataset. The transformation achieves 94% visual fidelity while reducing code size by 95%, removing framework boilerplate and build artifacts to produce clean, standalone HTML/CSS code. The dataset and generation pipeline are released to support research in layout modeling, code generation, and design research.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了WebUI-95，一个大规模标准化网页界面数据集，通过将最先进的UI-to-code模型应用于现有WebUI数据集构建而成。该转换在实现94%视觉保真度的同时，将代码体积减少约95%，去除了框架模板和构建产物，生成简洁独立的HTML/CSS代码。数据集及生成流程已开源，以支持布局建模、代码生成和设计研究等领域的研究。

papers.title: Design System-Compliant User Interface Generation with LLM Agents: A Comparative Study of Context Engineering Strategies
papers.short_title: Design System UI Generation: Context Engineering
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used for user interface (UI) generation, yet they often fail to apply organization-specific design systems. It remains unclear which context engineering strategy enables dependable compliance. This study compares three context engineering strategies for integrating design systems into LLM agents: instruction-based (embedding complete style guides in prompts), context-based (injecting task-relevant style guides into the context window), and registry-based (assembling pre-built components in the registry). We evaluate each strategy on compliance rate, task completion time, and token usage by generating six real-world UIs. Results show that the registry-based strategy achieved the highest compliance rate (95.08%), outperforming others with only moderate overhead. Our pilot study with nine practitioners further indicates reduced perceived difficulty and time burden while enhancing self-efficacy in their workflows. These findings demonstrate that using pre-built components in the registry enables more reliable and scalable design system-compliant UI generation with LLM agents.
papers.summary_en: This paper compares three strategies for integrating design systems into LLM-based UI generation: instruction-based, context-based, and registry-based. The registry-based strategy, which uses pre-built components, achieves the highest compliance rate (95.08%) with moderate overhead. A pilot study with practitioners shows it reduces perceived difficulty and time burden while improving self-efficacy. The findings suggest that using pre-built components enables more reliable and scalable design system-compliant UI generation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文比较了三种将设计系统集成到基于LLM的UI生成中的策略：基于指令、基于上下文和基于注册表。基于注册表的策略使用预构建组件，以适中的开销实现了最高的合规率（95.08%）。一项与从业者的初步研究表明，该策略降低了感知难度和时间负担，同时提高了自我效能。研究结果表明，使用预构建组件能够实现更可靠、可扩展的符合设计系统的UI生成。

papers.title: From Struggle to Success: Context-Aware Guidance for Screen Reader Users in Computer Use
papers.short_title: Context-Aware Guidance for Screen Reader Users
papers.abstract: Equal access to digital technologies is critical for education, employment, and social participation. However, mainstream interfaces are visually oriented, creating steep learning curves and frequent obstacles for screen reader users, and limiting their independence and opportunities. Existing support is inadequate—tutorials mainly target sighted users, while human assistance lacks real-time availability. We introduce AskEase, an on-demand AI assistant that provides step-by-step, screen reader user-friendly guidance for computer use. AskEase manages multiple sources of context to infer user intent and deliver precise, situation-specific guidance. Its seamless interaction design minimizes disruption and reduces the effort of seeking help. We demonstrated its effectiveness through representative usage scenarios and robustness tests. In a within-subjects study with 12 screen reader users, AskEase significantly improved task success while reducing perceived workload, including physical demand, effort, and frustration. These results demonstrate the potential of LLM-powered assistants to promote accessible computing and expand opportunities for users with visual impairments.
papers.summary_en: This paper presents AskEase, an on-demand AI assistant that provides real-time, step-by-step guidance for screen reader users navigating visually-oriented computer interfaces. By integrating multiple context sources to infer user intent, AskEase delivers precise, situation-specific instructions with minimal disruption. A within-subjects study with 12 screen reader users showed that AskEase significantly improved task success rates and reduced perceived workload, including physical demand, effort, and frustration. The work demonstrates the potential of LLM-powered assistants to enhance digital accessibility for visually impaired users.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出AskEase，一种按需AI助手，为屏幕阅读器用户在使用视觉导向的计算机界面时提供实时、分步指导。通过整合多种上下文来源推断用户意图，AskEase以最小干扰提供精确、情境化的指令。一项包含12名屏幕阅读器用户的被试内研究表明，AskEase显著提高了任务成功率，并降低了感知工作负荷，包括身体需求、努力和挫败感。该工作展示了基于大语言模型的助手在增强视障用户数字可访问性方面的潜力。

papers.title: Toward Personalized Proactive Agents on Smart Glasses: From Explicit Context Policies to Implicit User Differences
papers.short_title: Personalized Proactive Agents on Smart Glasses
papers.abstract: Smart glasses are envisioned as proactive agents that deliver context-aware assistance by anticipating users’ latent needs. However, current systems often overlook individual differences in how users perceive proactive behaviors, leading to perceived invasiveness for some users. This poster explores how personalization can address these challenges, considering both explicit policy specification and implicit preference extraction. We conducted seven workshops, encouraging participants to construct personalized contexts from shared probes, articulate multimodal cues that determine when proactive behaviors should be triggered, and express their feelings. We developed a taxonomy revealing that users construct personalization policies at varying levels of abstraction, from semantic descriptions to sensor-level cues. We also identified which individual differences, including utility-emotion orientations and autonomy preferences, lead to divergent perceptions of the same proactive behaviors. We discuss implications for designing language-based personalization interfaces, call for adaptive user modeling, and offer design considerations for personalized proactive agents on smart glasses.
papers.summary_en: This paper explores personalization for proactive smart glasses, addressing individual differences in user perceptions of proactive behaviors. Through workshops, the authors developed a taxonomy of personalization policies at varying abstraction levels and identified key individual differences, such as utility-emotion orientations and autonomy preferences, that affect user acceptance. They propose design implications for language-based personalization interfaces and adaptive user modeling to reduce perceived invasiveness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了智能眼镜主动式助手的个性化问题，针对用户对主动行为感知的个体差异。通过工作坊，作者构建了不同抽象层次的个性化策略分类体系，并识别出效用-情感取向和自主性偏好等关键个体差异如何影响用户接受度。他们提出了基于语言的个性化界面和自适应用户建模的设计启示，以降低感知侵入性。

papers.title: GuideMe: A VLM-Based System Assisting Independent Smartphone Learning for Older Adults
papers.short_title: GuideMe: VLM for Older Adults' Smartphone Learning
papers.abstract: Due to age-related cognitive and physical decline, older adults face numerous difficulties when learning new functions of smartphone applications. However, older adults often struggle to ask questions clearly and follow instructions independently. Through a formative study (N=16), we identified the behaviors and challenges of older adults seeking help independently and analyzed the effective mechanism of in-person instruction. Based on these findings, we proposed GuideMe, an in-situ conversational instruction system for older adults’ application learning. GuideMe utilizes Vision-Language-Models to analyze multimodal context in users’ situations, then assists users in confirming their intentions by asking clarifying questions, and finally provides step-by-step instructions using in-situ highlight and deictic gestures. We conducted a user study (N=18) that demonstrated that GuideMe significantly reduced users’ cognitive load during learning, helped them ask questions and follow instructions efficiently, and achieved performance comparable to that of in-person instruction.
papers.summary_en: GuideMe is a smartphone learning assistant for older adults that uses Vision-Language Models to understand users' on-screen context and provide step-by-step instructions with visual highlights and gestures. It addresses the challenges older adults face in asking questions and following instructions independently. A user study showed GuideMe reduces cognitive load and achieves performance comparable to in-person instruction.
papers.summary_zh: GuideMe是一款面向老年人智能手机学习的辅助系统，利用视觉语言模型理解用户的屏幕上下文，并通过视觉高亮和手势提供逐步指导。它解决了老年人在独立提问和遵循指令方面的困难。用户研究表明，GuideMe能降低认知负荷，并达到与真人指导相当的效果。

papers.title: Cocoa: Co-Planning and Co-Execution with AI Agents
papers.short_title: Cocoa: Co-Planning and Co-Execution with AI Agents
papers.abstract: As AI agents take on increasingly long-running tasks involving sophisticated planning and execution, there is a corresponding need for novel interaction designs that enable deeper human-agent collaboration. However, most prior works leverage human interaction to fix “autonomous” workflows that have yet to become fully autonomous or rigidly treat planning and execution as separate stages. Based on a formative study with 9 researchers using AI to support their work, we propose a design that affords greater flexibility in collaboration, so that users can 1) delegate agency to the user or agent via a collaborative plan where individual steps can be assigned; and 2) interleave planning and execution so that plans can adjust after partial execution. We introduce Cocoa, a system that takes design inspiration from computational notebooks to support complex research tasks. A lab study (n = 16) found that Cocoa enabled steerability without sacrificing ease-of-use, and a week-long field deployment (n = 7) showed how researchers collaborated with Cocoa to accomplish real-world tasks.
papers.summary_en: Cocoa is a system that enhances human-AI collaboration by allowing users to co-plan and co-execute tasks with AI agents, enabling flexible delegation of steps and interleaving of planning and execution. Inspired by computational notebooks, it supports complex research tasks and was validated through a lab study and field deployment, showing improved steerability and ease of use.
papers.summary_zh: Cocoa是一个增强人机协作的系统，允许用户与AI代理共同规划和执行任务，支持灵活分配步骤以及规划与执行的交错进行。受计算笔记本启发，它支持复杂研究任务，并通过实验室研究和实地部署验证，展示了更好的可控性和易用性。

papers.title: SeekUI: Predicting Visual Search Behavior on Graphical User Interfaces with a Reward-Augmented Vision Language Model
papers.short_title: SeekUI: Reward-Augmented VLM for GUI Search
papers.abstract: Visual search is key to understanding and improving interaction with graphical user interfaces (GUIs), yet predicting scanpaths on real GUIs remains an open challenge. Unlike free-viewing, visual search is goal-driven and shaped by both linguistic and visual features of the GUI. State-of-the-art models of visual search, trained on natural images, fail with GUIs because they cannot capture the effects of grouping and semantics on search strategies. We present SeekUI, a reward-augmented Vision Language Model (VLM) that predicts scanpaths directly from a GUI screenshot and a text cue describing the desired target. Our model extends the capability of VLMs to reproduce human-like visual search behavior on GUIs and outperforms baseline models across different types of GUIs. Importantly, it reproduces key empirical phenomena established in eye-tracking studies of visual search, including the Guess–Scan–Confirm strategy. In sum, SeekUI provides a foundation for predicting visual search behavior and has potential for informing GUI evaluation and optimization.
papers.summary_en: SeekUI is a reward-augmented vision-language model that predicts human visual search behavior on graphical user interfaces (GUIs) from a screenshot and a text cue. It outperforms existing models by capturing GUI-specific grouping and semantics, and reproduces key eye-tracking phenomena like the Guess-Scan-Confirm strategy. This work provides a foundation for predicting GUI search behavior, with applications in GUI evaluation and optimization.
papers.summary_zh: SeekUI是一种奖励增强的视觉语言模型，能够根据GUI截图和文本提示预测人类在图形用户界面上的视觉搜索行为。它通过捕捉GUI特有的分组和语义信息，优于现有模型，并复现了关键的眼动追踪现象，如“猜测-扫描-确认”策略。该工作为预测GUI搜索行为奠定了基础，可用于GUI评估与优化。

papers.title: Facilitating Proactive and Reactive Guidance for Decision Making on the Web: A Design Probe with WebSeek
papers.short_title: WebSeek: Proactive & Reactive Web Decision Guidance
papers.abstract: Web AI agents such as ChatGPT Agent and GenSpark are increasingly used for routine web-based tasks, yet they still rely on text-based input prompts, lack proactive detection of user intent, and offer no support for interactive data analysis and decision making. We present WebSeek, a mixed-initiative browser extension that enables users to discover and extract information from webpages to then flexibly build, transform, and refine tangible data artifacts–such as tables, lists, and visualizations–all within an interactive canvas. Within this environment, users can perform analysis–including data transformations such as joining tables or creating visualizations–while an in-built AI both proactively offers context-aware guidance and automation, and reactively responds to explicit user requests. An exploratory user study (N=15) with WebSeek as a probe reveals participants’ diverse analysis strategies, underscoring their desire for transparency and control during human-AI collaboration.
papers.summary_en: WebSeek is a mixed-initiative browser extension that helps users extract, transform, and analyze web data within an interactive canvas, combining proactive AI guidance with reactive responses to user requests. A user study shows that participants value transparency and control when collaborating with the AI, revealing diverse analysis strategies.
papers.summary_zh: WebSeek 是一个混合主动的浏览器扩展，帮助用户在交互式画布中提取、转换和分析网页数据，结合了主动的 AI 引导和对用户请求的被动响应。用户研究显示，参与者在与 AI 协作时重视透明度和控制权，并展现了多样化的分析策略。

papers.title: Orca: Browsing at Scale Through User-Driven and AI-Facilitated Orchestration Across Malleable Webpages
papers.short_title: Orca: AI-Facilitated Browsing at Scale
papers.abstract: Web-based activities span multiple webpages. However, conventional browsers with stacks of tabs cannot support operating and synthesizing large volumes of information across pages. While recent AI systems enable fully automated web browsing and information synthesis, they often diminish user agency and hinder contextual understanding. We explore how AI could instead augment user interactions with content across webpages and mitigate cognitive and manual efforts. Through literature on information tasks and web browsing challenges, and an iterative design process, we present novel interactions with our prototype web browser, Orca. Leveraging AI, Orca supports user-driven exploration, operation, organization, and synthesis of web content at scale. To enable browsing at scale, webpages are treated as malleable materials that humans and AI can collaboratively manipulate and compose into a malleable, dynamic, and browser-level workspace. Our evaluation revealed an increased “appetite” for information foraging, enhanced control, and more flexible sensemaking across a broader web information landscape.
papers.summary_en: Orca is a prototype web browser that uses AI to augment user-driven browsing across multiple webpages, treating pages as malleable materials for collaborative manipulation. It supports exploration, organization, and synthesis of web content at scale, reducing cognitive load while preserving user agency. Evaluation showed increased information foraging, enhanced control, and more flexible sensemaking.
papers.summary_zh: Orca 是一个原型网页浏览器，利用AI增强用户在多页面间的浏览，将网页视为可塑材料进行人机协作操作。它支持大规模网页内容的探索、组织和综合，减轻认知负担同时保持用户自主性。评估表明，用户信息觅食行为增加，控制感增强，并在更广泛的网络信息环境中实现了更灵活的意义建构。

papers.title: "Here, Let Me Help": An Empirical Study of User Interventions in Human-Web Agent Collaboration
papers.short_title: "Here, Let Me Help": An Empi...
papers.abstract: Web agents aim to execute complex online tasks from high-level instructions, yet fully autonomous execution remains challenging in practice. We present an empirical study of user interventions in human–web agent collaboration, moving beyond outcome-based metrics to examine how interventions unfold during execution. We conducted a controlled in-lab study with 30 participants whose interactions reflected early-stage web agent adoption across 12 structured tasks in shopping, travel, and information-seeking domains using live websites. Analyzing interaction logs, user inputs, and screen recordings, we identify diverse behaviors and propose a taxonomy capturing both the reasons for intervention and the forms they take. We distinguish explicit interventions, where users halt or override actions, from implicit interventions, where users guide or prepare the environment without stopping execution. Our findings reveal how task structure and execution breakdowns shape intervention behaviors to provide process-level evidence for designing web agents that better support users as active collaborators.
papers.summary_en: This paper presents an empirical study of how users intervene when collaborating with web agents on complex online tasks. Through a controlled lab study with 30 participants, the authors develop a taxonomy of interventions, distinguishing between explicit (halting or overriding actions) and implicit (guiding without stopping execution) types. The findings reveal how task structure and execution breakdowns shape intervention behaviors, providing process-level insights for designing web agents that better support users as active collaborators.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过实证研究探讨了用户在与网络代理协作完成复杂在线任务时的干预行为。基于30名参与者的受控实验室研究，作者提出了干预行为的分类体系，区分了显式干预（暂停或覆盖操作）和隐式干预（在不停止执行的情况下引导或准备环境）。研究揭示了任务结构和执行故障如何影响干预行为，为设计更好支持用户作为主动协作者的网络代理提供了过程层面的见解。

papers.title: Your Permission Leaks My Data: Second-Hand Privacy Harms in LLM Agents
papers.short_title: Second-Hand Privacy Harms in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based personal agents are becoming everyday tools, helping users manage messages, email, calendars, and documents. As these agents gain broader permissions, they not only process the user’s information but also access sensitive traces about friends, colleagues, and family in communication. This creates second-hand privacy harm: a user’s permissions enable unintended inference about non-consenting third parties. We study this externality under a permission-scoped inference setting and introduce second-hand privacy (2HP), an evidence-grounded metric that quantifies leakage using prediction accuracy, model confidence, and cited traces, with sensitivity-weighted attributes and penalties for unsupported claims. To avoid auditing real corpora, we evaluate 2HP in an LLM-simulated multi-channel ecosystem and test all permission subsets. Results show that exposure depends on which channels are granted, not how many, and cross-channel access amplifies leakage via evidence stitching. These findings position permission design as a key lever for reducing relational exposure in personal agent ecosystems.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies and formalizes second-hand privacy harms in LLM-based personal agents, where a user's permissions enable unintended inference about non-consenting third parties. The authors propose a metric called 2HP to quantify such leakage using prediction accuracy, model confidence, and cited traces. Through simulations, they show that exposure depends on which channels are granted, not how many, and cross-channel access amplifies leakage via evidence stitching. The work positions permission design as a key lever for reducing relational exposure in personal agent ecosystems.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别并形式化了基于LLM的个人代理中的二手隐私危害，即用户的权限使得对未同意的第三方进行非预期的推断成为可能。作者提出了一个名为2HP的指标，利用预测准确性、模型置信度和引用的痕迹来量化此类泄露。通过模拟实验，他们发现暴露程度取决于授予哪些渠道而非数量，且跨渠道访问通过证据拼接放大了泄露。该工作将权限设计定位为减少个人代理生态系统中关系暴露的关键杠杆。

papers.title: GhostUI: Unveiling Hidden Interactions in Mobile UI
papers.short_title: GhostUI: Hidden Interactions in Mobile UI
papers.abstract: Modern mobile applications rely on hidden interactions—gestures without visual cues like long presses and swipes—to provide functionality without cluttering interfaces. While experienced users may discover these interactions through prior use or onboarding tutorials, their implicit nature makes them difficult for most users to uncover. Similarly, mobile agents—systems designed to automate tasks on mobile user interfaces, powered by vision language models (VLMs)—struggle to detect veiled interactions or determine actions for completing tasks. To address this challenge, we present GhostUI, a new dataset designed to enable the detection of hidden interactions in mobile applications. GhostUI provides before-and-after screenshots, simplified view hierarchies, gesture metadata, and task descriptions, allowing VLMs to better recognize concealed gestures and anticipate post-interaction states. Quantitative evaluations with VLMs show that models fine-tuned on GhostUI outperform baseline VLMs, particularly in predicting hidden interactions and inferring post-interaction screens, underscoring GhostUI’s potential as a foundation for advancing mobile task automation.
papers.summary_en: GhostUI is a dataset that helps vision-language models detect hidden mobile interactions like long presses and swipes, which lack visual cues. It provides before-and-after screenshots, view hierarchies, gesture metadata, and task descriptions. Fine-tuning VLMs on GhostUI improves their ability to predict these interactions and infer resulting screen states, advancing mobile task automation.
papers.summary_zh: GhostUI是一个数据集，旨在帮助视觉语言模型检测移动应用中缺乏视觉提示的隐藏交互（如长按和滑动）。它提供了操作前后的截图、简化视图层级、手势元数据和任务描述。在GhostUI上微调的VLM在预测隐藏交互和推断操作后屏幕状态方面优于基线模型，推动了移动任务自动化的发展。

papers.title: Automating UI Optimization through Multi-Agentic Reasoning
