papers.short_title: Multi-Agentic UI Optimization
papers.abstract: We present AutoOptimization, a novel multi-objective optimization framework for adapting user interfaces. From a user’s verbal preferences for changing a UI, our framework guides a prioritization-based Pareto frontier search over candidate layouts. It selects suitable objective functions for UI placement while simultaneously parameterizing them according to the user’s instructions to define the optimization problem. A solver then generates a series of optimal UI layouts, which our framework validates against the user’s instructions to adapt the UI with the final solution. Our approach thus overcomes the previous need for manual inspection of layouts and the use of population averages for objective parameters. We integrate multiple agents sequentially within our framework, enabling the system to leverage their reasoning capabilities to interpret user preferences, configure the optimization problem, and validate optimization outcomes. We evaluate each step of our framework inside a Mixed Reality use case and demonstrate that AutoOptimization effectively increases the usability of UI adaptation schemes.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces AutoOptimization, a framework that automates UI adaptation by interpreting user verbal preferences, configuring multi-objective optimization problems, and generating optimal layouts through a Pareto frontier search. It uses multiple AI agents to reason about user instructions, set objective parameters, and validate outcomes, eliminating the need for manual layout inspection or population-based averages. Evaluated in a Mixed Reality context, the framework improves the usability of UI adaptation by producing tailored, optimized interfaces.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了AutoOptimization框架，通过解析用户的口头偏好，自动配置多目标优化问题，并利用帕累托前沿搜索生成最优界面布局。该框架集成多个AI智能体，分别负责理解用户指令、设定目标参数和验证优化结果，从而避免了人工检查布局或依赖群体平均值的需求。在混合现实场景中的评估表明，该框架能有效提升界面自适应方案的可用性。

papers.title: KeySense: LLM-Powered Hands-Down, Ten-Finger Typing on Commodity Touchscreens
papers.short_title: KeySense: LLM-Powered Ten-Finger Typing
papers.abstract: Existing touchscreen software keyboards prevent users from resting their hands, forcing slow and fatiguing index-finger tapping (“chicken typing”) instead of familiar hands-down ten-finger typing. We present KeySense, a purely software solution that preserves physical keyboard motor skills. KeySense isolates intentional taps from resting-finger noise with cognitive–motor timing patterns, and then uses a fine-tuned LLM decoder to turn the resulting noisy letter sequence into the intended word. In controlled component tests, this decoder substantially outperforms 2 statistical baselines (top-1 accuracy 84.8% vs 75.7% and 79.3%). A 12-participant study shows clear ergonomic and performance benefits: compared with the conventional hover-style keyboard, users rated KeySense as markedly less physically demanding (NASA-TLX median 1.5 vs 4.0), and after brief practice, typed significantly faster (WPM 28.3 vs 26.2, p <0.01). These results indicate that KeySense enables accurate, efficient and comfortable ten-finger text entry on commodity touchscreens, without any extra hardware.
papers.summary_en: KeySense is a software-only system that enables hands-down, ten-finger typing on commodity touchscreens by using cognitive-motor timing patterns to distinguish intentional taps from resting-finger noise, and a fine-tuned LLM decoder to correct noisy input. In experiments, it achieved 84.8% top-1 accuracy, outperforming statistical baselines, and in a user study, it reduced physical demand (NASA-TLX median 1.5 vs 4.0) and improved typing speed (28.3 vs 26.2 WPM) compared to conventional hover-style keyboards.
papers.summary_zh: KeySense 是一个纯软件系统，通过利用认知-运动时序模式区分有意敲击与手指静置噪声，并使用微调的大语言模型解码器纠正含噪输入，从而在商用触摸屏上实现双手十指打字。实验表明，其 top-1 准确率达 84.8%，优于统计基线；用户研究中，与传统悬停式键盘相比，KeySense 显著降低了体力需求（NASA-TLX 中位数 1.5 vs 4.0）并提升了打字速度（28.3 vs 26.2 WPM）。

papers.title: As Content and Layout Co-Evolve: TangibleSite for Scaffolding Blind People's Webpage Design through Multimodal Interaction
papers.short_title: As Content and Layout Co-Evolve: Tangi...
papers.abstract: Creating webpages requires generating content and arranging layout while iteratively refining both to achieve a coherent design, a process that can be challenging for blind individuals. To understand how blind designers navigate this process, we conducted two rounds of co-design sessions with blind participants, using design probes to elicit their strategies and support needs. Our findings reveal a preference for content and layout to co-evolve, but this process requires external support through cues that situate local elements within the broader page structure as well as multimodal interactions. Building on these insights, we developed TangibleSite, an accessible web design tool that provides real-time multimodal feedback through tangible, auditory, and speech-based interactions. TangibleSite enables blind individuals to create, edit, and reposition webpage elements while integrating content and layout decisions. A formative evaluation with six blind participants demonstrated that TangibleSite enabled independent webpage creation, supported refinement across content and layout, and reduced barriers to achieving visually consistent designs.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces TangibleSite, an accessible web design tool that supports blind people in creating webpages through multimodal interaction. Based on co-design sessions revealing that blind designers prefer content and layout to co-evolve, the tool provides real-time tangible, auditory, and speech feedback to scaffold this process. A formative evaluation showed that TangibleSite enables independent webpage creation, facilitates iterative refinement of both content and layout, and reduces barriers to achieving visually consistent designs.
papers.summary_zh: 本文介绍了TangibleSite，一个通过多模态交互支持盲人创建网页的可访问设计工具。基于协同设计会话发现盲人设计师偏好内容与布局共同演化，该工具通过实时触觉、听觉和语音反馈来支撑这一过程。形成性评估表明，TangibleSite能够实现独立网页创建，促进内容与布局的迭代优化，并降低实现视觉一致设计的障碍。

papers.title: Crepe: A Mobile Screen Data Collector Using Graph Query
papers.short_title: Crepe: Mobile Screen Data Collector via Graph Query
papers.abstract: Collecting mobile screen information datasets remains challenging for academic researchers. Commercial organizations often have exclusive access to mobile data, leading to a “data monopoly” that restricts academic research and user transparency. Existing open-source mobile data collection frameworks primarily focus on mobile sensing data rather than screen content. We present Crepe, a no-code Android app that enables researchers to collect information displayed on screen through simple demonstrations of target data. Crepe utilizes a novel Graph Query technique, which augments mobile UI structures to support flexible identification, location, and collection of specific data pieces. The tool emphasizes participants’ privacy and agency by providing full transparency over collected data and allowing easy opt-out. We designed and built Crepe for research purposes only and in scenarios where researchers obtain explicit consent from participants. Code for Crepe will be open-sourced to support future academic research data collection.
papers.summary_en: Crepe is a no-code Android app that allows researchers to collect screen content data via simple demonstrations, using a novel Graph Query technique to flexibly identify and extract specific information from mobile UI structures. It addresses the data monopoly issue by providing an open-source tool that prioritizes participant privacy and transparency, enabling opt-out and explicit consent. The tool is designed for academic research, aiming to democratize access to mobile screen data.
papers.summary_zh: Crepe是一款无代码的Android应用，允许研究人员通过简单演示来收集屏幕内容数据，利用新颖的图查询技术灵活识别和提取移动UI结构中的特定信息。它通过提供开源工具，优先考虑参与者隐私和透明度，支持退出和明确同意，从而解决数据垄断问题。该工具专为学术研究设计，旨在使移动屏幕数据的获取更加民主化。

papers.title: Agent A/B: Automated and Scalable A/B Testing on Live Websites with Interactive LLM Agents
papers.short_title: Agent A/B: LLM A/B Testing on Live Websites
papers.abstract: A/B testing is central to UI/UX design, yet our formative study with six industry practitioners revealed that it is slowed by scarce user traffic, long runtimes, and high operational costs. To address these challenges, we introduce Agent A/B, an end-to-end system that deploys large language model (LLM) agents with structured personas to interact with live webpages and generate scalable behavioral evidence before launch. In a case study on Amazon.com, Agent A/B simulated a between-subjects A/B test of filter panel designs with 1,000 agents and found that the reduced filter list produced more purchases, reproducing directional outcomes also observed in a parallel large-scale human experiment. Results further suggest that agent-based simulations can detect interface-sensitive behavioral differences and surface subgroup patterns while offering faster, lower-risk insights. We position Agent A/B as a complement to human testing, enabling earlier prototyping, pre-deployment validation, and hypothesis-driven UX evaluation. We will release our code upon paper acceptance.
papers.summary_en: Agent A/B is an end-to-end system that uses LLM agents with structured personas to simulate A/B tests on live websites, addressing the high costs and slow pace of traditional human testing. In a case study on Amazon.com, it reproduced the directional outcomes of a large-scale human experiment with 1,000 agents, detecting interface-sensitive behavioral differences and subgroup patterns. The system enables faster, lower-risk pre-deployment validation and hypothesis-driven UX evaluation, serving as a complement to human testing.
papers.summary_zh: Agent A/B是一个端到端系统，利用具有结构化角色的大语言模型代理在真实网站上模拟A/B测试，以解决传统人工测试成本高、速度慢的问题。在亚马逊网站的案例研究中，该系统使用1000个代理复现了大规模人类实验的方向性结果，检测到界面敏感的行为差异和子群体模式。该系统能够实现更快、风险更低的部署前验证和假设驱动的用户体验评估，作为人工测试的补充。

papers.title: Improving Data Quality via Pre-Task Participant Screening in Crowdsourced GUI Experiments
papers.short_title: Pre-Task Screening for Crowdsourced GUI Experiments

papers.title: IntentWeave: A Progressive Entry Ladder for Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals
papers.short_title: IntentWeave: Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals

papers.title: A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents
papers.short_title: A11y-CUA: Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents

papers.title: WebPerceptor: An Open Source Chromium Plugin for Real-Time LLM-Based In-Line, In-Browser Re-Writing of Website Content
papers.short_title: WebPerceptor: LLM In-Browser Re-Writing
papers.abstract: We introduce the "AI Mediated Web", an automatic, personalised, in-line, real-time remixing of web content by an LLM based on given prompts and presented in-browser such that the user perceives the end result as a published web page. We present WebPerceptor an open source, client-side Chromium plugin which, for any webpage, identifies text content, relays this to a local or cloud-based LLM with a user-defined prompt and then modifies the existing text (to replace, append, or remove it) based on the LLM response. We discuss the potential benefits and harms of an AI mediated web where the idea of a shared, canonical, objective web will no longer hold as AI becomes the mediator of what we perceive when we browse online.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces the concept of an 'AI Mediated Web' where web content is automatically and personally rewritten in real-time by an LLM based on user prompts. The authors present WebPerceptor, an open-source Chromium plugin that intercepts webpage text, sends it to an LLM with a user-defined prompt, and modifies the text accordingly. The work highlights both the potential benefits and harms of such technology, noting that it challenges the notion of a shared, objective web.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了“AI中介网络”的概念，即基于用户提示，由大语言模型自动、个性化地实时改写网页内容。作者介绍了WebPerceptor，一个开源Chromium插件，它截取网页文本，将其与用户定义的提示一起发送给大语言模型，并根据模型响应修改文本。该工作强调了此类技术的潜在益处与危害，指出它挑战了共享、客观网络的概念。

papers.title: Look Here, Click Me: Improving Older Adults' Perception of Manipulable User Interface Components through AI-Based Perceptual Guidance
papers.short_title: Look Here, Click Me: Improving Older A...
papers.abstract: Older adults often struggle to identify manipulable components in UIs due to low familiarity with digital devices. Despite existing digital literacy programs, they mainly rely on memorizing step-by-step operations in specific applications, offering limited support for adapting to new digital environments. This study proposes an AI-based perceptual training program that guides users to easily detect manipulable UI components through perceptual information, color and location. Our AI system extracts perceptual information from UI components on a screen and generates textual guidance. We conducted a user study with 13 older adults, including a training session and pre-/post- interviews, and measured their detection performance and confidence. Results showed that basic UI detection training improved participants’ detection abilities, and our perceptual guidance helped older adults with low confidence better recognize UI components. We expect that our program enables older adults to fundamentally understand digital environments beyond rote memorization, supporting their long-term digital adaptation.
papers.summary_en: This paper proposes an AI-based perceptual training program that helps older adults identify manipulable UI components by highlighting their color and location. A user study with 13 participants showed that the program improved detection performance, especially for those with low confidence. The approach aims to move beyond rote memorization of specific apps, supporting long-term digital adaptation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种基于AI的感知训练程序，通过突出UI组件的颜色和位置，帮助老年人识别可操作元素。对13名参与者的用户研究表明，该程序提升了检测表现，尤其对低信心用户效果显著。该方法旨在超越对特定应用的死记硬背，支持长期的数字适应。

papers.title: Bridging Gulfs in UI Generation through Semantic Guidance
papers.short_title: Semantic Guidance for UI Generation
papers.abstract: While generative AI enables high-fidelity UI generation from text prompts, users struggle to articulate design intent and evaluate or refine results—creating gulfs of execution and evaluation. To understand the information needed for UI generation, we conducted a thematic analysis of UI prompting guidelines, identifying key design semantics and discovering that they are hierarchical and interdependent. Leveraging these findings, we developed a system that enables users to specify semantics, visualize relationships, and extract how semantics are reflected in generated UIs. By making semantics serve as an intermediate representation between human intent and AI output, our system bridges both gulfs by making requirements explicit and outcomes interpretable. A comparative user study suggests that our approach enhances users’ perceived control over intent expression and outcome interpretation, and facilitates more predictable iterative refinement. Our work demonstrates how explicit semantic representation enables systematic and explainable exploration of design possibilities in AI-driven UI design.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of users struggling to express design intent and evaluate AI-generated UIs. Through a thematic analysis of UI prompting guidelines, the authors identify hierarchical and interdependent design semantics. They develop a system that uses these semantics as an intermediate representation, making requirements explicit and outcomes interpretable. A user study shows this approach improves perceived control and enables more predictable iterative refinement in AI-driven UI design.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对用户在表达设计意图和评估AI生成界面时面临的困难，通过对UI提示指南的主题分析，识别出层次化且相互依赖的设计语义。作者开发了一个系统，将这些语义作为中间表示，使需求明确化、结果可解释。用户研究表明，该方法增强了用户对意图表达和结果解释的感知控制，并促进了更可预测的迭代优化。

papers.title: Co-Disclosing the Computer: LLM-Mediated Computing through Reflective Conversation
papers.short_title: LLM-Mediated Computing via Reflective Conversation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are changing how we interact with computers. As they become capable of generating software dynamically, they invite a fundamental rethinking of the computer’s role in human activity. In this conceptual paper, we introduce LLM-mediated computing: a paradigm in which interaction is no longer structured around fixed applications, but emerges in real-time through human intent and LLM interpretation. We make three contributions: (1) we articulate a new interaction metaphor of reflective conversation to guide future design, (2) we use the lens of postphenomenology to understand the human-LLM-computer relation, and (3) we propose a new mode of computing based on co-disclosure, in which the computer is constituted in use. Together, they define a new mode of computing, provide a lens to analyze it, and offer a metaphor to design with.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces LLM-mediated computing, a new paradigm where interaction emerges in real-time through human intent and LLM interpretation, replacing fixed applications. It proposes a reflective conversation metaphor, uses postphenomenology to analyze human-LLM-computer relations, and defines a co-disclosure mode where the computer is constituted in use. These contributions together define a new computing mode, provide an analytical lens, and offer a design metaphor.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出LLM中介计算这一新范式，其中交互通过人类意图与LLM解释实时涌现，取代固定应用。它提出反思性对话隐喻，运用后现象学分析人-LLM-计算机关系，并定义共揭示模式，即计算机在使用中被构成。这些贡献共同定义了新的计算模式、提供了分析视角并给出了设计隐喻。

papers.title: (Computer) Vision in Action: Comparing Remote Sighted Assistance and a Multimodal Voice Agent in Inspection Sequences
papers.short_title: Vision in Action: Remote Sighted vs Multimodal Agent
papers.abstract: Does human–AI assistance unfold in the same way as human–human assistance? This research explores what can be learned from the expertise of blind individuals and sighted volunteers to inform the design of multimodal voice agents and address the enduring challenge of proactivity. Drawing on granular analysis of two representative fragments from a larger corpus, we contrast the practices co-produced by an experienced human remote sighted assistant and a blind participant—as they collaborate to find a stain on a blanket over the phone—with those achieved when the same participant worked with a multimodal voice agent on the same task, a few moments earlier. This comparison enables us to specify precisely which fundamental proactive practices the agent did not enact in situ. We conclude that, so long as multimodal voice agents cannot produce environmentally occasioned vision-based actions, they will lack a key resource relied upon by human remote sighted assistants.
papers.summary_en: This paper compares how a blind person and a remote sighted assistant collaborate to find a stain on a blanket with how the same person interacts with a multimodal voice agent on the same task. Through detailed analysis, it identifies that the voice agent fails to perform environmentally triggered, vision-based proactive actions that human assistants naturally do. The authors argue that without such capabilities, multimodal voice agents cannot replicate the key proactive support provided by human remote sighted assistants.
papers.summary_zh: 本文比较了盲人与远程视力助手合作寻找毯子上污渍的过程，以及同一人与多模态语音代理完成相同任务时的互动。通过细致分析，发现语音代理无法执行人类助手自然做出的、由环境触发的基于视觉的主动行为。作者认为，缺乏这种能力，多模态语音代理就无法复制人类远程视力助手提供的关键主动支持。

papers.title: Invisible Consent: Browser Automation by LLM Agents is Not Privacy-aware
papers.short_title: Invisible Consent: LLM Browser Automation Privacy
papers.abstract: Cookie consent interfaces are intended to elicit informed tracking choices from human users, yet LLM-based browsing agents may resolve these dialogs autonomously while the user is unaware of the moment of decision. We call this phenomenon Invisible Consent: consent signals generated on a user’s behalf without a meaningful opportunity for the user to notice, deliberate, or intervene. We study Invisible Consent through controlled real-browser experiments on instrumented mock websites that present consent interfaces on load, varying consent UI patterns and agent-side instructions. Across conditions, we find agents tend to default to the easiest path to proceed, accepting cookies. Even under an explicit deny-all instruction, acceptance persists in 14.4% of trials with explicit consent interaction, and the residual rate tracks both the prompt and interface design.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies and empirically demonstrates 'Invisible Consent,' a phenomenon where LLM-based browsing agents autonomously resolve cookie consent interfaces without user awareness or intervention. Through controlled experiments, the authors show that agents default to accepting cookies even when instructed to deny all, with a 14.4% residual acceptance rate under explicit deny instructions. The findings highlight that current LLM agents lack privacy awareness, and their behavior is influenced by both UI design and prompt instructions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别并实证了“隐形同意”现象，即基于LLM的浏览代理在用户不知情或无法干预的情况下自主处理Cookie同意界面。通过控制实验，作者发现即使明确指示拒绝所有Cookie，代理仍默认接受，在明确拒绝指令下仍有14.4%的残留接受率。研究结果表明，当前LLM代理缺乏隐私意识，其行为受UI设计和提示指令的共同影响。

papers.title: Toward Independent Online Shopping of the Visually Impaired Through Voice-based Computer-Using Agent
papers.short_title: Voice Agent for Visually Impaired Shopping
papers.abstract: Visually impaired individuals face barriers in online shopping because product details are often conveyed through images, and alternative text is frequently insufficient. The recent advent of Computer-Using Agents (CUA) based on Large Multimodal Models, which can directly manipulate graphical user interfaces, offers new opportunities for such accessibility. However, there is a lack of research that considers how voice-based systems should be designed to support visually impaired users in complex online shopping contexts. Thus, our study qualitatively explores the experiences and needs of visually impaired users as they shop online through voice interaction with a CUA We conducted a Semi-Automatic Wizard-of-Oz study with 12 visually impaired participants, in which they performed shopping tasks with a voice-based CUA system, followed by debriefing interviews. This paper proposes design implications for creating a more inclusive and disability-centered online shopping environment with voice-based CUA for visually impaired users.
papers.summary_en: This paper explores how visually impaired users can independently shop online using a voice-based Computer-Using Agent (CUA) powered by large multimodal models. Through a Wizard-of-Oz study with 12 participants, the authors identify key challenges and needs, proposing design implications for creating more accessible and disability-centered online shopping experiences. The work bridges the gap between CUA technology and accessibility, offering practical guidance for voice-based systems that support complex shopping tasks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了视障用户如何通过基于大型多模态模型的语音计算机使用代理（CUA）独立进行在线购物。通过一项包含12名参与者的半自动向导实验，作者识别了关键挑战与需求，并提出了设计启示，以创建更包容、以残障为中心的在线购物体验。该研究弥合了CUA技术与无障碍性之间的差距，为支持复杂购物任务的语音系统提供了实用指导。

papers.title: Agentic Automation Experiences - Rethinking the Interaction of Humans and AI Agents
papers.short_title: Agentic Automation: Human-AI Interaction
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have enabled agentic AI systems that coordinate multiple, specialized agents behind unified interfaces. These systems can independently initiate actions and solve complex problems. In traditional automation systems within organizations, workers maintained clear oversight—they could see which system handled each task and trace outcomes to specific processes. The integration of agentic AI, however, obscures this relationship and makes it more difficult for humans to identify which agent is responsible for a given outcome. This creates novel research challenges in the field of “Automation Experience”, particularly in terms of transparency, human agency, and long-term human-AI collaboration dynamics. This workshop focuses on these three critical research dimensions. First, multi-agent transparency and attribution explore how humans understand decision-making when responsibility is shared across multiple coordinating agents. Second, human agency examines how workers can keep control when collaborating with proactive AI systems that act on their own. Third, long-term temporal evolution looks at human skills change over time, including how skills are maintained and how dependencies form. Through real-life organizational cases, presentations, and collaborative activities, workshop participants will advance their understanding of human experience with agentic AI and establish a research agenda for organizational contexts.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies key challenges in human-AI interaction when agentic AI systems coordinate multiple specialized agents, obscuring transparency and accountability. It proposes a research agenda focusing on three dimensions: multi-agent transparency and attribution, human agency in maintaining control, and long-term skill evolution. The workshop aims to advance understanding of human experiences with agentic AI in organizational contexts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别了当代理型AI系统协调多个专业智能体时，人类与AI交互中的关键挑战，即透明度和责任归属变得模糊。它提出了一个研究议程，聚焦三个维度：多智能体透明性与归因、人类保持控制的能力，以及长期技能演变。该研讨会旨在推进对组织环境中代理型AI人类体验的理解。

papers.title: INLAY: Preemptive, In-Context Intelligence for Casual Web Browsing
papers.short_title: INLAY: Preemptive In-Context Web Browsing
papers.abstract: AI assistance in browsers often depends on explicit invocation, which is effective for well-defined tasks but imposes significant overhead during exploratory ‘casual’ browsing where intent is implicit or latent. We introduce Inlay, a preemptive INtelligence LAYer that bridges the intent-action gap herein by proactively embedding AI-driven insights and cues directly within webpages. Grounded in Information Foraging Theory, Inlay enhances ‘information scents’ by shifting users from high-effort query formulation to low-effort intent confirmation while preserving user agency. Our preliminary user study (N=12) provides early signals that Inlay’s context-aware interventions may anticipate emergent needs and encourage deeper exploration while sustaining foraging flow. Our findings suggest that proactive augmentation can transform browsing from command-driven interaction to collaborative AI-assisted exploration.
papers.summary_en: Inlay is a browser extension that proactively embeds AI insights into webpages to assist casual browsing, reducing the need for explicit user queries. Grounded in Information Foraging Theory, it enhances 'information scents' by shifting from high-effort query formulation to low-effort intent confirmation. A preliminary study (N=12) suggests it may anticipate user needs and encourage deeper exploration without disrupting flow.
papers.summary_zh: Inlay 是一种浏览器扩展，通过主动在网页中嵌入AI洞察来辅助随意浏览，减少用户显式查询的需求。基于信息觅食理论，它通过将高努力的查询制定转变为低努力意图确认来增强“信息线索”。初步用户研究（N=12）表明，它可能预判用户需求并鼓励更深入的探索，同时不破坏浏览流。

papers.title: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
papers.short_title: Dark Patterns vs GUI Agents: LLM Susceptibility
papers.abstract: The dark patterns, deceptive interface designs manipulating user behaviors, have been extensively studied for their effects on human decision-making and autonomy. Yet, with the rising prominence of LLM-powered GUI agents that automate tasks from high-level intents, understanding how dark patterns affect agents is increasingly important. We present a two-phase empirical study examining how agents, human participants, and human-AI teams respond to 16 types of dark patterns across diverse scenarios. Phase 1 highlights that agents often fail to recognize dark patterns, and even when aware, prioritize task completion over protective action. Phase 2 revealed divergent failure modes: humans succumb due to cognitive shortcuts and habitual compliance, while agents falter from procedural blind spots. Human oversight improved avoidance but introduced costs such as attentional tunneling and cognitive load. Our findings show neither humans nor agents are uniformly resilient, and collaboration introduces new vulnerabilities, suggesting design needs for transparency, adjustable autonomy, and oversight.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how LLM-powered GUI agents, humans, and human-AI teams respond to 16 types of dark patterns (deceptive interface designs). It finds that agents often fail to recognize dark patterns and prioritize task completion over protection, while humans succumb to cognitive shortcuts. Human oversight improves avoidance but introduces new vulnerabilities like attentional tunneling. The study highlights that neither humans nor agents are uniformly resilient, and collaboration creates unique risks, suggesting design needs for transparency and adjustable autonomy.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了LLM驱动的GUI代理、人类以及人机团队如何应对16种暗模式（欺骗性界面设计）。研究发现，代理常无法识别暗模式，且优先完成任务而非采取保护措施，而人类则因认知捷径而屈服。人类监督提高了规避能力，但引入了注意力隧道等新漏洞。研究表明，人类和代理均非普遍具有韧性，协作会带来独特风险，建议设计需注重透明度与可调自主性。

papers.title: DuetUI: A Bidirectional Context Loop for Human-Agent Co-Generation of Task-Oriented Interfaces
papers.short_title: DuetUI: Bidirectional Context Loop for Co-Generation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models are reshaping task automation, yet remain limited in complex, multi-step real-world tasks that require aligning with vague user intent and enabling dynamic user override. From a formative study with 12 participants, we found that end-users actively seek to shape task-oriented interfaces rather than relying on one-shot outputs. To address this, we introduce the human-agent co-generation paradigm, materialized in DuetUI. This LLM-empowered system unfolds alongside task progress through a bidirectional context loop—the agent scaffolds the interface by decomposing the task, while the user’s direct manipulations implicitly steer the agent’s next generation step. In a technical ablation study and a user study with 24 participants, DuetUI improved task efficiency and interface usability, supporting more seamless human-agent collaboration. Our contributions include the proposal of this novel paradigm, the design of a proof-of-concept DuetUI prototype embodying it, and empirical and technical insights from an initial evaluation of how this bidirectional loop may help align agents with human intent and inform future development.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces DuetUI, a system that enables human-agent co-generation of task-oriented interfaces through a bidirectional context loop. Unlike one-shot LLM outputs, DuetUI allows users to iteratively shape the interface as the agent decomposes tasks, with user manipulations implicitly guiding the agent's next steps. Evaluations show improved task efficiency and usability, supporting more seamless collaboration. The work contributes a novel paradigm, a proof-of-concept prototype, and empirical insights for aligning agents with human intent.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出DuetUI系统，通过双向上下文循环实现人与智能体共同生成任务导向界面。与一次性LLM输出不同，DuetUI允许用户在智能体分解任务时迭代调整界面，用户操作隐式引导智能体下一步生成。评估表明该系统提升了任务效率和界面可用性，支持更无缝的人机协作。该工作贡献了新范式、概念验证原型以及关于对齐智能体与人类意图的实证与技术见解。

papers.title: The Invisible Mentor: Inferring User Actions from Screen Recordings to Recommend Better Workflows
papers.short_title: InvisibleMentor: Inferring Actions from Screen Recordings
papers.abstract: Users of feature-rich tools like Excel often miss more efficient workflows, repeating tedious steps and making avoidable errors. Current approaches to helping them require either manual prompting, which is effortful for users, or automated logging, which is limiting for developers. We present InvisibleMentor, a system inspired by over-the-shoulder learning: it observes what users do, then shows them how to do it better. To do this, InvisibleMentor analyzes screen recordings with a vision-language model to reconstruct actions and context, then uses a large language model to generate vision-grounded task reflection, structured suggestions grounded in observed behavior. In a user study, participants found InvisibleMentor’s suggestions more clear, more relevant, and more useful than those from a prompt-based assistant, demonstrating that AI can do more than automate away work—it can help users master it.
papers.summary_en: InvisibleMentor is a system that passively observes users' screen recordings of tasks in tools like Excel, then uses vision-language and large language models to reconstruct actions and generate context-aware suggestions for more efficient workflows. Unlike existing methods that require manual prompting or automated logging, it learns from natural user behavior without extra effort. A user study showed its suggestions were clearer, more relevant, and more useful than those from a prompt-based assistant, demonstrating AI's potential to help users master tools rather than just automate tasks.
papers.summary_zh: InvisibleMentor是一个系统，它通过被动观察用户在Excel等工具中的屏幕录制，利用视觉-语言模型和大语言模型重建操作并生成上下文感知的建议，以帮助用户采用更高效的工作流程。与需要手动提示或自动日志记录的现有方法不同，它无需用户额外努力即可从自然行为中学习。用户研究表明，其建议比基于提示的助手更清晰、更相关、更有用，展示了AI不仅自动化工作，还能帮助用户掌握工具的潜力。

papers.title: Characterizing Unintended Consequences of GUI Agents For Web Browsing
papers.short_title: Unintended Consequences of GUI Agents for Web Browsing
papers.abstract: The integration of LLMs into GUI agents promises to revolutionize web browsing automation, yet the practical user experience remains challenging. This paper systematically characterizes user-reported issues with GUI agents by focusing on three dimensions: phenomena, influences, and user-centric mitigation. We adopted a two-phase method combining social media analysis (N=221 posts) and semi-structured interviews (N=21). Our findings reveal a taxonomy of complaints unique to GUI agents, including deficits in grounding abstract intent into concrete interface affordances, the inability to adapt to dynamic visual states, and the execution of erroneous actions. These lead to influences distinct from text-based hallucinations, ranging from task abandonment to security risks like uncontrolled file system access. In response, users are forced to employ ad-hoc mitigation strategies, including ecological sandboxing, and cursor shadowing to correct GUI agents behaviors. We contribute: (1) a comprehensive characterization of complaints specific to GUI agents interaction, (2) an analysis of how these phenomena degrade interaction integrity, and (3) design implications for creating consequence-aware agents.
papers.summary_en: This paper systematically characterizes user-reported issues with GUI agents for web browsing, identifying unique problems such as difficulty grounding abstract intent into interface actions, inability to adapt to dynamic visual states, and execution of erroneous actions. These issues lead to consequences like task abandonment and security risks, prompting users to adopt ad-hoc mitigation strategies like ecological sandboxing and cursor shadowing. The study contributes a taxonomy of complaints, an analysis of how these phenomena degrade interaction integrity, and design implications for consequence-aware agents.
papers.summary_zh: 本文系统性地描述了用户在使用GUI代理进行网页浏览时报告的问题，识别出独特的缺陷，如难以将抽象意图转化为具体界面操作、无法适应动态视觉状态以及执行错误操作。这些问题导致任务放弃和安全风险等后果，迫使用户采用生态沙箱和光标跟踪等临时缓解策略。研究贡献包括投诉分类、这些现象如何降低交互完整性的分析，以及为设计具有后果意识的代理提供启示。

papers.title: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
papers.short_title: PrivWeb: Content-aware Privacy for Web Agents
papers.abstract: While web agents gained popularity by automating web interactions, their requirement for interface access introduces privacy risks that are understudied, particularly from users’ perspective. Through a formative study (N=15), we found that users frequently misunderstand agent data practices, and desire unobtrusive, transparent data management. To achieve this, we developed PrivWeb, a trusted add-on on web agents that utilizes a localized LLM to anonymize private information on interfaces based on user preferences. It employs a tiered delegation to balance automation and intrusiveness, using ambient notifications for low-sensitivity data and enforces a mandatory pause for high-sensitivity data. The user study (N=14) across travel, information retrieval, shopping, and entertainment tasks showed that PrivWeb enhances perceived privacy protection and trust compared to transparency-only baselines, without increasing cognitive load. Crucially, we identified user delegation strategies: they prefer to manually execute sensitive steps for high-sensitivity data, while granting agent access to low-sensitivity data.
papers.summary_en: PrivWeb is a privacy-preserving add-on for web agents that uses a local LLM to anonymize user data on interfaces based on preferences. It introduces tiered delegation, where low-sensitivity data triggers ambient notifications and high-sensitivity data requires mandatory user pauses. A user study showed it improves perceived privacy and trust without increasing cognitive load, and users prefer manual execution for sensitive steps while granting agent access for low-sensitivity data.
papers.summary_zh: PrivWeb是一个面向网络代理的隐私保护插件，利用本地大语言模型根据用户偏好对界面上的个人信息进行匿名化处理。它采用分层委托机制，对低敏感数据使用环境通知，对高敏感数据强制用户暂停确认。用户研究表明，与仅提供透明度的基线相比，PrivWeb在不增加认知负荷的情况下提升了隐私感知和信任度，且用户倾向于手动执行高敏感步骤，而将低敏感数据委托给代理处理。

papers.title: Towards Human-Centered Agent Authorization: A Landscape Analysis of Commercial AI Agents
papers.short_title: Human-Centered Agent Authorization: Landscape Analysis
papers.abstract: Emerging AI agents require high autonomy, yet current authorization frameworks fail to support necessary user oversight. Through structured walkthroughs of 18 commercial web-based agents, we analyzed how these systems implement permission negotiation and revocation. We uncover pervasive problematic authorization patterns, including bundled permissions, lazy disconnect, non-persistent disclosure, and default opt-in data practices. Crucially, we identify a dominant two-layer architecture where agents demand broad system permissions masked by interface guardrails, shifting security reliance from deterministic protocols to probabilistic model compliance. We propose the concept of human-centered agent authorization to prioritize user control, understanding, and trust when granting, managing, and auditing AI agent permissions.
papers.summary_en: This paper analyzes 18 commercial AI agents and identifies problematic authorization patterns like bundled permissions and lazy disconnect. It reveals a two-layer architecture where broad system permissions are masked by interface guardrails, shifting security from deterministic protocols to probabilistic model compliance. The authors propose human-centered agent authorization to prioritize user control and trust in permission management.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过分析18个商业AI代理，揭示了捆绑权限、延迟断开等有问题的授权模式。研究发现一种双层架构，其中广泛的系统权限被界面护栏掩盖，将安全性从确定性协议转移到概率性模型合规。作者提出以人为中心的代理授权概念，以优先考虑用户在权限管理中的控制权和信任。

papers.title: AI at your Fingertips: Wearable Ring as a Low-Friction Interface for Agentic AI
papers.short_title: Wearable Ring Interface for Agentic AI
papers.abstract: While “Agentic AI” can now execute complex, multi-step workflows, human interaction with these agents remains tethered to high-friction screens. We present a technology probe designed to explore the experience of screenless, “fire-and-forget” task delegation. Our system consists of a custom-built wearable ring with touch input and haptic feedback, paired with an agentic pipeline that autonomously recovers from failures to ensure robust execution. Through an exploratory user study (N = 11) involving real-world scenarios, we identify design tensions in screenless interaction. Our findings reveal a conflict between delegation and verification: participants valued the efficiency of screenless interaction for simple tasks but lacked the confidence to delegate complex workflows without audio/visual feedback. We further highlight the social tension of public voice input, where users prefer whispering to maintain privacy and social acceptability. This work contributes a functional prototype and initial design implications for the future of always-available AI agents that minimize visual attention.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a wearable ring interface for delegating tasks to AI agents without screens, using touch input and haptic feedback. Through a user study, it reveals a key tension: users appreciate the efficiency for simple tasks but lack confidence for complex ones without audio/visual feedback. It also highlights social concerns with public voice input. The work provides design implications for low-friction, always-available AI interaction.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种可穿戴戒指界面，通过触摸输入和触觉反馈实现无屏幕的AI任务委托。用户研究发现，用户虽认可简单任务的效率，但缺乏音频/视觉反馈时对复杂任务信心不足，同时公开语音输入存在社交顾虑。该工作为低摩擦、随时可用的AI交互提供了设计启示。

papers.title: TaskAudit: Detecting Functiona11ity Errors in Mobile Apps via Agentic Task Execution
papers.short_title: TaskAudit: Detecting Functionality Errors via Agentic Tasks
papers.abstract: Accessibility checkers are tools in support of accessible app development, and their use is encouraged by accessibility best practices. However, most current checkers evaluate static or mechanically-generated contexts, failing to capture common accessibility errors impacting mobile app functionality. In this work, we define functiona11ity errors as accessibility barriers that only manifest through interaction (i.e., named according to a blend of “functionality” and “accessibility”). We introduce TaskAudit, which comprises three components: a Task Generator that constructs interactive tasks from app screens, a Task Executor that uses agents with a screen reader proxy to perform these tasks, and an Accessibility Analyzer that detects and reports accessibility errors by examining interaction traces. Our evaluation on real-world apps shows that TaskAudit detects 48 functiona11ity errors from 54 app screens, compared to between 4 and 20 with existing checkers. Our analysis demonstrates common error patterns that TaskAudit can detect in addition to those from prior work, including label-functionality mismatch, cluttered navigation, and inappropriate feedback.
papers.summary_en: TaskAudit is a system that detects accessibility errors in mobile apps by automatically generating and executing interactive tasks using screen reader agents. It identifies 'functiona11ity errors'—accessibility issues that only appear during user interaction—which traditional static checkers miss. In tests on real apps, TaskAudit found 48 such errors across 54 screens, far more than existing tools, and uncovered new error patterns like label-functionality mismatch and cluttered navigation.
papers.summary_zh: TaskAudit是一个通过自动生成并执行交互任务来检测移动应用无障碍错误的系统，它利用屏幕阅读器代理来模拟用户操作。该系统能够识别“功能无障碍错误”——即仅在用户交互过程中才会显现的无障碍问题，而传统的静态检查工具无法发现这些错误。在真实应用的测试中，TaskAudit在54个屏幕中检测到48个此类错误，远超现有工具，并发现了标签-功能不匹配、导航混乱等新的错误模式。

papers.title: Simulating Human Cursor Trajectories for Path-Sensitive GUI Evaluation
papers.short_title: Simulating Cursor Trajectories for GUI Evaluation
papers.abstract: User simulation models support predictive evaluation of interface designs by generating synthetic interaction behavior. While existing models can accurately simulate unconstrained pointing and clicking, many common graphical user interface interactions impose geometric constraints on cursor motion, where the path taken directly affects interaction outcomes. We present a parametrizable generative user simulation model that generates realistic cursor trajectories for such tasks by formulating constrained movement as a receding-horizon optimization problem using Model Predictive Contouring Control. The model balances speed, smoothness, and continuous path and boundary compliance. Evaluation against human data in both abstract tunnel steering tasks and realistic interface scenarios, including cascading menus and lasso selection, shows that the simulated trajectories closely match human behavior and support scalable, trajectory-level analysis of path-sensitive interface designs.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a generative user simulation model that realistically mimics human cursor trajectories in path-sensitive GUI tasks, such as steering through menus or making lasso selections. The model uses Model Predictive Contouring Control to balance speed, smoothness, and compliance with geometric constraints. Evaluations show it closely matches human behavior, enabling scalable, trajectory-level analysis of interface designs.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种生成式用户模拟模型，能够真实地模拟人类在路径敏感的图形用户界面任务（如菜单导航或套索选择）中的光标轨迹。该模型采用模型预测轮廓控制，在速度、平滑度以及几何约束的符合性之间取得平衡。评估表明，该模型与人类行为高度一致，支持对界面设计进行可扩展的轨迹级分析。

papers.title: MIWA: Mixed-Initiative Web Automation for Better User Control and Confidence
papers.short_title: MIWA: Mixed-Initiative Web Automation
papers.abstract: In the era of Big Data, web automation is frequently used by data scientists, domain experts, and programmers to complete time-consuming data collection tasks. However, developing web automation scripts requires familiarity with a programming language and HTML, which remains a key learning barrier for non-expert users. We provide MIWA, a mixed-initiative web automation system that enables users to create web automation scripts by demonstrating what content they want from the targeted websites. Compared to existing web automation tools, MIWA helps users better understand a generated script and build trust in it by (1) providing a step-by-step explanation of the script’s behavior with visual correspondence to the target website, (2) supporting greater autonomy and control over web automation via step-through debugging and fine-grained demonstration refinement, and (3) automatically detecting potential corner cases that are handled improperly by the generated script. We conducted a within-subjects user study with 24 participants and compared MIWA with Rousillon, a state-of-the-art web automation tool. Results showed that, compared to Rousillon, MIWA reduced the task completion time by half while helping participants gain more confidence in the generated script.
papers.summary_en: MIWA is a mixed-initiative web automation system that allows non-expert users to create scripts by demonstrating desired content. It enhances user understanding and trust through step-by-step visual explanations, fine-grained control via debugging and refinement, and automatic detection of corner cases. A user study showed MIWA halved task completion time and increased user confidence compared to the state-of-the-art tool Rousillon.
papers.summary_zh: MIWA是一种混合主动式网页自动化系统，允许非专家用户通过演示所需内容来创建脚本。它通过逐步的视觉解释、细粒度的调试与优化控制，以及自动检测边界情况，增强了用户对脚本的理解和信任。用户研究表明，与最先进的工具Rousillon相比，MIWA将任务完成时间减半，并提高了用户的信心。

papers.title: Video2Action: Reducing Human Interactions in Action Annotation of App Tutorial Videos
papers.short_title: Video2Action: Reducing Human Interactions in Action Annotation
papers.abstract: Tutorial videos of mobile apps have become a popular and compelling way for users to learn unfamiliar app features. To make the video accessible to the users, video creators always need to annotate the actions in the video, including what actions are performed and where to tap. However, this process can be time-consuming and labor-intensive. In this paper, we introduce a lightweight approach Video2Action, to automatically generate the action scenes and predict the action locations from the video by using image-processing and deep-learning methods. The automated experiments demonstrate the good performance of Video2Action in acquiring actions from the videos, and a user study shows the usefulness of our generated action cues in assisting video creators with action annotation.
papers.summary_en: Video2Action is a lightweight system that automatically extracts action scenes and predicts tap locations from mobile app tutorial videos using image processing and deep learning. It reduces the manual effort required for action annotation, which is typically time-consuming for video creators. Experiments show good performance in action detection, and a user study confirms the generated cues help creators annotate actions more efficiently.
papers.summary_zh: Video2Action是一个轻量级系统，利用图像处理和深度学习方法，自动从手机应用教程视频中提取动作场景并预测点击位置。它减少了视频创作者通常需要花费大量时间进行手动动作标注的工作量。实验表明该系统在动作检测方面表现良好，用户研究也证实生成的提示信息能帮助创作者更高效地标注动作。

papers.title: Sparkybot: An Embodied AI Agent-Powered Robot with Customizable Characters andInteraction Behavior for Children
papers.short_title: Sparkybot: Embodied AI Robot for Children
papers.abstract: Sparkybot is a novel robotic platform designed to enrich children-robot interaction by leveraging embodied agent technology. The platform allows children to customize the interaction characters and behaviors of the robot, providing a more personalized and engaging experience. Two scenarios are demonstrated to showcase how children can customize and interact with the robot. Our goal is to provide a platform that enables children to interact with robots in a more creative and engaging way.
papers.summary_en: Sparkybot is a robotic platform that uses embodied AI agents to enable children to customize the robot's character and interaction behaviors, enhancing personalization and engagement. It demonstrates two scenarios where children can tailor the robot's appearance and responses, fostering creative interaction. The platform aims to make child-robot interaction more adaptable and enjoyable.
papers.summary_zh: Sparkybot是一个利用具身智能体技术的机器人平台，允许儿童自定义机器人的角色和交互行为，从而提升个性化和参与度。通过两个场景演示，儿童可以调整机器人的外观和反应方式，促进创造性互动。该平台旨在使儿童与机器人的交互更加灵活有趣。

papers.title: Using LLMs to Customize the UI of Webpages
papers.short_title: Using LLMs to Customize the UI of Webpages
papers.abstract: LLMs have capabilities to understand natural language and code, which makes them a great candidate for user-driven customization of webpages. A process that focuses on natural language can be useful for those who are less technologically literate. In this paper, we explore the potential of using LLMs to modify webpages, and what kinds of opportunities and challenges that come with it. We observe that specific prompts referring to color or targeted components can succeed, vague requests and any complex website tend to perform poorly.
papers.summary_en: This paper explores using large language models (LLMs) to enable non-technical users to customize webpage UIs through natural language requests. The authors find that LLMs can successfully modify specific elements like colors or targeted components, but struggle with vague requests and complex websites. The work highlights both the potential and limitations of LLM-driven UI customization, particularly for users with low technical literacy.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探索利用大语言模型（LLM）通过自然语言请求实现网页用户界面的个性化定制，尤其面向技术素养较低的用户。研究发现，LLM能成功修改颜色或特定组件等具体元素，但难以处理模糊请求和复杂网站。该工作揭示了LLM驱动UI定制的潜力与局限。

papers.title: DiLogics: Creating Web Automation Programs with Diverse Logics
papers.short_title: DiLogics: Web Automation with Diverse Logics
papers.abstract: Knowledge workers frequently encounter repetitive web data entry tasks, like updating records or placing orders. Web automation increases productivity, but translating tasks to web actions accurately and extending to new specifications is challenging. Existing tools can automate tasks that perform the same logical trace of UI actions (e.g., input text in each field in order), but do not support tasks requiring different executions based on varied input conditions. We present DiLogics, a programming-by-demonstration system that utilizes NLP to assist users in creating web automation programs that handle diverse specifications. DiLogics first semantically segments input data to structured task steps. By recording user demonstrations for each step, DiLogics generalizes the web macros to novel but semantically similar task requirements. Our evaluation showed that non-experts can effectively use DiLogics to create automation programs that fulfill diverse input instructions. DiLogics provides an efficient, intuitive, and expressive method for developing web automation programs satisfying diverse specifications.
papers.summary_en: DiLogics is a programming-by-demonstration system that uses NLP to help users create web automation programs capable of handling diverse input specifications. Unlike existing tools that only automate tasks with fixed UI action sequences, DiLogics supports tasks requiring different executions based on varied input conditions by semantically segmenting data and generalizing from user demonstrations. The system enables non-experts to efficiently build automation programs that fulfill diverse instructions, as shown in user studies.
papers.summary_zh: DiLogics是一个通过演示编程的系统，利用自然语言处理帮助用户创建能处理多样化输入规范的网页自动化程序。与仅能自动化固定UI操作序列的现有工具不同，DiLogics通过语义分割数据并从用户演示中泛化，支持基于不同输入条件需要不同执行逻辑的任务。用户研究表明，非专家用户能高效地使用DiLogics构建满足多样化指令的自动化程序。

papers.title: Never-ending Learning of User Interfaces
papers.short_title: Never-ending Learning of User Interfaces
papers.abstract: Machine learning models have been trained to predict semantic information about user interfaces (UIs) to make apps more accessible, easier to test, and to automate. Currently, most models rely on datasets that are collected and labeled by human crowd-workers, a process that is costly and surprisingly error-prone for certain tasks. For example, it is possible to guess if a UI element is "tappable" from a screenshot (i.e., based on visual signifiers) or from potentially unreliable metadata (e.g., a view hierarchy), but one way to know for certain is to programmatically tap the UI element and observe the effects. We built the Never-ending UI Learner, an app crawler that automatically installs real apps from a mobile app store and crawls them to discover new and challenging training examples to learn from. The Never-ending UI Learner has crawled for more than 5,000 device-hours, performing over half a million actions on 6,000 apps to train three computer vision models for i) tappability prediction, ii) draggability prediction, and iii) screen similarity.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces the Never-ending UI Learner, an automated system that crawls real mobile apps to collect training data for UI understanding models, overcoming the limitations of costly and error-prone human labeling. By programmatically interacting with UI elements, it generates reliable labels for tasks like tappability and draggability prediction. The system has crawled over 6,000 apps for 5,000 device-hours, training three computer vision models. This approach enables continuous learning from diverse, real-world examples without manual annotation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了永不停止的UI学习器，这是一个自动爬取真实移动应用以收集UI理解模型训练数据的系统，克服了人工标注成本高且易出错的问题。通过程序化地交互UI元素，它为可点击性、可拖拽性等任务生成了可靠的标签。该系统已爬取超过6000个应用，累计5000设备小时，训练了三个计算机视觉模型。这种方法无需人工标注，即可从多样化的真实世界示例中持续学习。

papers.title: iTutor: A Generative Tutorial System for Teaching the Elders to Use Smartphone Applications
papers.short_title: iTutor: Generative Tutorial for Elders
papers.abstract: We present iTutor, a generative tutorial system for promoting smartphone use proficiency among elders. iTutor is unique because it can dynamically generate tutorials based on current operation goals and UI context, which we achieved through leveraging prompt engineering to large language models (LLMs). Our evaluations showed potential for this approach, as we yielded 78.6% accuracy in the instruction generation process. We conclude by providing the roadmap for further development.
papers.summary_en: iTutor is a generative tutorial system that helps elderly users learn smartphone applications by dynamically generating step-by-step instructions based on their current goals and the app's user interface. It uses prompt engineering with large language models to achieve this, and initial evaluations show 78.6% accuracy in instruction generation. The system represents a novel approach to assistive technology for older adults, with a roadmap for future improvements.
papers.summary_zh: iTutor是一个生成式教程系统，通过基于用户当前操作目标和界面上下文动态生成逐步指导，帮助老年用户学习智能手机应用。它利用大型语言模型的提示工程实现这一功能，初步评估显示指令生成准确率达78.6%。该系统为老年人辅助技术提供了一种新颖方法，并规划了未来改进路线。

papers.title: VisionTasker: Mobile Task Automation Using Vision Based UI Understanding and LLM Task Planning
papers.short_title: VisionTasker: Mobile Automation via Vision & LLM
papers.abstract: Mobile task automation is an emerging field that leverages AI to streamline and optimize the execution of routine tasks on mobile devices, thereby enhancing efficiency and productivity. Traditional methods, such as Programming By Demonstration (PBD), are limited due to their dependence on predefined tasks and susceptibility to app updates. Recent advancements have utilized the view hierarchy to collect UI information and employed Large Language Models (LLM) to enhance task automation. However, view hierarchies have accessibility issues and face potential problems like missing object descriptions or misaligned structures. This paper introduces VisionTasker, a two-stage framework combining vision-based UI understanding and LLM task planning, for mobile task automation in a step-by-step manner. VisionTasker firstly converts a UI screenshot into natural language interpretations using a vision-based UI understanding approach, eliminating the need for view hierarchies. Secondly, it adopts a step-by-step task planning method, presenting one interface at a time to the LLM. The LLM then identifies relevant elements within the interface and determines the next action, enhancing accuracy and practicality. Extensive experiments show that VisionTasker outperforms previous methods, providing effective UI representations across four datasets. Additionally, in automating 147 real-world tasks on an Android smartphone, VisionTasker demonstrates advantages over humans in tasks where humans show unfamiliarity and shows significant improvements when integrated with the PBD mechanism. VisionTasker is open-source and available at https://github.com/AkimotoAyako/VisionTasker.
papers.summary_en: VisionTasker is a two-stage framework for mobile task automation that uses vision-based UI understanding to convert screenshots into natural language, eliminating the need for error-prone view hierarchies. It then employs a step-by-step planning method where an LLM processes one interface at a time to identify relevant elements and decide actions, improving accuracy. Experiments show it outperforms prior methods on UI understanding benchmarks and automates 147 real-world tasks effectively, especially benefiting users unfamiliar with the tasks.
papers.summary_zh: VisionTasker是一个两阶段移动任务自动化框架，通过基于视觉的UI理解将截图转化为自然语言描述，避免了易出错的视图层级依赖。它采用逐步规划方法，让大语言模型每次处理一个界面，识别相关元素并决定下一步动作，从而提升准确性。实验表明，它在UI理解基准测试上优于先前方法，并能有效自动化147个真实任务，尤其对用户不熟悉的任务表现更佳。

papers.title: GPTVoiceTasker: Advancing Multi-step Mobile Task Efficiency Through Dynamic Interface Exploration and Learning
papers.short_title: GPTVoiceTasker: Multi-step Mobile Task Efficiency
papers.abstract: Virtual assistants have the potential to play an important role in helping users achieves different tasks. However, these systems face challenges in their real-world usability, characterized by inefficiency and struggles in grasping user intentions. Leveraging recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), we introduce GptVoiceTasker, a virtual assistant poised to enhance user experiences and task efficiency on mobile devices. GptVoiceTasker excels at intelligently deciphering user commands and executing relevant device interactions to streamline task completion. For unprecedented tasks, GptVoiceTasker utilises the contextual information and on-screen content to continuously explore and execute the tasks. In addition, the system continually learns from historical user commands to automate subsequent task invocations, further enhancing execution efficiency. From our experiments, GptVoiceTasker achieved 84.5% accuracy in parsing human commands into executable actions and 85.7% accuracy in automating multi-step tasks. In our user study, GptVoiceTasker boosted task efficiency in real-world scenarios by 34.85%, accompanied by positive participant feedback. We made GptVoiceTasker open-source, inviting further research into LLMs utilization for diverse tasks through prompt engineering and leveraging user usage data to improve efficiency.
papers.summary_en: GPTVoiceTasker is a virtual assistant that leverages large language models to improve multi-step task efficiency on mobile devices. It interprets user commands, dynamically explores interfaces for novel tasks, and learns from historical usage to automate future actions. Experiments show 84.5% accuracy in command parsing and 85.7% in task automation, with a 34.85% boost in real-world task efficiency. The system is open-source, enabling further research into LLM-driven task automation.
papers.summary_zh: GPTVoiceTasker 是一款利用大语言模型提升移动设备多步骤任务效率的虚拟助手。它能智能解析用户指令，动态探索界面以处理新任务，并通过历史使用数据学习自动化后续操作。实验表明，其命令解析准确率达84.5%，任务自动化准确率达85.7%，在真实场景中任务效率提升34.85%。该系统已开源，为基于大语言模型的任务自动化研究提供了基础。

papers.title: LlamaTouch: A Faithful and Scalable Testbed for Mobile UI Task Automation
papers.short_title: LlamaTouch: Mobile UI Task Automation Testbed
papers.abstract: The emergent large language/multimodal models facilitate the evolution of mobile agents, especially in mobile UI task automation. However, existing evaluation approaches, which rely on human validation or established datasets to compare agent-predicted actions with predefined action sequences, are unscalable and unfaithful. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents LlamaTouch, a testbed for on-device mobile UI task execution and faithful, scalable task evaluation. By observing that the task execution process only transfers UI states, LlamaTouch employs a novel evaluation approach that only assesses whether an agent traverses all manually annotated, essential application/system states. LlamaTouch comprises three key techniques: (1) On-device task execution that enables mobile agents to interact with realistic mobile environments for task execution. (2) Fine-grained UI component annotation that merges pixel-level screenshots and textual screen hierarchies to explicitly identify and precisely annotate essential UI components with a rich set of designed annotation primitives. (3) A multi-level application state matching algorithm that utilizes exact and fuzzy matching to accurately detect critical information in each screen, even with unpredictable UI layout/content dynamics. LlamaTouch currently incorporates four mobile agents and 496 tasks, encompassing both tasks in the widely-used datasets and our self-constructed ones to cover more diverse mobile applications. Evaluation results demonstrate LlamaTouch’s high faithfulness of evaluation in real-world mobile environments and its better scalability than human validation. LlamaTouch also enables easy task annotation and integration of new mobile agents. Code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/LlamaTouch/LlamaTouch.
papers.summary_en: LlamaTouch is a testbed for evaluating mobile UI task automation agents that overcomes the scalability and faithfulness limitations of existing methods by assessing whether an agent traverses all essential application states rather than comparing to predefined action sequences. It features on-device task execution, fine-grained UI component annotation, and a multi-level state matching algorithm to handle dynamic UI content. The testbed includes 496 tasks and four agents, demonstrating high faithfulness and better scalability than human validation.
papers.summary_zh: LlamaTouch是一个用于评估移动UI任务自动化智能体的测试平台，通过判断智能体是否遍历所有关键应用状态而非与预定义动作序列比较，克服了现有方法在可扩展性和忠实性上的局限。它具备设备端任务执行、细粒度UI组件标注以及多层级状态匹配算法以处理动态UI内容。该测试平台包含496个任务和四个智能体，展示了在真实移动环境中的高忠实性评估和优于人工验证的可扩展性。

papers.title: Enabling Real-World Assistive Agents: From Live Vision to Proactive Context-Aware Information Delivery
papers.short_title: Real-World Assistive Agents: Live Vision to Proactive Delivery
papers.abstract: Interacting with the real world is a fundamental part of daily life, yet it remains challenging for individuals who are blind or visually impaired (BVI). It demands live, contextual understanding of dynamic environments, along with interactive, multimodal communication to fulfill their sensory and cognitive needs. To address this, my dissertation develops assistive AI systems and frameworks that observe the real world through multimodal sensing, reason about essential information in response to user contexts, and deliver human-like verbal communication to support real-world understanding. First, I explored the design insights of assistive AI agents by investigating how BVI users interact with human-like video AI systems across diverse real-world contexts. Second, with the identified insights, such as a lack of proactivity, I developed a mobile application that analyzes live camera feeds to generate real-time visual descriptions aligned with user goals, delivering them in harmony with the audio environment. Lastly, I extend it with a set of human-like capabilities, such as memory, spatial understanding, and the ability to infer intent from natural interactions, to act as a long-term assistive companion. Ultimately, my dissertation advances a paradigm shift from digital agents to real-world assistive agents that enhance the independence and agency of BVI individuals.
papers.summary_en: This dissertation develops assistive AI systems for blind or visually impaired individuals that process live video to understand real-world contexts, proactively deliver relevant information, and communicate verbally. The work first identifies design insights through user studies, then builds a mobile app that generates real-time visual descriptions aligned with user goals, and finally extends it with memory, spatial reasoning, and intent inference to act as a long-term companion. The core contribution is a paradigm shift from passive digital assistants to proactive, context-aware agents that enhance independence and agency in real-world interactions.
papers.summary_zh: 本论文开发了面向盲人或视障人士的辅助AI系统，通过处理实时视频理解现实世界情境，主动传递相关信息，并进行类人语音交流。研究首先通过用户研究识别设计洞见，随后构建了一款移动应用，能根据用户目标生成实时视觉描述，最后扩展了记忆、空间推理和意图推断能力，使其成为长期辅助伙伴。核心贡献在于实现了从被动数字助手到主动、情境感知智能体的范式转变，增强了用户在现实世界中的独立性和自主性。

papers.title: ReDemon UI: Reactive Synthesis by Demonstration for Web UI
papers.short_title: ReDemon UI: Reactive Synthesis for Web UI
papers.abstract: ReDemon UI synthesizes React applications from user demonstrations, enabling designers and non-expert programmers to create UIs that integrate with standard UI prototyping workflows. Users provide a static mockup sketch with event handler holes and demonstrate desired runtime behaviors by interacting with the rendered mockup and editing the sketch. ReDemon UI identifies reactive data and synthesizes a React program with correct state update logic. We utilize enumerative synthesis for simple UIs and LLMs for more complex UIs.
papers.summary_en: ReDemon UI is a system that synthesizes React applications from user demonstrations, allowing designers and non-expert programmers to create interactive UIs by sketching static mockups and demonstrating desired behaviors. It identifies reactive data and generates correct state update logic, using enumerative synthesis for simple UIs and LLMs for complex ones. This approach integrates with standard UI prototyping workflows, reducing the need for manual coding.
papers.summary_zh: ReDemon UI 是一个通过用户演示合成 React 应用程序的系统，允许设计师和非专业程序员通过绘制静态原型并演示期望行为来创建交互式用户界面。它识别响应式数据并生成正确的状态更新逻辑，对简单界面使用枚举合成，对复杂界面使用大语言模型。该方法与标准 UI 原型设计工作流集成，减少了手动编码的需求。

papers.title: Log2Plan: An Adaptive GUI Automation Framework Integrated with Task Mining Approach
papers.short_title: Log2Plan: GUI Automation with Task Mining
papers.abstract: GUI task automation streamlines repetitive tasks, but existing LLM or VLM-based planner-executor agents suffer from brittle generalization, high latency, and limited long-horizon coherence. Their reliance on single-shot reasoning or static plans makes them fragile under UI changes or complex tasks. Log2Plan addresses these limitations by combining a structured two-level planning framework with a task mining approach over user behavior logs, enabling robust and adaptable GUI automation. Log2Plan constructs high-level plans by mapping user commands to a structured task dictionary, enabling consistent and generalizable automation. To support personalization and reuse, it employs a task mining approach from user behavior logs that identifies user-specific patterns. These high-level plans are then grounded into low-level action sequences by interpreting real-time GUI context, ensuring robust execution across varying interfaces. We evaluated Log2Plan on 200 real-world tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in task success rate and execution time. Notably, it maintains over 60.0% success rate even on long-horizon task sequences, highlighting its robustness in complex, multi-step workflows.
papers.summary_en: Log2Plan introduces a two-level planning framework for GUI automation that combines high-level task planning from user commands with low-level action execution grounded in real-time UI context. It integrates task mining from user behavior logs to personalize and reuse automation patterns, improving robustness against UI changes and long-horizon tasks. Evaluated on 200 real-world tasks, it achieves over 60% success rate on complex multi-step workflows, outperforming existing LLM/VLM-based approaches in success rate and execution time.
papers.summary_zh: Log2Plan提出了一种双层规划框架，用于GUI自动化，该框架将用户命令的高层任务规划与基于实时UI上下文的底层动作执行相结合。它通过从用户行为日志中挖掘任务模式，实现自动化的个性化和复用，增强了对UI变化和长周期任务的鲁棒性。在200个真实任务上的评估表明，该方法在复杂多步工作流中成功率超过60%，在成功率和执行时间上均优于现有的基于LLM/VLM的方法。

papers.title: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
papers.short_title: Morae: Proactive Pausing for User Choices
papers.abstract: User interface (UI) agents promise to make inaccessible or complex UIs easier to access for blind and low-vision (BLV) users. However, current UI agents typically perform tasks end-to-end without involving users in critical choices or making them aware of important contextual information, thus reducing user agency. For example, in our field study, a BLV participant asked to buy the cheapest available sparkling water, and the agent automatically chose one from several equally priced options, without mentioning alternative products with different flavors or better ratings. To address this problem, we introduce Morae, a UI agent that automatically identifies decision points during task execution and pauses so that users can make choices. Morae uses large multimodal models to interpret user queries alongside UI code and screenshots, and prompt users for clarification when there is a choice to be made. In a study over real-world web tasks with BLV participants, Morae helped users complete more tasks and select options that better matched their preferences, as compared to baseline agents, including OpenAI Operator. More broadly, this work exemplifies a mixed-initiative approach in which users benefit from the automation of UI agents while being able to express their preferences.
papers.summary_en: Morae is a UI agent that proactively pauses task execution at decision points, using large multimodal models to interpret user queries and UI content, enabling blind and low-vision users to make informed choices. In a study, it outperformed baseline agents like OpenAI Operator by helping users complete more tasks and select options better matching their preferences, exemplifying a mixed-initiative approach that balances automation with user agency.
papers.summary_zh: Morae 是一种用户界面代理，能在任务执行过程中主动在决策点暂停，利用大型多模态模型理解用户查询和界面内容，使盲人或低视力用户能够做出知情选择。实验表明，与 OpenAI Operator 等基线代理相比，它帮助用户完成更多任务并选择更符合偏好的选项，体现了平衡自动化与用户自主权的混合主动方法。

papers.title: Creating General User Models from Computer Use
papers.short_title: Creating General User Models from Computer Use
papers.abstract: Human-computer interaction has long imagined technology that understands us—from our preferences and habits, to the timing and purpose of our everyday actions. Yet current user models remain fragmented, narrowly tailored to specific applications, and incapable of the flexible, cross-context reasoning required to fulfill these visions. This paper presents an architecture for a general user model (GUM) that learns about you by observing any interaction you have with your computer. The GUM takes as input any unstructured observation of a user (e.g., device screenshots) and constructs confidence-weighted natural language propositions that capture that user’s behavior, knowledge, beliefs, and preferences. GUMs can infer that a user is preparing for a wedding they’re attending from a message thread with a friend. Or recognize that a user is struggling with a collaborator’s feedback on a draft paper by observing multiple stalled edits and a switch to reading related work. GUMs introduce an architecture that infers new propositions about a user from multimodal observations, retrieves related propositions for context, and continuously revises existing propositions. To illustrate the breadth of applications that GUMs enable, we demonstrate how they augment chat-based assistants with contextual understanding, manage OS notifications to surface important information only when needed, and enable interactive agents that adapt to user preferences across applications. We also instantiate a new class of proactive assistants (Gumbos) that discover and execute useful suggestions on a user’s behalf based on their GUM. In our evaluations, we find that GUMs make calibrated and accurate inferences about users, and that assistants built on GUMs proactively identify and perform actions of meaningful value that users wouldn’t think to request explicitly. Altogether, GUMs introduce new methods that leverage large multimodal models to understand unstructured user context, enabling both long-standing visions of HCI and entirely new interactive systems that anticipate user needs.
papers.summary_en: This paper proposes a general user model (GUM) that learns about users by observing any computer interaction, such as screenshots, and constructs confidence-weighted natural language propositions about their behavior, knowledge, and preferences. The model can infer context like wedding planning from message threads or struggles with feedback from editing patterns, and it continuously revises its propositions. GUMs enable applications like context-aware chatbots, smart notification management, and proactive assistants that autonomously perform useful actions. Evaluations show GUMs make accurate inferences and enable assistants to identify valuable tasks users wouldn't explicitly request.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种通用用户模型（GUM），通过观察用户的任何计算机交互（如屏幕截图）来学习用户，并构建关于其行为、知识和偏好的置信度加权自然语言命题。该模型能从消息线程推断婚礼筹备，或从编辑模式识别反馈困难，并持续修正已有命题。GUM支持上下文感知聊天机器人、智能通知管理以及能自主执行有用操作的主动助手等应用。评估表明，GUM能做出准确的推断，并帮助助手发现用户不会明确请求的有价值任务。

papers.title: Multi-Click: Cross-Tab Web Automation via Action Generalization
papers.short_title: Multi-Click: Cross-Tab Web Automation
papers.abstract: Repetitive actions are a common and frustrating part of using the web. Prior work has proposed automating repetitive actions with natural language descriptions, demonstrations, and pseudocode. However, these approaches introduce abstractions that can be difficult to write, evaluate, and fit within web workflows. We describe a new approach, Multi-Click, for simultaneously performing the same action (e.g., clicking or typing) across multiple pages while maintaining the immediacy and understandability of direct manipulation. Users can intuitively select groups of analogous elements within or across windows/tabs (e.g., equivalent elements in different instantiations of a template) and interact with these elements as if each simultaneously had keyboard or cursor focus (e.g., one click propagates to multiple targets). Multi-Click introduces algorithms for identifying analogous elements from structural and visual attributes; techniques for intuitively selecting and visualizing targets; and uses interactive data grids to manage variation in text entry and retrieval tasks.
papers.summary_en: Multi-Click is a new web automation technique that lets users perform the same action (like clicking or typing) simultaneously across multiple tabs or windows by selecting analogous elements. It uses algorithms to identify similar elements based on structure and visuals, and provides intuitive selection and visualization tools. This approach avoids complex abstractions like natural language or pseudocode, keeping automation direct and understandable.
papers.summary_zh: Multi-Click 是一种新的网页自动化技术，允许用户通过选择相似元素，在多个标签页或窗口中同时执行相同操作（如点击或输入）。它利用算法基于结构和视觉属性识别相似元素，并提供直观的选择和可视化工具。该方法避免了自然语言或伪代码等复杂抽象，保持了自动化的直接性和可理解性。

papers.title: agentAR: Creating Augmented Reality Applications with Tool-Augmented LLM-based Autonomous Agents
papers.short_title: agentAR: AR Apps via Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Creating Augmented Reality (AR) applications requires expertise in both design and implementation, posing significant barriers to entry for non-expert users. While existing methods reduce some of this burden, they often fall short in flexibility or usability for complex or varied use cases. To address this, we introduce agentAR, an AR authoring system that leverages a tool-augmented large language model (LLM)–based autonomous agent to support end-to-end, in-situ AR application creation from natural language input. Built on an application structure and tool library derived from state-of-the-art AR research, the agent autonomously creates AR applications from natural language dialogue. We demonstrate the effectiveness of agentAR through a case study of six AR applications and a user study with twelve participants, showing that it significantly reduces user effort while supporting the creation of diverse and functional AR experiences.
papers.summary_en: agentAR is an AR authoring system that uses a tool-augmented LLM-based autonomous agent to create AR applications from natural language input. It reduces the need for expert knowledge by automating the design and implementation process, supporting diverse and functional AR experiences. The system's effectiveness is demonstrated through case studies and user studies, showing significant reduction in user effort.
papers.summary_zh: agentAR 是一个增强现实（AR）创作系统，利用工具增强的大语言模型自主代理，从自然语言输入中创建 AR 应用。它通过自动化设计和实现过程，降低了对专业知识的需求，支持多样且功能丰富的 AR 体验。案例研究和用户研究证明了该系统的有效性，显著减少了用户的工作量。

papers.title: Automated Mapping of Adaptive App GUIs from Phones to TVs
papers.short_title: Auto Mapping Adaptive GUIs: Phone to TV
papers.abstract: With the increasing interconnection of smart devices, users often desire to adopt the same app on quite different devices for identical tasks, such as watching the same movies on both their smartphones and TVs. However, the significant differences in screen size, aspect ratio, and interaction styles make it challenging to adapt Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) across these devices. Although there are millions of apps available on Google Play, only a few thousand are designed to support smart TV displays. Existing techniques to map a mobile app GUI to a TV either adopt a responsive design, which struggles to bridge the substantial gap between phone and TV, or use mirror apps for improved video display, which requires hardware support and extra engineering efforts.
